## 6. Performance

### 6.1 Baseline before production edits

Add a UI-frame harness before touching production code. Proposed:

- `apps/vectorcraft-cli` gains an optional `ui-perf` feature/dependency on `vectorcraft-ui-egui` and
  `apps/vectorcraft-cli/src/perf_ui.rs`, invoked as `vectorcraft-cli perf --ui --frames 1200 --json PATH`.
- It builds a deterministic `Session` with `perf::synthetic(50_000)`, installs `theme::install_fonts` and the same
  `craft-fonts`/interface fonts as production, and runs a **version-neutral** frame driver on a fixed
  `egui::Context`: baseline 0.36.2 calls `VectorcraftApp::logic` then `ui` inside `run_ui` and `logic` inside
  `run_logic`; the candidate calls `tick` then `ui` inside `run_ui` and `tick` inside `run_logic`. Both invoke the
  host `raw_input_hook`/iteration boundary once per frame, in the real host order. The baseline must not use a
  nonexistent `tick` API or a shim that changes its lifecycle.
- Count one sample per accepted `run_ui` frame (use the driver's frame completion / `cumulative_frame_nr()` delta),
  not per layout pass. Logic-only iterations are reported separately. Record the exact lifecycle, hook calls and
  pass count for both sides.
- Fixed environment: 1440×900, 1x, dark theme, dock open, no hidden panels; `pixels_per_point` set explicitly;
  `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR` fixed; same profile/features/compiler.
- Workloads: cold first frame/font load; 1,200 idle frames; 1,000 pan frames; 1,000 zoom frames; selection drag;
  panel scroll; dialog open/close; text typing; save/reopen; screenshot request (where renderer available).
- Metrics: full `Context::run_ui` wall time, app `perf.frame_ms`, shape count, tessellation/vertex counts,
  `textures_delta` bytes and texture count, peak RSS, idle repaint delay/count, logic-only tick time.
- Report p50/p95/p99 over ≥1,000 accepted frames; 10 warmups + 30 timed iterations for discrete operations; ≥20
  fresh processes for startup. Do not call a p99 from 20/30 samples a tail estimate.

Also run the existing `vectorcraft-cli perf --paths 50000 --deep` (engine/render budgets) on the same fixture and
`vectorcraft-cli bench FILE` for a representative example. These measure different things; do not compare compile
time or CLI throughput to UI latency.

### 6.2 Paired comparison

- **Performance control:** the pre-migration control is the then-current main `4a7cba0…` (the two-commit DXF delta) with its
  coherent 0.36 lock, not `8906073…` alone. The candidate is the migration branch rebased onto `4a7cba0…` (or a
  later main after the same gate). This keeps `crates/cad/src/import/curve.rs` identical on both sides and isolates
  the egui migration. `8906073…` remains the historical planning baseline and rollback identity, not the paired
  control. If the DXF delta cannot be included in the control, measure it separately and show it does not touch the
  measured UI paths.
- Same compiler (1.95), profile, features (`wgpu`/`accessibility`, `interface-fonts`, `bundled-fonts`), fonts,
  fixture, OS, renderer/driver, DPI and viewport. Record all three source SHAs, lock identities and the exact diff
  between control and candidate (and the stock adapter, if any).
- **Three arms in the first baseline report and in every investigated regression:** unchanged 0.36, stock
  0.37.0 (`841a328b`) and the selected fork/candidate, with the same environment. The stock arm uses the same
  operation in a pinned minimal adapter/harness when fork-only app code cannot compile unchanged; record the
  adapter diff and any remaining semantic difference. App acceptance may still use the paired old/candidate arms,
  but no upstream attribution is claimed without the stock arm. Keep stock results even when they are not the
  acceptance pair.
- Use the shared performance protocol's floors: at least 10 warmups + 30 timed iterations for steady operations,
  20 fresh processes for startup, and at least 1,000 *accepted* frames for any frame distribution. Do not call a
  p99 from 20/30 samples a tail estimate. Software and real-GPU results are separate.
- Separate software renderer (Windows WARP / lavapipe) and real GPU (i915 renderD128 on Linux if the chosen
  Vulkan/GL backend works) results. No display session is inherited; qualify the backend through managed jobs.
- Alternate the control/candidate order, include the stock arm in the same environment, and run sequentially with
  no concurrent builds.
- Predefine gates: investigate a repeatable >5% median or >10% p95 regression, or >5% peak-RSS increase above the
  measured noise floor; a new idle busy-loop or repaint storm; or any existing absolute budget failure. For
  sub-millisecond operations require >0.05 ms or corroborating allocation/instruction counts. Re-run noisy
  comparisons and reject inconclusive ones; never widen a threshold or an expanding noise allowance after seeing a
  failure. Existing `perf` budgets are absolute and remain in force.
- Measure renderer construction (DX12 FXC) separately from first frame; measure font discovery separately if
  `system_fonts` is ever considered.
- Record raw samples, median/p95/p99, RSS, allocation/texture counters and load average for each arm. Retain
  baseline, stock and candidate executables and logs outside disposable targets.

### 6.3 Regression response

If #8731-like text tessellation or #8736-like shader cost appears on our fixtures:

- reproduce on unchanged 0.36, stock 0.37 and selected fork;
- isolate plain vs color-glyph rows, Repeat/MirroredRepeat semantics, first-frame vs steady state;
- only then consider a row-level fast path or explicit override constants;
- clamp-only sampling is not an acceptable fix; preserve wrap/filter semantics.

## 7. Reviewable PR stages, dependency DAG and rollback

### 7.1 Stages

Every branch/tag push and every new PR in this table needs fresh, explicit human approval after the exact
publication and validation are shown. Planning, implementation and review do not grant publication approval.
Public text carries no agent/model/tool attribution.

| Stage | Repository | Contents | Depends on | Must pass |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| V0 | VectorCraft | This plan only | — | Adversarial review; no code |
| V1 | VectorCraft | Version-neutral UI perf harness, lifecycle/screenshot/accessibility test scaffolding on **0.36.2**; baseline, `4a7cba0…` control and stock-0.37.0 captures | V0 | `cargo xtask ci` on baseline; baseline/control/stock perf report; no production behavior change |
| D1a | storytold/winit | Complete reviewed immutable winit: W1–W15 minus W5, plus W17–W27 including replacement W20, W15P, bounded transfer; provenance/PATCHES and clean-fetch proof | Independent winit adversarial review; upstream prerequisites | winit test suites, W15P/transfer contract tests, clean `cargo fetch --locked` |
| D1b | storytold/egui | Complete reviewed immutable egui **P8** (`craft/0.37.0-release`): P2/P3/P4/P5/P6, P2b (E4 regular + PRIMARY), P7 (E7/E19/E21), P7b (E21b), P7c (#8763/#8748); provenance/PATCHES and clean-fetch proof | D1a; independent egui adversarial review; P8 prerequisites | egui test suites, E21b/W27 and P7c regression tests, clean `cargo fetch --locked` |
| L1 | craft-libs | CL-1 coherent 0.37 API port on `3832c47…` (which already carries `8614e4a`/`1764bca`): `craft-platform` and security/settings/docking/printing fixes preserved, egui 0.37 pins to D1b; includes the CL-2 capture-slot prototype for the DesignCraft/GridCraft pilots (VectorCraft does not consume it) | D1b | craft-libs fmt/clippy/tests, `cargo test -p craft-ui --test visual_regression` (414 exact positives, 36 negative controls, no autoupdate), no security regression; packaged-manifest check; no stale PR199 tree |
| L2 | craft-libs | CL-2F final capture-helper API freeze after the DesignCraft/GridCraft adapters are reviewed; final immutable craft-libs revision on the L1 base | L1; adapter review | Shared capture contract tests; visual regression; final package/lock check; adversarial review |
| V2 | VectorCraft | Atomic compatibility PR: manifests, lock, root patches, `Id`/`Role`/`MouseWheel`/shared screenshot-helper adoption/fonts/scroll/panel-width changes, required E21 byte deletion and E21b canvas producer/owner lifecycle, **and the accessible names/glyph-fixture fixes required to keep kittest 0.37's strict tests green**; no blanket `with_accessibility_check(false)` | V1, D1a, D1b, L2 | `cargo xtask ci`, `ui-deps`, wasm, native build; exact test counts; rebase/DXF gate |
| V3 | VectorCraft | Lifecycle: host iteration/tick/input/ui, multi-pass/logic-only, hidden paint, monotonic clock, separate counters | V2 | Lifecycle tests; no command/undo duplicates; hidden background jobs |
| V4 | VectorCraft | Extended Clipboard/PRIMARY/PasteImage and native E21/E21b/text/RTL qualification; required canvas adapter already in V2 | V2/V3 | Clipboard/IME tests; native Wayland/X11/macOS-manual gate |
| V5 | VectorCraft | Broader accessibility audit/coverage (all names/roles, hidden/disabled, keyboard), panel width persistence, full font/glyph matrix | V2/V3 | `cargo test --workspace` with kittest strict; no-default-fonts gates |
| V6 | VectorCraft | Full native/web/Windows/Linux validation, performance, screenshots, docs/parity evidence; adversarial implementation review | V2–V5 | Full acceptance matrix; performance gates; review findings closed |
| V7 | VectorCraft | Remove superseded test helpers and local shims (never a capture slot); no behavior change | V6 | Same gates; diff review |

V2 is deliberately atomic: a manifest/lock bump alone would leave `main` unbuildable. It also cannot postpone the
accessible-name fixes that `egui_kittest` 0.37 now enforces: the workspace tests would fail immediately. Do not keep
a blanket `with_accessibility_check(false)` as a staging shortcut. V3–V5 may land in parallel only if each branch
includes V2 and they do not touch the same lifecycle files; prefer sequential for review. V2 waits for the complete
D1a winit and D1b egui P8 revisions and for L2; no intermediate fork or craft-libs stage is a production pin.

**Rebase gate before V2:** fetch current `storytold/vectorcraft` main, record its full SHA and diff against the
pinned review baseline. The recorded drift is exactly two commits from `8906073…` to `4a7cba0…`, both changing only
`crates/cad/src/import/curve.rs` (DXF spline). Rebase the migration branch onto that (or a later) main, preserve the
DXF fix, run the DXF import tests, and use the same `4a7cba0…` source as the performance control in §6.2. If more
files or dependency changes appear, stop and re-audit before implementation; do not drop or rewrite the unrelated
fix.

### 7.2 Rollback

- Before V2, preserve the exact baseline `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, baseline/control/stock executables, D1a/D1b
  fork revisions and L1/L2 craft-libs revisions outside disposable build dirs. Do not rely on `cargo update` to
  reconstruct an old graph.
- Rollback is a revert of the complete V2 (or V2–V6) commits, not a version-string edit. The old 0.36.2 lock and
  craft-libs revisions must remain reachable. Keep the old dependency set in a local branch/commit and in
  evidence; do not delete it during build-cache cleanup. The `4a7cba0…` DXF fix is upstream work, not part of the
  rollback.
- Per stage: **D1a** and **D1b** roll back by a new immutable revision on the prior base; never force-push or move
  a published tag, and never delete a published revision. **L1** and **L2** roll back by a new craft-libs revision
  on the previous base (L2 → L1 → `3832c47…`), preserving the prior capture-helper and PR199 port. **V2–V6** revert
  the app commits to the coherent 0.36.2 lock and its craft-libs revisions. Record each revert revision, parent and
  validation, and keep the superseded immutable revisions reachable.
- If a fork/craft-libs revision becomes unavailable, stop and restore the last coherent graph; do not substitute
  a branch, path patch or a second egui version.
- No persistence format change is planned. If one becomes necessary, specify backward compatibility and keep
  unreadable data, or abandon that part of the change.

### 7.3 Documentation and evidence

- `docs/architecture.md`: revise the UI/lifecycle section to describe host iteration, `tick`/input/`ui`, logic-only iterations,
  root `Ui`, screenshot callbacks and the dependency patch policy.
- `docs/development.md`: record the selected egui/winit/craft-libs revisions, `ui-deps`, the UI perf harness and
  any changed browser/Windows workflow. Keep the existing font rules (`craft-fonts`, `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR`).
- `docs/control-protocol.md`: update `ui.screenshot` only if native evidence changes the minimized/covered
  behavior; keep the timeout/error contract otherwise.
- `ROADMAP.md` progress log and the touched docs' status/revision history: record the dependency migration. Do not
  move `docs/target-app-parity.md` scores, `docs/gaps.md` entries or parity checklists unless a measured behavior
  actually changes; this migration is infrastructure, not a feature claim.
- Keep all evidence under `/home/codex/work/ssd2/task-evidence/egui037-migration-20261022/vectorcraft/`: exact
  source/lock identity, build/test logs with counts, screenshots, perf raw samples, dependency metadata, review
  findings and commands. Do not put source or deliverables in disposable build targets.

## 8. Blocking unknowns and acceptance criteria

These are not “future work”; they block calling the migration done:

1. **Complete final forks and reachability.** Approve and publish reachable immutable **D1a** `storytold/winit`
   (W1–W15 minus W5, plus W17–W27 including replacement W20, W15P, bounded transfer) and **D1b** `storytold/egui` P8 (P2b, P7, P7b/E21b,
   P7c, complete). Record exact full SHAs and tree hashes, preserve fork authorship/PATCHES, and prove a clean
   `cargo fetch --locked`. No intermediate fork stage is a production pin; candidate aiongg revisions remain
   research inputs; no final SHA is invented in this plan.
2. **Final craft-libs revision (resolved by the published pin).** The CL-1/CL-2F delta is published in
   craft-libs `25da131…`; the current workspace pins `craft-ui`, `craft-window`, `craft-keymap` and
   `craft-print` to descendant `a0916808…`, retaining that delta and upstream shared docking. The plan-time requirement was to finish that delta on the `3832c47…` base (which already
   carries the selected `8614e4a`/`1764bca` changes), preserving `craft-platform`,
   security/settings/docking/printing fixes, pin D1b and pass `craft-ui` visual regression. Do not merge PR199
   head `b68de8c` or audit tree `ec8840a` as trees. L1 (CL-1) and L2 (CL-2F) preceded V2; publication waited for
   the shared gates and the capture-helper adapter review.
3. **`default_fonts`/font provider.** `ui-egui` library tests and no-default-feature builds must bind non-empty
   families; production `Tofu` would otherwise draw synthetic boxes, and downstream kittest tests do not inherit
   kittest's own dev-dependency fonts. `system_fonts` remains off unless measured and approved; the shared
   font-fixture identities and licences apply.
4. **kittest strict accessibility.** Every visible input in every test that renders it must have a name and a
   correct role. This may require broad, reviewable field/row changes; `row_label` must return its existing label
   response rather than add a duplicate.
5. **Capture callback semantics.** The app must prove exactly-one completion, hidden-window paint, timeout and
   late-callback safety with a weak completion slot (the live slot owns the strong `Context`/owning-viewport wake handle waker; callback pixels
   only; no strong `Context`), pre-issue checked-byte admission (4/128/256 MiB defaults), geometry-epoch binding
   and rejection of any resize/DPI/zoom/surface change before save, and `RequestPaintWhileHidden` for a queued but
   unissued request. Use the L2 shared craft-ui helper; no app-local slot.
6. **Clipboard/PRIMARY.** eframe `clipboard` must be enabled and must not duplicate the app's `SystemClipboard`
   paste, especially for `PasteImage`. W15P/E4 must provide the winit-owned per-seat PRIMARY path with fresh
   keyboard-or-pointer serials, synchronous claims, bounded 2 s/16 MiB/4-read/2-writer/queue-8 transfers and no
   first-seat fallback; arboard PRIMARY is not an unmeasured default.
7. **IME replacement and outgoing text.** The canvas needs an engine-level delete-surrounding operation with a
   precise char/byte contract and one undo step, plus the E21b model/preedit/UTF-8 payload producer and the
   complete egui P7b/W27 lifecycle (owner identity, `Available` empty vs `Unavailable`, committed clear boundary,
   latest-`None` authority, current-epoch mismatch and old-epoch rejection). UI `TextEdit` behavior is separate.
8. **Upstream rebase gate.** At plan time, main was `4a7cba0…`, two commits ahead of the pinned review baseline, touching
   only `crates/cad/src/import/curve.rs` (DXF spline). Rebase before V2, preserve that fix, rerun its import tests,
   and isolate it from performance comparisons (§6.2). Recheck if main advanced further.
9. **macOS evidence.** No macOS host/display is available here. Keyboard layouts, IME (including press-and-hold),
   Metal/GL, native pickers, termination and traffic-light positioning remain an explicit release gate.
10. **Windows 7.** 0.37 + glow + clipboard + the separate `vendor/windows-link` packaging patch must
    compile/package and be smoke-tested; no support claim from a modern runner alone. Keep the hayro/krilla PDF
    patches independent.
11. **Performance.** Paired control at `4a7cba0…` and candidate with the same engine delta, plus a stock-0.37.0
    arm in the first report and every investigated regression, using the shared sample floors and the 5%
    median / 10% p95 / 5% RSS gates. Upstream #8731, #8736 and #8512 are reports, not results; do not claim a
    regression or a fix without ours.
12. **Dependency identities.** Enumerate every fork-family package at one storytold source; audit external
    `kittest`/`accesskit*` as compatible registry identities, not egui-git crates. Skrifa/harfrust/glifo duplicates
    are expected; measure binary size and confirm no public type crossing. A new `egui`/winit duplicate is a hard
    failure.
13. **Role semantics.** Review the `SelectableLabel → Button`, `Checkbox → CheckBox`, `CollapsingHeader →
    DisclosureTriangle` and `Other → Unknown` mappings against actual screen-reader semantics, not just compile.
14. **Wayland/X11/GPU backend.** The host has an i915 render device but no inherited display session; a managed
    Linux job must qualify the actual compositor/backend/DPI. Availability is not a qualified result.
15. **Web.** A wasm `check` is not a browser workflow; headless Chrome WebGPU/WebGL2, paste/drop, save/download and
    screenshots are required.

**Done means:** one coherent 0.37 graph; `cargo xtask ci` and `ui-deps` pass from a clean checkout; lifecycle
tests prove no duplicate/stopped work and no stale input replay; screenshots use the shared L2 weak slot and are
correlated, epoch-bound and admission-bounded; W15P/E21b/W27 and accessibility tests pass; native Linux/Windows and
browser workflows are recorded; performance is paired against the same-engine control with the stock-0.37
attribution arm and within gates; macOS is either evidenced or explicitly unresolved; and the final adversarial
review has no open correctness finding.

no reviewer finding is treated as an executed test result or an implementation claim.

| 4 | Screenshot callback violates weak-slot/cancel contract | **Accepted and fixed.** Replaced receiver/strong-`Context` design with a per-request weak completion slot, pre-issue pixel admission, aggregate limits and shared craft-ui helper after CL-2F. §3.5, §4.4, §5.2. |

Separate host-iteration and accepted-UI-frame counters; stale input only in a known UI phase; test driver preserves host order; baseline uses `logic`/`ui`, not `tick`. §2.4, §4.2, §5.2, §6.1. |
| 6 | Whole-family pin gate not exhaustive | **Accepted and fixed.** Full fork-family allowlist plus separate external `kittest`/`accesskit*` registry audit; negative fixtures; version alone insufficient. §4.1. |
| 7 | The performance harness uses a nonexistent 0.36.2 `tick` API | **Accepted and fixed.** Version-neutral harness: baseline `logic`+`ui`, candidate `tick`+`ui`, same hook order, accepted-frame counting, same-engine control for isolation. §6.1/§6.2. |
| 8 | `row_label` is already a real `Label` | **Accepted and fixed.** Return the existing `ui.label` response and use `label_inputs_by`; do not duplicate the label; handle custom-painted `widgets::label_row` separately. §3.10, §4.8. |

| Minor | Baseline date stale | **Verified and corrected** to 2026-10-23 11:50:04 +0700. Header/§2.1. |

### 8.2 Dispositions of the adversarial review (`vectorcraft-v2`)

Every finding in `plan-reviews/vectorcraft-v2.md` is closed below by source-grounded plan text, not a footnote.

| # | Finding | Disposition |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | No stock-0.37.0 control arm | **Accepted and fixed.** Stock 0.37.0 (`841a328b`) is a measured arm in the first baseline report and every investigated regression, with the same environment and a pinned minimal adapter where fork-only code cannot compile; retained even when app acceptance pairs 0.36 with the candidate. §5.3, §6.2, §7.1 V1, §8.11. |
| 2 | Capture admission and geometry under-specified; 64 MiB too small | **Accepted and fixed.** Adopted the shared 4 requests / 128 MiB per image / 256 MiB aggregate defaults (stricter only if the documented intended surface fits), checked bytes reserved before issue, no eviction; records logical/screen bounds, viewport, DPI/zoom and surface epoch at issuance and rejects/retries any change before save, including change-back, then verifies scale/aspect. §3.5, §4.4, §5.2, §8.5. |
| 3 | W27 old-epoch invalidation missing | **Accepted and fixed.** Old-epoch `done` is rejected and invalidates that epoch, never edits the new owner; current-epoch mismatch applies incoming once and defers outgoing. §3.9, §4.6, §5.6, §5.7. |
| 4 | P7c ownership of #8763/#8748 absent | **Accepted and fixed.** P7c owns both fixes and their pointer/keyboard and hidden-parent regressions; D1b includes P7c, V2 depends on it, and an app workaround needs equivalent tests plus a removal condition. §3.11, §7.1, §8.1. |
| 5 | Empty-family font claim source-wrong | **Accepted and fixed.** Production `MissingGlyphPolicy` defaults to `Tofu`; the kittest harness alone defaults to `Panic`. Mutation 8 now expects the non-empty-family assertion failure; `theme.rs`'s "egui panics…" comment is scheduled for correction. §1, §3.8, §3.10, §4.7, §5.7, §8.3. |
| 6 | craft-ui visual regression and negative controls missing from L1/V2 | **Accepted and fixed.** L1/L2 run `cargo test -p craft-ui --test visual_regression` with 414 exact positive pairs and 36 negative controls; no tolerance or autoupdate, and app screenshot tolerances stay separate. §5.3, §7.1. |
| 7 | `ui-deps` ledger conflates required and optional packages | **Accepted and fixed.** Required-used, optional/forbidden-if-present and external registry identities are separate ledger classes; the transitive `accesskit_*` platform crates are audited; a missing optional package passes. §4.1. |
| 8 | D1 not split into winit then egui | **Accepted and fixed.** D1a winit precedes D1b egui P8, each with its own review, SHA, tree hash and clean-fetch proof; V2 depends on D1a, D1b and L2. §4.1, §7.1, §8.1. |
| 9 | Rollback is app-only | **Accepted and fixed.** Per-stage rollback: new immutable revisions for D1a/D1b and L1/L2, never force-push or move published tags; V2–V6 revert to the coherent 0.36.2 lock. §7.2. |
| 10 | Dead provisional app-local capture slot | **Accepted and fixed.** Removed: VectorCraft adopts the L2 helper only and keeps no app-local or provisional slot. §3.5, §4.4, §7.1 V7. |
| 11 | Clipboard rationale overstates impact | **Accepted and fixed.** Reworded to egui-winit's text clipboard/`Event::Paste` path; the arboard `SystemClipboard` remains the independent rich-format owner and the textless-paste tests stay. §3.6. |
| 12 | W15P synchronous ownership details absent | **Accepted and fixed.** Fresh keyboard-or-pointer serial and focused seat, synchronous claim in the triggering turn, no first-seat fallback; bounded async reads 2 s/16 MiB/4 reads/2 writers/queue 8, cancellation with owner-specific wake. §3.6, §4.5, §5.7, §8.6. |

  `Id::new` → `Id::unique`; test-only U+22EE → `…` because 0.37's bundled fonts dropped it. The U+22EE change is
  test-fixture only; VectorCraft production source has no U+22EE (checked).

## 10. Open decisions to confirm with the owner/reviewer

These are decisions this plan recommends but does not silently make:

- Use the full selected fork (including E5/E12/E21 and the new E21b) even though VectorCraft's UI is LTR.
  Recommended: yes, for one suite graph and correct IME; prove UI text layout with tests.
- Keep eframe `system_fonts` off. Recommended: yes, until measured and licensed/tested; the app already has a font
  database. The shared pinned fixtures, not system fonts, are the test oracle.
- Keep `links` off on native (existing behavior); add only if a native `ctx.open_url` path is shown to need it.
- Replace `mac_window::center_buttons` with `Frame::set_traffic_lights_position` only after macOS evidence.
  Recommended for this migration: no.
- Serialize screenshots (one outstanding) rather than supporting concurrent captures. Recommended: yes; simpler
  correlation and memory bound. Use the shared weak completion slot, never a strong `Context` in the callback.
- Add `PasteImage` handling rather than disabling eframe's image clipboard. Recommended: yes, with dedupe tests.
- Keep the app's `SystemClipboard` as the rich-format owner for regular clipboard on Wayland, while the selected
  W15P path owns PRIMARY. Recommended: yes; this is the selected design, not an unresolved ownership test.
- Adopt the shared craft-ui capture helper from L2 (CL-1 + CL-2F); no app-local capture slot.
  Recommended: yes, for all eleven craft-ui consumers.

## Request-bound Type tool IME reset — local implementation, 2026-10-24

An interrupted incoming composition now retains the complete ID returned by
`Context::request_ime_reset`. Only its matching `Event::ImeResetCompleted`, in raw event order,
admits subsequent IME preedit/commit/surrounding-delete events. Old terminals, empty preedit,
idle frames and host cancellation return values do not acknowledge the request. A later caret,
target, committed-context or Context change supersedes the old ID. Pointer/navigation/command
notices keep the remaining raw suffix blocked until their actual handler establishes the final
destination. Ordinary uninterrupted composition keeps its existing key ownership.

Each UI pass observes its actual final custom descriptor, including discarded passes and exits
without geometry. Losing custom publication to absence, hidden/focus state or a stock field
retires a pending ID; returning to the same target/caret requests a new ID once. Hooks installed
before the host's first UI pass distinguish its preceding logic callback from standalone hidden
logic, which cannot claim fresh UI geometry. The callbacks capture no Context or app.

The regression source covers the previously failing click-A→B/fresh-が path with a real returned
fence, ordered fresh suffixes without an old terminal, stale/foreign/duplicate IDs, pressed
navigation and shortcuts, discarded/stock/focus reactivation, graphics replacement, external
edits at the same caret, and full-pass versus standalone logic. This local update is pending
dependency refresh, formatting, compilation, tests and independent implementation review. Native
and browser IME acceptance remains separate: unsupported integrations, reset failures or missing
acknowledgements keep interrupted IME mutations blocked; elapsed time or a nonempty preedit never
provides a fallback acknowledgement.

Every format Illustrator opens, places, saves or exports, against VectorCraft's format table (`FORMATS`,
`OPEN_EXTS`, `PLACE_EXTS` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/fileio/formats.rs`). Illustrator's list comes from its public
documentation (helpx "file formats" and Save/Export pages), not from its installed bundle: the clean-room rule
forbids reading the install. Part of [target-app-parity.md](target-app-parity.md).

**Fidelity** is estimated unless a test is named. Test sources: unit and property tests per crate
(`crates/svg/tests`, `crates/pdf/tests`, `crates/format/tests/prop_format.rs`), import fuzzing
(`crates/engine/tests/import_fuzz.rs`), the Affinity corpus (`cargo xtask corpus --affinity`, 51 pinned public
files, CI job `affinity-corpus.yml`). There is **no real-world Illustrator corpus**: test inputs are written
from the public specifications, and users' own `.ai` files are used locally only.

## Summary

| | Illustrator | VectorCraft | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Formats opened or placed | ~30 | 25 | missing: FreeHand, CorelDRAW, DWG, HEIC/HEIF, JPEG 2000, PICT, PCX, Pixar, Word `.doc`, PS |
| Formats saved (Save As) | 6 (AI, AIT, PDF, EPS, SVG, SVGZ) | 6 + native | `.ai` written PDF-compatible (no Illustrator editing data) or as legacy version 7 (layers and groups, one artboard per file) |
| Formats exported | ~16 | 17 | missing: DWG, 3D (OBJ/USDA/glTF); extra: GIF/PNG-8 palette export, DXF up to 2018, layered PSD |
| **Overall (weighted by use)** | | **~75%** | `.ai` and PDF dominate the weighting |

EPS editing-data follow-up (2026-10-16): both mesh-corner layouts (with and without opacity)
read in RGB, CMYK and gray. Vector opacity-mask art and its Clip, Invert, Disabled and Linked
flags are retained. Winding-declared legacy compound member groups keep their shared paint even
when followed by `9 () XW`. Fully rasterized print pages are compared using the same filtered
minification for both representations; the existing error thresholds and ordinary vector-page
checks remain. Synthetic regressions reject truncated meshes, non-unit rational weights,
unbalanced mask art, unknown mask operators, missing artwork and wrong page framing. Real
user files remain local; no SVG replacement or tracing is used. Small rendering differences
continue to produce import warnings.

## The main format: `.ai`

The format that decides beta. Illustrator's `.ai` is a PDF (or, for old files, PostScript) plus Illustrator's
private editing data. VectorCraft:

- **Reads** the PDF page (vectors, text, images, colour, transparency, layers via optional content) and the
  *structure* of the editing data (below). Opens Illustrator EPS the same way through its own PostScript
  Level 3 interpreter. A `.ai` in PostScript form (versions 3 to 8, and what Rhino and other CAD apps
  write) is its own editing data: it opens through the layers its program has, compared with its page
  when the program runs, from the layers alone when it names its prolog without including it (#1027), and with its art on one
  layer when it has no layers (Illustrator 3, and image editors' exported paths: storytold/photocraft#6036).
  RGB in the PDF page's `ICCBased` spaces keeps the file's numbers in a `.ai` (the `uncalibrated_rgb`
  import option, on for editor documents, off for PDFs), so `.ai` files tagged with a non-sRGB RGB profile
  open with different, unconverted RGB colours than before.
  A PDF-compatible `.ai` opens on its PDF part's trim boxes (its artboards), the bleed boxes round them
  becoming the document's bleed, so art in the bleed shows outside the artboard, within the bleed guide (#1266).
  A PDF saved with its editing data (`AIPDFPrivateData`) opens the same way.
- **Writes** a PDF-compatible `.ai` (Save As › `ai`): Illustrator opens it as plain art. It never writes
  Illustrator's private editing data, which is undocumented.
- **Writes** a legacy `.ai` of version 7 (Save As › `ai` › Version: Legacy (version 7), `aiVersion: "7"`): the
  PostScript form, from the published *Adobe Illustrator File Format Specification* version 7.0
  ([PRONOM fmt/423](https://doc.ai-hao123.com/sitemap.xml)), which apps reading `.ai` open with its
  structure (#868). It keeps layers (names, order, visibility, lock), groups, compound paths, clipping groups,
  solid colours, linear and radial gradients and RGB images. The format has one artboard: each artboard chosen in
  the options dialog's artboard picker (thumbnails to check, default all) is a file of its own,
  `{name}-{artboard}.ai` when there are several. It has no transparency: objects are written opaque, and images
  with see-through pixels, opacity or a blending mode are flattened (an opaque image of themselves and the art
  under them, clipped to where they show; that art stays) or omitted (Transparent Images,
  `transparentImages: "flatten"|"omit"`). Type is written as editable text objects (point type, area type and type
  on a path, with their fonts' PostScript names, sizes, colours, alignment, indents, leading, tracking and
  scaling), which the reading app sets in those fonts; characters outside Windows-1252, vertical type, ruby, inline
  graphics and gradient or pattern fills make that type outlines, and Text: Outlines (`outlineText: true`) writes
  all type as outlines. The format can hide only layers: hidden objects go to a hidden layer of their own above
  their layer, are omitted, or are made visible (Hidden Objects, `hiddenObjects: "layer"|"omit"|"visible"`).
  Sublayers become groups; appearances, effects and brushes are expanded; object names are left out; layer
  names, spot color and gradient names and the title are written in Windows-1252, with `?` for characters outside
  it (two spot colors or two gradients whose names become the same are numbered).
  The file is also a PostScript program that runs: its prolog, a procedure set of VectorCraft's own written from
  the PostScript Language Reference, gives the format's operators their meaning, so it prints and previews
  (gradients filled with their first stop's colour, type left to the apps that read the format). VectorCraft
  opens a file with that prolog from its program, as the format.
- **Known failures in users' files:** layer structure flattened or multiplied (#951: 109 layers instead of
  14; #868: round trip with Illustrator 2018 loses layers and groups), guides and non-printing construction
  lines lost (#779), some files 4× slower to open since the editing data is read whole (#758), live effects,
  brushes and symbols come in as their drawn look (#637; pattern fills are read since #1025); legacy `.ai`
  without the prolog opens since #1027, its legacy type (`To` … `TO`) since #868.
- Estimate: **~65%** for real exchange with Illustrator users (open: ~75%; save: PDF-compatible, or legacy
  version 7 with layers and groups; not yet tested by users who hand files back).
  Closing the open-side issues: 10–20 h with users' files.

### Illustrator's private editing data

the app's own editing copy of a file (an EPS after its `%%EOF`, a `.ai`'s `AIPrivateData` streams, a PDF's `AIPDFPrivateData` streams when it was saved with the editing data (#868), Zstandard or zlib, the EPS's in ASCII85) is not documented as a whole. VectorCraft reads its structure: layers and sublayers (names, order, visibility, lock, printing, preview, dimming, colour), groups as they were nested, compound paths (painted by their last path, or the last painted one, with the paths of groups inside them kept as their paths: #1410), clipping groups and layer clipping, object names, hidden and locked objects, fills and strokes (grey, CMYK, RGB, named and spot colours, spot colours defined in Lab with their Lab values (#1032), global process colours as global swatches at their tint), linear and radial gradients, pattern fills with their patterns as pattern swatches (#1025), opacity, blend modes, isolation and knockout, embedded images where their matrix puts them, rotated ones too (#2269), with their alpha channel (CMYK images keep their ink amounts, as they do when a `.ai` opens from its PDF part, and an alpha channel that hides part of a CMYK image becomes a grayscale opacity mask), placed (linked) files as linked images in their place, each showing the low-resolution preview the file keeps of it until its file is found or relinked in the Links panel (#1264), guides, and every artboard where it is. A gradient with stops in the middle runs its whole ramp across its shape, and a gradient object does not pass its fill to the next path (#1390). An object whose art style is one fill and one stroke at most (solid colours, its own gradient, a variable-width profile) with an Outer Glow or Drop Shadow comes in as itself with them; one with more, other effects, a brush or dashes aligned to corners comes in as its drawn look (a group named after it). Type keeps its art style as a live appearance whatever its stack, so it can be retyped: each fill and stroke of the style's stack (solid colours, gradients and pattern fills, placed as the drawn look places them) with its own opacity, blend mode and effects, the effects on the whole object, and where the characters paint among them; the effects read are Warp, Offset Path, Transform (with copies), Drop Shadow, Outer Glow, Feather, Gaussian Blur and Bas Relief (its settings at their defaults), and a style with others keeps the type's drawn look. The page's drawing of such a style isn't held to look like VectorCraft's where its drawn look lay. Gradients take their matrix (`Xm`, radials and skewed ones too), focal point and the order of stops sharing a ramp point; gradient meshes, a clipping path's own fill and the artboards' names are read too. `editingData: "always"` (`convert --editing-data`) opens a `.ai` or an Illustrator EPS from its editing data even where it draws differently from its page, which can be older, with a note. Type is made from the file's text document, whole and editable, shown or not: point type (its frame's matrix, which newer files leave out when it is neither turned nor scaled, read as none), area type (a story in several frames as threaded type) and type on a path, with its characters, fonts, size, leading, tracking, scaling, baseline shift, fill and stroke (grey, RGB or CMYK), alignment, indents and paragraph spacing; the page's drawing of it (often in pieces) is left out. Where the text document can't say (a frame of another kind, or a document that doesn't agree with the page), type that shows comes from the page into its text object's place (no group around it), and hidden type is left out with a note. Kerning, underline and the other character and paragraph options aren't read yet. A `.ai` saved without PDF compatibility (a placeholder page) opens from its editing data alone, its point type, area type and type on a path made from the text document. A `.ai` whose PDF part shows only text isn't taken for that placeholder when its page states an art, trim or bleed box: it opens from its editing data alone where that reads, else from its PDF part (#1387). Text objects with an appearance keep their own text and frame, type of hidden layers stays hidden, and type on later artboards lands on its text objects (#1391); area type whose frame is too short for a line of the fallback font shows its first line (the frame is made taller, with a warning in the open result) (#1392). Symbols, pattern fills whose pattern it can't read, placed files the data keeps no preview of and anything else it doesn't read make the file come in as its page (on a layer that doesn't show, they are left out of that layer), with a warning saying what. The layers' art is also compared with the page (by lightness, so colours written as their CMYK equivalents compare alike, and by whether a pixel is inked at all); the page is used when they differ by more than 5%, where one draws an object the other doesn't (away from type, whose lines may be laid out afresh), and when an EPS whose page is its art's box has art printed outside it (#735). An EPS whose page is its art's box keeps that page when it comes in through its layers, not the editing data's artboard, and a text object counts as drawn by the page by its colours, not only its lightness, so a red stroke stacked over a dark red one stays (#1102). `textAs: "outlines"` opens a `.ai` whose type shows from its PDF part, which has the outlines; `editingData: false` opens any of them as its page or PDF part only, for print pipelines (#735). A file whose import left something out (hidden text, art or layers) is never written over by an export or Save As to its own path unless `acknowledgeLoss: true` (`convert --replace-lossy`), so the original keeps what the document lacks. Where a `.ai` can't be read that way (or its layers are turned off in the import options), we read its PDF-compatible part, so Illustrator-only live objects arrive as appearance, and plain groups arrive ungrouped: that part draws each object on its own and marks only layers, clipping groups and groups with opacity, blending or a mask (those come back). Art outside the artboards isn't in that part at all (Illustrator's PDF part leaves it out), so it doesn't open; the import says so in a note (#472). Its pages still go where the editing data puts the artboards (a grid stays a grid), with the art on each, when it has as many artboards as pages, of the same sizes (#1068). Its pages are laid out so that art one of them draws past its artboard (notes beside a design, which the part doesn't clip) doesn't lie over the page before it in the row, where it was taken for that page's art: the check against the editing data then found art its layers don't have there and opened the file as its PDF part, without the art outside the artboards. That part also has no paragraphs: area type is written line by line, and comes back as area type only where its font is installed and lays the lines out with the same breaks, else as a point type object per line (#508). Art off the page that a PDF does draw opens on the pasteboard.

## Format by format

| Format | Illustrator | Ours: open/place | Ours: save/export | Fidelity and tests |
|---|---|---|---|---|

| Illustrator template `.ait` | open, save | yes | PDF-compatible only, from Save as Template (`.vctemplate` stays its default) | New from Template opens a saved `.ait` untitled with its layers and art (`tests_pdfedit.rs`) |
| Illustrator `.ai` | open, save | yes (PDF-compatible + editing-data structure, File Info) | PDF-compatible, or legacy version 7 (layers and groups) | see above; no real-file corpus |

| SVG / SVGZ | open, place, save | yes | yes (SVG Options, Preserve Editing, symbols, filters, rich text) | strongest format; tests in `crates/svg/tests`; text on a path follows basic shapes as their SVG 2 equivalent paths (#1527); CSS transforms and the `font` shorthand (#1565), percentage lengths in symbols (#1596), Inkscape flowed text as area type (#1568) and Inkscape pages as artboards (#1601) import; an unsupported filter is named in its warning (#1598); an artboard exported on its own (Export As with Use Artboards, Export for Screens, Asset Export) has the artboard's name as `<title>`, Save the document's (#3544); attributes in other applications' XML namespaces (`plotter:pen="2"`) kept on their objects from import to export, as `data-*` attributes are (`crates/svg/tests/it/foreign_attributes.rs`) |

CNC preset and VCarve QA remain open |

| CSS | export (CSS Properties) | — | yes | |
| OBJ / USDA / glTF | 3D export | — | no | needs 3D (gap G3) |
| Affinity `.af`, `.afdesign`, `.afpub` | no | yes (beyond Illustrator) | no (#665) | 51 pinned files, [affinity-validation.md](affinity-validation.md) |
| Clipboard: PDF, SVG, PNG, EMF, text | yes | yes | yes | copied files paste as art |

## PDF editable imports

- [x] Place from bytes or unlinked paths, and PDF clipboard paste, keep the selected page's live text. Synthetic two-page regressions in `crates/engine/src/cmd/fileio/tests_pdffidelity.rs` cover both sources, page selection and explicit outlines. The single-page importer honors the same text choice as Open; existing PDF fallback rules are unchanged.

## Corpus download integrity

- [x] PngSuite opt-in downloads are pinned, SHA-256 verified and bounded before publication (#1729); no archive extraction. This secures fixture acquisition and does not raise format-fidelity scores.

## Feature submission evidence

**Feature evidence last updated:** 2026-10-22.

The shared assessment status line and revision history are current upstream; this dated section records the submission's feature evidence and revisions without rescoring upstream or claiming a new combined build or runtime measurement.

- Current-main conflict reconciliation retains upstream and feature behavior; scores and estimates unchanged
- Superseded 2026-10-20 behavior, retained as history: Artboard Options shares existing presets and orientation controls and can fit artwork without moving it; artwork fitting uses the original target artboard and revision-scoped bounds caches

- Artboard Options puts Fit to Artwork Bounds and Fit to Selected Art in the Preset menu. Artwork bounds cover all drawn document art, including other artboards and off-board art; selection bounds may span artboards. Fit changes only the active artboard and keeps artwork stationary, including position-only fitting with Move Artwork enabled. Existing Background Color and presets remain available; scores and estimates unchanged.

Artboard Options forwards the active Artboard tool's Scale Artwork with Artboard option for ordinary resizing. Fit to Artwork Bounds and Fit to Selected Art explicitly leave artwork stationary. Dialog regression coverage checks preset/orientation/typed-size intent with scaling on and off, draft cancellation, one-step Undo/Redo, and fitting while Move Artwork and Scale Artwork are enabled. This is a narrow follow-up to #3277; no parity score or estimate is reassessed.

Every known shortfall against Illustrator, one entry each, **ranked by how much it stops a professional from
switching**. This is the work list: unless you were given a task, pick the highest-ranked gap you can make
progress on, write a plan, and update the entry (and [target-app-parity.md](target-app-parity.md)) in the same PR.

Gap ids are stable (PRs say "Part of gap 2"); the rank can change. Hours are Opus 5.5 agent wall-clock hours for
one agent, estimated unless marked; calibration in
[target-app-parity.md](target-app-parity.md#calibration). **Beta** marks the gaps that must close before the beta
stage ([ROADMAP.md](../ROADMAP.md)).

## G1 Interaction fidelity

- **Done:** Distance Guides ([public page](https://yisc.ai-hao123.com/xuexi/partner-49397327.html)): with Smart Guides on and something selected, the Selection tool with Alt/Option held over another object shows the horizontal and vertical distances between them, and over an empty part of an artboard the selection's distances from its four edges, labelled in the General unit; Preferences › Smart Guides › Invoke Distance Guides turns them off. Hover only, as documented: not while moving or nudging. No entry closed; estimates unchanged.

- **Done (part of #4028):** Recolor Artwork › Assign: double-clicking a row's new color opens the Color Picker, as the [public page](https://yrjd.yx-sf.com/xuexi/document-52559923.html) describes ("double-click it and select a color in the Color Picker"). OK sets the row's new color in the model it was picked in, so a CMYK mix is no longer a hex value converted back; Cancel leaves the row. A Lab new color is kept, but can't be typed yet: the picker's Lab fields work in RGB, as for fill and stroke. **Missing:** Lab entry in the picker, swatch libraries in the picker and the row's right-click menu (Pick from Swatches, Limit to Library).

- **Done (#3416):** Recolor Artwork Edit chips scroll to the last color while the heading, color wheel and actions stay visible. Screen resize and UI scaling, Preview, Confirm, Cancel, Undo and #1733 wheel drags are covered in `tests/recolor.rs`. No gap entry closed; estimates unchanged.

- **Polygon/Star count persistence:** Exact-size placement saves the chosen count for later drags and reopening the existing canvas dialog. Regression coverage includes both tools, repeated drags, switching tools and Cancel. The remaining G1 scope and estimates are unchanged.

- **Artboard Options shares existing presets and orientation controls and can fit artwork without moving it; artwork fitting includes all drawn document art across artboards and off-board; artwork bounds are cached by active document and revision, and selection uses the shared bounds cache across artboards:** Shared existing preset definitions are reused; no external preset assets are added. Presets preserve each selected artboard's orientation, and orientation choices apply even when the active board already matches. Fit operations draft bounds until OK, affect only the active artboard and leave artwork in place. Regression coverage checks draft/Cancel, selected-set application, active-only fitting and Undo. Broader scope and estimates unchanged.

- **Implemented, regression-tested and contributor-confirmed:** status messages and readouts use stable responsive allocations sized for localized labels and ordinary coordinates. Original-file acceptance confirmed 2026-10-19; broader G1 scope and estimates unchanged. Sample widths are cached by language, document unit and pixels per point rather than remeasured every frame.

- **Canvas review follow-up:** Cached canvas dimensions match the renderer limit before cache-key creation, view construction and worker submission. Controlled-worker regression checks oversized width and height, high DPI and the render transform without allocating oversized images. G1 scope and estimates are unchanged.
- **Done (#3106):** while the window is resized, rotated or moved to a screen of another DPI, the cached canvas frame is redrawn at its own scale until the next render, at most the renderer's largest raster size. Broader G1 scope and estimates unchanged.
- **Done:** the selection tools take a clipping path (a clip group's or a layer's clipping mask) on its outline, within the selection tolerance, before the art it clips, so Direct Selection reshapes a mask where the art covers its edge; Select Behind lists the same, and the eyedropper and the tools that act on what is drawn are unchanged. Broader G1 estimates unchanged.
- **Done:** one selected clip group's Properties panel has Edit Clipping Path and Edit Contents at its top, which select its clipping path or its clipped art for the selection tools (public doc cited in target-app-parity.md). Broader G1 estimates unchanged.
- **Done:** the Properties panel has the additional contextual controls of the public Properties panel overview: Blend Options in Quick Actions for one blend with the Blend tool, Merge Live Paint for a Live Paint group selected with more paths to merge (Live Paint Make and Merge refuse type, images and other objects that aren't paths, which used to vanish among the group's sources), the Width Profile list in Appearance with the Width tool or a variable-width stroke, an applied effect's Delete icon beside fx (with several effects it opens the Appearance panel), and Corner and Corner Radius for corners selected with Direct Selection (public doc cited in target-app-parity.md). Broader G1 estimates unchanged.
- **Done (#2691):** a selected Grid Repeat ([public page](https://www.mw-wm.com/s/ep00MQi1Eq2KHWxflF)) shows a handle below the grid, one right of it and one past its bottom-right corner: dragging them adds or removes rows, columns or both (1 to 500). A slider between the first two columns and one between the first two rows set the horizontal and vertical spacing, staying halfway across the gap under the pointer. Each drag is one undo step through `object.repeat.options` and Escape cancels it; the controls hide with the edges or the bounding box, and bounding-box handles keep priority where they meet. Radial Repeat handles remain. Estimates unchanged.

- **Done (#2877):** a selected Mirror Repeat shows its axis: drag the line or the center handle to move it, an end handle to rotate it (Shift: 45°); each drag is one undo step and Escape cancels it. Bounding-box handles take priority over the axis line; the center and end handles keep their actions. Broader G1 estimates unchanged.

- **Existing-guide Escape cancellation:** Selection and Direct/Group Selection clear pending presses and cancel begun guide previews. App-input regressions cover preselected-guide document and interaction-start selection restoration, Undo/Redo and saved state, and later on-canvas motion/release. All eight app-input checks and the Direct Selection Escape control passed in current full CI; [Validation evidence](target-app-parity.md#evidence-what-ships-today-by-area). The broader G1 scope and estimate remain unchanged.

- **Done:** Artboards menu, trash and Properties delete selected artboards together; selecting all retains artboard 1. Pointer-event regressions cover ordinary artwork, the first-board survivor, Undo/Redo and the single-board guard; broader artboard reports remain open.

- **Done:** Artboard Delete/Backspace delete selected boards, retaining the original first when all are selected. The last board and active drags stay protected; headless shortcut regressions cover artwork, saved state and Undo/Redo.
- **Done:** status-bar artboard navigation synchronizes the Artboard tool selection before keyboard or Properties deletion, preserving ordinary artwork selection. Actual Next-button regressions cover both deletion keys, Properties Delete, Undo/Redo and other tools in `chrome.rs`. **Tab-switch follow-up:** changing the active document through its tab aligns the Artboard tool with the displayed board; same-tab multiselection and Move/Scale Artwork options are preserved. Three tab regressions and historical full CI on `a0671777` passed; [Validation evidence](target-app-parity.md#evidence-what-ships-today-by-area). The broader G1 scope and estimate remain unchanged. With the Artboard tool active, closing a clean active tab restores the surviving document's displayed board before Properties Delete.
- **Implemented and tested:** Undo removes invalid Artboard selection indices without resetting valid multiselection or Move/Scale Artwork options. Headless history tests cover actual panel New/Duplicate, deletion, artwork, object selection, saved state and Undo/Redo; full workspace CI passes.
- **Added:** Alt swaps the orientation of a new guide dragged from either ruler. Preview and final placement use the current axis; cancelling preserves the document and Redo, and a completed drag is one undo step. Tool and egui event regressions cover these interactions; the broader G1 pass and estimate remain unchanged.
- **Width-point follow-up:** Adjoining adjustments avoid intermediate overflow; non-finite normalized or resulting factors are rejected before committing. Engine regressions cover atomic rejection, Undo/Redo and native save/reopen. Current full CI passed; [Validation evidence](target-app-parity.md#evidence-what-ships-today-by-area). The broader G1 pass and estimate remain unchanged.
- **Done:** double-click a stroked segment to create a width point through Width Point Edit. Opening, Cancel and deleting the prospective point preserve the document and history; OK creates the point and optionally adjusts adjoining widths in one undo step. Regression and visual evidence: [Width-point creation](target-app-parity.md#evidence-what-ships-today-by-area).
- **Done:** Shift-double-click opens Width Point Edit with adjoining adjustment enabled. Plain double-click retains the default; dispatch, neighboring widths, Undo/Redo and Cancel have regression coverage.
- **Done (#1227):** object clicks with the Artboard tool create a fitted artboard, preserving art and selection; handles, modified clicks and drags retain their meaning. Covered by tool-event regression tests and undo/cancellation checks.
- **Done (#3705, in part):** pastes follow the drawing mode ([drawing modes](https://tlkg.yx-sf.com/peixun/software-06471762.html)): Draw Inside takes Paste, Paste in Place and Paste on All Artboards inside the object drawn into, Draw Behind puts Paste in Place and Paste on All Artboards behind the selection, and Shift+D no longer stops at Draw Behind when one group or other non-path object is selected.
- **Done:** Artboard Options' Show Center Mark and Show Cross Hairs ([public source](https://rnem.tcti.cn/yinqing/webinar-59303251.html)): per-artboard checkboxes (`artboard.setProps`/`artboard.new` `showCenterMark`, `showCrossHairs`) that the canvas draws as a center cross and lines from the middle of each side through the center; exports and print leave them out.

Both per artboard, one undo step, in the native format only when set. View › Rulers › Show Video Rulers is in G7.
- **Done (#3705):** Draw Inside in isolation mode ([isolation mode](https://xgnv.ai-hao123.com/sheji/satisfaction-53968918.html)): with the object drawn into isolated by a double-click, art drawn or pasted inside it takes isolation mode into its clip group, so it can be clicked and isn't dimmed; it used to stay locked and dimmed beside the isolated path, and double-clicks never reached the clip group.
- **Done:** Artboard Options' Show Center Mark and Show Cross Hairs ([public source](https://doc.tcti.cn/tag/AI)): per-artboard checkboxes (`artboard.setProps`/`artboard.new` `showCenterMark`, `showCrossHairs`) that the canvas draws as a center cross and lines from the middle of each side through the center; exports and print leave them out. Video safe areas, video rulers and the pixel aspect ratio remain missing.

- **Done (#2691):** a double-click on the Line Segment, Arc, Rectangular Grid or Polar Grid tool opens its Tool Options, as the [Rectangular Grid tool](https://yzqn.yx-sf.com/zhineng/analytics-42300717.html) and [Arc tool](https://zkuw.yx-sf.com/shuju/report-20452859.html) pages (step 3) and the [Tools](https://zkuw.yx-sf.com/shuju/report-20452859.html) page describe: the tool's click dialog without a place to draw (Line Segment adds Fill Line; the grids keep their Default Size and Reference Point). Broader G1 estimate unchanged.
- **Done:** Simplify of part of a path, as the [manual-simplify page](https://mmrp.yx-sf.com/yanjiu/mobile-85039228.html) describes for part of a path picked with Direct Selection: with anchors or segments of a path direct-selected, Object › Path › Simplify (the slider, Auto-Simplify and the dialog) refits only each run of selected segments between its end anchors, which stay where they are with their outer handles; the other anchors and segments stay exactly as they were, a closed path's run may cross its start point, separate runs on one path simplify independently in one undo step, and the runs stay selected (`object.path.simplify` `wholePaths: true` simplifies such paths whole). Tests: `crates/engine/src/tests/simplify_part.rs`, `simplify_slider_and_dialog_simplify_only_the_direct_selected_part_of_a_path`. Broader G1 estimate unchanged.

  The request to change interpolation of existing paths remains open.
- **Improved:** the Curvature tool's curve: each stretch of three points follows the circle through
  them (handles along its tangent, `chord / (3 cos²(α/2))` long) and the ends of an open path mirror

  and uneven spacing doesn't loop (#1236, in part). The rubber band, dragged, inserted and converted
  points use the same rule. Re-curving a dragged point's neighbours on an existing path remains open.

- **Done (#2120):** Smart Guides line extension: dragging the end of a straight segment with Direct Selection or Curvature, the point snaps to the segment's own direction at any angle and the guide runs along it from the other end. Inside the estimate below.
- **Done (#1692):** Tab in the Color Picker moves through one color model's fields before the next. Completed upstream before the layout change (#2008).
- **Improved (#2008):** Color Picker layout: stacked top-right actions, aligned inputs, less empty space, a distinct header and compact color controls. Narrow windows use stacked sections and vertical scrolling. Pointer/key, warning, layout and mode-switch regressions cover the change; the broader fidelity pass and estimates remain unchanged.
- **Done (#834):** bezier drag previews no longer freeze: a Pen, Anchor Point or Direct Selection drag gets every
  position the pointer is seen at, including the one where it comes back into the window after leaving it and a
  move in the frame it lets go, so the release commits where the pointer let go; a click's jitter stays a click.
- **Missing (noted for reporters, 2026-10-14):** aligning anchor points selected with
  Direct Selection to a key anchor (from #1636: they align to their bounds; the current public Align page does
  not say how the key anchor is chosen, so this waits for the owner). Inside the estimate below.
- **Missing:** a tool-by-tool, panel-by-panel pass over modifiers, cursors, the Properties panel per context,
  isolation mode and small behaviours, against the public tool and shortcut documentation. Itemized in
  [ui-parity.md](ui-parity.md). The Shaper's construction-mode widget and gesture refinements remain.
- **Evidence:** no side-by-side session has ever happened (the clean-room rule forbids running Illustrator, so
  the pass works from the documentation); users keep reporting small differences: #991, #975, #973, #955, #908.
- **Impact:** a power user notices this in the first minutes and stops trusting the tool.
- **Estimate:** 60–90 h; splits well by tool across agents.

## G9 Illustrator `.ai` and EPS files from real users

- **Done (2026-10-16):** EPS legacy mesh corners and vector opacity masks retained; winding-declared compound member groups keep shared paint. Raster print-page minification no longer causes a false editing-data fallback; comparison limits remain unchanged. Synthetic regressions cover damage and missing artwork. This narrows G9; scores and estimates unchanged.

- **Missing:** faithful layer and group structure from the editing data in real files (#951: 109 layers instead
  of 14), guides and non-printing construction
  lines (#779), open speed on large files (#758), live effects, brushes and symbols as live objects (#637; plain art styles read Drop Shadow, Outer Glow and Feather as live effects; pattern fills and global colours are read since #1025, placed (linked) files since #1264). Writing Illustrator's own editing data is out of scope
  (undocumented): a PDF-compatible `.ai` opens in Illustrator 2018 without its layers and groups (#868). Save As
  `.ai` › Version: Legacy (version 7) writes the PostScript form from the published version 7 specification
  instead, keeping layers (names, order, visibility, lock), groups, compound paths, clipping groups, gradients and
  images, and type as editable text objects (or outlines), one artboard per file (an artboard picker chooses
  which); transparency, live effects and object names don't survive it (transparent images are flattened or
  omitted, hidden objects go to a hidden layer, are omitted or made visible), and type is set again in the
  reader's fonts. Legacy type in `.ai` files in PostScript form is read on open. It waits for testing by users
  who hand files back.
- **Evidence:** the issues above; 28 of the 350 issues are about `.ai`/EPS (about 22 people, the most common single
  format theme), 20 fixed, and the 8 open ones are about structure (layers, guides, speed, live objects), not missing
  art. No real-file `.ai` corpus (users' files may be used locally, never committed).
- **Impact:** blocks anyone who hands files back to Illustrator users. Opening and reworking their own archive
  works, with layer cleanup in some files. This is the main-format gap that keeps the stage at alpha.
- **Estimate:** 10–20 h with users' files to test against.

## G10 Launch and stability on real machines

- **Unconfirmed (2026-10-14):** Tool cursors are painted into the window on Wayland (#1652; not run on Linux, #1645 stays open until confirmed). On Windows the custom title bar's window stays truly borderless, so the pointer lines up with what is drawn on systems where the hidden caption offset it (#1791, #1758; awaiting the reporter's confirmation).
- **Done:** RPM required dependencies use 64-bit library capabilities and declare glibc 2.35, libm and libgcc_s (#1275); generated metadata and isolated synthetic-provider checks cover x86_64/aarch64. Real-distribution install/start-up QA is still missing.
- **Missing:** the app not starting or staying in the background on some Windows 11 machines (#858, #964 fixed
  2026-10-10, #620, #818), slow pointer on a Linux AppImage (#575), macOS paste from other apps (#954), a
  web-free crash/hang reporter, a field record.
- **Evidence:** open issues; the never-crash lints and `guard` stop panics, not driver, windowing or packaging
  failures.
- **Impact:** an app that doesn't start on someone's machine is 0% for them.
- **Estimate:** 20–35 h, needs reporters' help on hardware we don't have.

## G8 Hardening at scale

- **Done:** PngSuite fetching verifies 175 original PNGs and redistribution notices against a pinned SHA-256/size manifest before publishing; file and total-size budgets, cache verification and no archive extraction (#1729). The real-world corpus and manual QA gaps below remain.

- **Done:** bounded synthetic control-input expansion (#1709): click/drag counts and pending-event capacity are checked before mutation, and control-channel bursts yield between frames. The corpus and platform QA below remain pending.
- **Done (2026-10-14):** WMF/EMF import refuses an oversized embedded PNG or JPEG from its header, before any pixels are decoded (#1776). PDF open no longer takes exponential time on a crafted name tree with shared nodes when it looks for the editing data (#1781). The size limits on a native file's embedded data also apply to files read from memory, not only streamed ones (#1783). Saving over a private file on Unix no longer leaves a readable temporary copy beside it while the file is written (#1778). An Export for Screens suffix can no longer place files outside the export folder (#1777). Package refuses a folder where it would overwrite the open document or one of its linked files (#1786). ruzstd 0.9.1 fixes a decompression bomb (RUSTSEC-2026-0344) reachable from EPS/`.ai` and Affinity import (#1807). Scatter graph data near the largest number is refused with a message instead of hanging the app (#1780). One very long Liquify stroke segment can no longer create an unbounded number of dabs (#1779). MCP limits: 16 MiB lines, 64-message batches, 256-step `command_batch` with 8 MiB of kept results and 256 MiB control replies (#1764, fixes #1727). MCP requires the JSON-RPC 2.0 envelope and matches control replies by id, and an app refusal without an id reports the app's reason (#1768, fixes #1728). The corpus and platform QA below remain pending.
- **Done:** control sockets have bounded idle, absolute partial-line and reply-write waits (#1726); real TCP tests cover idle, trickled and blocked peers, buffered partial lines, persistent requests and connection-slot recovery. The corpus and platform QA below remain pending.
- **Done (later 2026-10-14):** nesting capped at 32 objects across SVG, PDF, EPS and native files, self-using symbols
  and patterns (#1852); deep or self-referencing PDF and `.ai` data (#1871), decompression bombs and impossible
  predictors (#1873, #1700, #1701), self-drawing brushes (#1872), hostile EPS, Affinity and native data (#1863:
  #1715, #1714, #1704, #1699; save fallback #1695), ids at their largest value, failed `command.batch` rollback,
  timed-out control requests and oversized Eyedropper images (#1862: #1718, #1697, #1725, #1717), bounded shadows,
  glows and stacked Transform effects (#1864: #1706, #1705).
- **Done (2026-10-22):** SVG images in SVG images share the reader's depth cap: usvg reads an image while it reads the
  SVG showing it, on the same stack, so their depths add up, and `text/plain` and untyped data URLs (which usvg also
  reads as SVG) are measured as `image/svg+xml` ones are; an image past the cap is left out with a warning instead of
  overflowing the stack (#3562). SVGZ images are unpacked before usvg reads them, within one 512 MB cap for all of a
  file's images, where usvg unpacked a data URL's SVGZ without a cap (#3563).
- **Done (2026-10-22):** stacked geometry effects make at most 2 million anchors of a path (of all the paths of a
  type, symbol or image art together), or the path's own count when that is more. Roughen spaces its points further
  apart, Zig Zag makes fewer ridges a segment and Free Distort, Twist and the warps split segments into longer
  pieces where they would pass it, and an effect that would still pass it (Offset Path, Round Corners, a plug-in) is
  left out. The result is also kept to about 8 million lines for the renderer to draw at 1 px/pt (Wang's formula at
  vello's 0.25 px tolerance): a large Roughen or Zig Zag draws each point as up to hundreds of lines, so it is built
  again with fewer points. Three Roughens of a rectangle in a 25 KB file needed tens of gigabytes of geometry, and two
  million anchors of them 141 million lines (7 GB, past vello's 2²⁷ lines a path); the file now opens in 0.4 s and
  about 450 MB (#3578). The budget is per path, not per document: many objects that each reach it still add up.
- **Done (2026-10-23):** a brushed stroke makes at most 2 million anchors in total, the same figure as the
  stacked-effects budget above. Pattern tiling and scatter capped each factor on its own (20,000 tiles a run, 4,000
  subdivisions a segment, 20,000 copies a track), but those caps are per track and a path has as many tracks as it
  has subpaths, so they multiplied instead of bounding: one track at its cap measures 20,000 pieces and 320,000
  anchors, and sixteen subpaths measured exactly sixteen times that, 5.1 million anchors in 0.57 s. A piece is now
  taken whole or not at all, and the walk that counts an art tile's anchors charges the whole budget for a tree it
  cannot finish, so nesting buys no room (#3594). The budget is per brushed stroke, not per document: many strokes
  that each reach it still add up, and a brush inside a symbol is bounded per stroke rather than per instantiation.
- **Missing:** a corpus of real-world SVG/PDF/EPS files; more Affinity versions and platforms (51 pinned files
  now, including 28 original Affinity 3.2.3 feature probes; large interacting documents and complex typography
  missing); Windows, Linux and browser QA by hand; packaging polish (Homebrew cask #588, Flathub #554, update
  checks #615).
- **Impact:** unknown failures on users' files.
- **Estimate:** 30–50 h (the corpus and QA part blocks beta).

Shared editing-child traversal also preserves Shaper handling. Broader scope and estimates unchanged.

Broader G11 scope and estimates unchanged.

- **Done (2026-10-14):** Align and Distribute act on the anchor points selected with Direct Selection: the points of one path align to each other, not to the artboard, and Distribute spaces them (#1641, fixes #1636; aligning to a key anchor is still missing). Delete removes every selected anchor of a closed path (it used to remove the wrong ones), removes objects selected whole along with the selected anchors of others, and keeps the remainder selected so a second Delete removes it (#1674). In isolation mode Direct Selection and Group Selection pick only inside the isolated object (#1666). Escape cancels a Direct Selection drag (#1803, #1743). Escape while typing ends the edit, keeps the type selected and switches to the Selection tool (#1802, #1686, #1656). A filled Pencil path keeps a stroke of None (#1804, part of #1679). In the Pathfinder panel a group selected alone counts its nested shapes, so an expanded stroked object keeps the Shape Modes enabled (#1642, #1635). Object › Expand turns radial, grid and mirror repeats into groups of their instances (#1765, #1756). Select › Same matches type on its characters' fill and stroke (#1746, #1737). Roughen with Smooth keeps turn-backs smooth instead of making cusps that draw as spikes (#1646, #1643). Scribble draws one zig-zag per region, with no lines across holes and notches; convex shapes are unchanged (#1651, #1648).

- **Done:** Divide splits filled paths along open cutting lines and curves (#1307), preserving the frontmost filled appearance, implicit filled closure, holes, unrelated objects and one Undo/Redo; the existing bounded-map fallback remains.

- **Done:** Numeric fields keep a text drag's start when the pointer gains focus and movement exceeds the click threshold (#1326, in part). A completed focus click selects the whole value; keyboard focus, double-click and numeric stepping remain regression-tested. Short movements still classified as clicks can select all; that case remains open.

- **Done:** DXF reads control-point SPLINE closure (#1299 follow-up after #1320); open curves keep their open state. DXF export now recognizes circular cubic paths conservatively and writes native CIRCLE/ARC where stroke semantics permit; R12 weighted strokes remain POLYLINE, and a non-circular ellipse keeps the existing fallback. CNC preset and VCarve QA remain open. Escape leaves Artboard editing for Selection; during a drag it first cancels the gesture. Headless egui key events cover idle Escape, active-drag cancellation and a subsequent Escape in `tests/distortkeys.rs`.

- **Done:** Simplify and Add Anchor Points clear stale component selections on rewritten paths; Simplify previews and reports original/new point counts (#1272).
- **Done:** Object › Path › Simplify opens its slider at the Auto-Simplify level for the selection and previews that result, as the [manual-simplify page](https://www.mw-wm.com/s/ep00MQi1Eq2KHWxflF) describes; simplifying only a Direct Selection part of a path is done too (G1).
- **Done:** no-op anchor Align preserves Undo, Redo, saved state and path geometry (#1180 follow-up),
  with the same 1e-9 pt tolerance as whole-object Align; actual alignment remains one undo step.
- **Done:** Direct Selection picks a segment independently of its anchors and Delete preserves neighboring edges (#1278);
  scaled text's size and horizontal-scale controls account for object/group transforms (#1034),

  selected with Direct Selection (#1839, #1824); Snap to Grid wins over Snap to Pixel (#1840, #1816 unconfirmed); Redo
  during a drag keeps the drag (#1856, #1719); a template layer dims its images by Dim Images instead of fading the

  closed, the document left modified (#1865, #1685).
- **Done:** the Shape Builder offers the empty areas closed shapes enclose as regions, such as the middle of four
  circles that touch, and merges them with the regions around them (#1691).
- **Done (#2523):** Shape Builder Gap Detection shares Live Paint's spatially indexed gap finder,
  including its overshoot/hook safeguards. The existing Shape Builder Tool Options offers Small (3 pt),
  Medium (6 pt), Large (12 pt) or Custom (up to 72 pt). Temporary bridges are used in detection and
  merging, but are never added to the art. Off by default; `shapeBuilder.merge` and

  runs separate, without bridging the gap. The remainder stays selected for a second Delete; explicit Remove
  Anchors still reconnects/refits. Other G11 items and the estimate below remain unchanged.
- **Done (#1910):** Transform Each's Reflect X flips left-right and Reflect Y flips top-bottom (aligned with
  Effect › Distort › Transform). Properties flip buttons keep the reference app's Properties names (Flip Along Horizontal / Vertical
  Axis).
- **Done (#885):** the Transform effect dialog's checkboxes are visible, and it has Transform Objects, Transform
  Patterns and Scale Strokes & Effects: off, Transform Objects leaves the geometry in place; the other two scale
  stroke weights, dashes and the fills' and strokes' effect distances and move pattern tiles with the object, copy
  `k` by the transformation `k` times. Canvas, export and Expand Appearance agree. Not yet: a Transform effect in
  a fill's or stroke's own effect list ignores the two options, and object effects after it keep their distances.
- **Done (#937, reproduced case):** Shape Builder regions on art of more than 4,096 segments (traced or type
  outlines): the planar map no longer gives up there, so lines cut such art instead of the tool offering whole
  shapes (the planar map's edge-source and face lookups were quadratic in the segments, now indexed, and the cap is 65,536; Divide with open paths shares it). The edge-source index files a long segment under the grid cells along it, so a diagonal hatch (every line's bounds hold most points) no longer costs a scan of the hatch per edge. The grid holds a budget of references (64 per item plus four rows' or columns' worth), the items past it scanned, so coincident segments can't make it quadratic in memory.
- **Done (2026-10-24):** Shape Builder line and edge pieces on dense hatches: where the sweep cut a line's way there
  and its way back a rounding error apart and joined the two cuts with a stub a little over its tolerance, the stub
  came back as a speck of a piece (lines at exact 0.25 or 0.5 pt steps across a 45° line). The planar map now contracts
  such stubs into one vertex (within 4× the sweep's tolerance up and down its frame and 1/16 of the 0.01 pt precision
  along it, bounded by each cluster's extent so a run of tiny level segments keeps its length); regression tests
  in `crates/pathops/src/planar.rs`. Estimate unchanged.
- **Missing:** SVG units reverting to points (#864); a Transform effect in a fill's or stroke's own effect list ignores
  Transform Patterns and Scale Strokes & Effects (#885, above). Shape Builder regions (#937, closed), PDF text placement
  (#722, above), the bezier drag preview (#834, #3065, #3729) and deleting an interior anchor of an open path (above)
  are done.
- **Done (#722):** PDF text opens where the file draws it. Each line used to come in as point type laid out by the
  font's metrics (its kerning, one even tracking, every glyph on one baseline, a vertical glyph's column an em wide),
  so glyphs slid wherever the file spaced them otherwise. Now a line takes the font's kerning or none, whichever the
  file followed, and tracking that puts every glyph where the file drew it (word and character spacing and `TJ`
  adjustments per character); text rise (`Ts`) stays in the line as baseline shift; a vertical glyph is centred on
  its column by the font's own metrics (`/W2`, else half its `/W` or `/DW`, ISO 32000-1 §9.7.4.3); justified text
  boxes come back as justified area type. Fixtures written from ISO 32000-1 §9 (`tests_text_placement`). A font
  that is neither embedded nor installed still draws in a stand-in with the old fit.
- **Impact:** wrong output in everyday work.
- **Estimate:** 8–15 h.
