- **Done:** Ruby (ふりがな) for live text (`type.ruby`): a reading over a byte range, above or below (right of the
  column in vertical type), aligned, sized, overhanging or squeezed; saved natively, laid out with line growth, drawn
  on the canvas and in SVG/PDF (outlines where ruby is present), EPS, EMF/WMF and legacy `.ai` (outlines where ruby is
  present), and kept by Create Outlines, Expand Appearance and flattening; estimate unchanged.
- **Done:** colour emoji fonts with bitmap glyphs (`sbix`, as Apple Color Emoji; `CBDT`/`CBLC`, as Noto Color Emoji):
  each glyph is its largest strike's PNG, placed and transformed with the type, its fill and stroke ignored; PDF writes
  it in the font's Type 3 glyphs (or as an image), SVG as an image when type is outlined (live text leaves emoji to the
  viewer, and their fonts aren't embedded), EPS and legacy `.ai` as images, and Create Outlines makes embedded images.

  duplicate, flipped, JPEG and TIFF glyphs and `CBDT` BGRA and mask data draw nothing, nor do emoji in ruby or in
  enveloped or warped type; estimate unchanged.
- **Done:** COLR colour fonts (v0 and v1): a glyph's layers are vector art (solid colours, linear and radial
  gradients, clips, blend modes, palette 0, the foreground colour from the run's fill), placed with the type, drawn on

  paths with Create Outlines. Limits: glyphs using sweep gradients, Porter-Duff compositing, radial gradients from a
  circle that isn't the centre, or repeating gradients are images of the glyph until documents have those paints;
  estimate unchanged.
- **Done:** OpenType SVG colour fonts: each glyph's SVG document is read by the SVG importer into vector art,
  in the run's colours where it uses `currentColor` (or the legacy `context-fill`/`context-stroke`), then drawn, exported and outlined as COLR
  glyphs are (PDF real text writes them as text that draws nothing, their art drawn where they sit). Images in glyph documents
  go with the glyph's art; text and scripts are left out, as the table asks. Limit: CPAL palette variables; estimate
  unchanged.
- **Done:** threading ports (#2572): every selected area type and type on a path shows an in port and an out port,
  empty, with an arrow where it is threaded or with the red "+" of text that doesn't fit; with the Selection tool a
  click on the out port of any of them loads the text to thread on, and a click on the in port threads a new or
  clicked frame before it, so the story starts there (`text.thread.add` `before`). A double-click on a port where the
  frame is threaded breaks the thread there, the story flowing into the frames before the break and the frames after it
  left empty (`text.thread.break`; [archived help](https://abnk.ai-hao123.com/jiaocheng/management-82363228.html)); estimate unchanged.
- **Done:** variable fonts: the font menu's Font Technology › Variable lists only variable font families (a family
  with a variable file beside static ones included), together with the script, kind and favourites filters, as
  [Find, apply, and adjust variable fonts](https://feed.waepv.cn/d/OSaBm7QIJW)

- **Done:** COLR and SVG glyphs go with type that geometry effects reshape, into Expand Appearance and EMF/WMF
  export, where the type's outlines used to leave them out; bitmap glyphs (emoji) too, as images that hold their

- **Missing:** CJK vertical

- **Done:** the Effect Gallery (#2883): Effect › Effect Gallery… browses the Artistic, Brush Strokes, Distort, Sketch, Stylize and Texture filters, edits each filter's settings, builds an ordered stack (add, reorder, hide, remove) with a live canvas preview, and OK applies it as separate appearance effects in one undo step (`dialogs::effect_gallery::tests::stack_ok_is_one_undo_step`, `stack_preview_is_one_interaction`).
- **Done:** Effect › Sketch › Conté Crayon (`sketch.conteCrayon`: Foreground Level, Background Level, Texture, Scaling, Relief, Light Direction, Invert; original visual approximation, defaults unverified), the last missing filter.
- **Done:** Effect › Artistic › Colored Pencil (`artistic.coloredPencil`, pencil width, stroke pressure, paper brightness; original visual approximation).
- **Done:** the pixel-filter pipeline and all 57 Photoshop-style filters (Artistic, Blur, Brush Strokes, Distort, Pixelate,
  Sharpen, Sketch, Stylize, Texture, Video), with live preview and editable native settings. Smart Blur supports Edge Only and Overlay Edge
  modes. Per-filter detail: [effects-parity.md](effects-parity.md).
- **Estimate:** 1–2 h (Effect Gallery thumbnails and in-dialog preview).

## G13 Illustrator 2026 (30.x) additions

- **Done:** TIFF choices and format settings in Export for Screens and Asset Export (30.2), using the existing encoder; UI-to-file regressions cover selection, scaling, options and persistence.
- **Done:** artboard background colors on the canvas (30.0): Properties › Artboards › Fill and Artboard Options set
  each artboard's color, and the canvas draws its paper in it. Exports and print do not draw the color yet.

- **Done:** Object › Intertwine (#1763): Make, Edit and Release; the Intertwine tool highlights the overlap area under
  the pointer, a click swaps which object is on top there, and a path (Shift: a rectangle) drawn around overlaps
  arranges each one inside it; `object.intertwine.arrange` also brings an object to the front or sends it to the back
  where three or more overlap. The group renders, saves and exports through its live expansion. Still missing: the
  right-click Bring Forward / Send Backward menu where three or more objects overlap; adding objects to the group by
  dragging them in the Layers panel is untested.
- **Done (from users' reports):** Object › Create Gradient Mesh on an embedded image turns it into a mesh over its
  rectangle, with the image's transform kept; each point takes the average colour and opacity of the picture around it
  (#1676). A linked image is refused, as the public documentation has it.
- **Partial:** blend easing (#1124, 30.7): Window › Blend has Type (Ease In, Ease Out, Ease In Out,
  Ease Out In), Ramp 0–100% and independent color Shift; easing is disabled without a spine.
  The original polynomial distributions approximate the public description. On-canvas easing handles
  and their synchronization remain missing. [Public source](https://doc.tcti.cn/tag/AI).

- **Done:** gradient Dither (30.0): the Gradient panel's Dither box (`paint.editGradient` `dither`, also in `paint.setFill`'s
  `gradient`, swatches and the native file) draws a linear or radial gradient fill as pixels with seeded noise of up to a
  colour level, which hides banding on the canvas and in raster exports; SVG and PDF exports write the fill as an image at
  the Document Raster Effects resolution, and PDF with Preserve Editing keeps the gradient editable. Fills only, as the
  [public documentation](https://info.yx-sf.com/sitemap.xml) says. Freeform gradients ignore it.
- **Done:** gradient Method (30.0): the Gradient panel's Method menu, Classic or Perceptual (`paint.editGradient`
  `method`, also in `paint.setFill`'s `gradient`, swatches and the native file, written only when Perceptual). Perceptual
  mixes a linear or radial gradient's colours in OKLab, so blue to yellow passes through a light blue-grey rather than
  mid grey; renderers draw it through stops on that curve (within half a colour level), and SVG and PDF exports write it
  as an image at the Document Raster Effects resolution, as the
  [public documentation](https://olku.tcti.cn/anfang/analysis-01421877.html) says perceptual gradients are rasterised there.
  Classic draws exactly as before; freeform gradients mix their own way. With Dither, a Perceptual fill is the
  perceptual mix with dither's noise (an image with the noise in SVG and PDF); a stroke has no noise.
- **Missing (asked for by users, from earlier versions):** radial gradients in Image Trace's
  Gradients option, which traces linear ones only (draft #1849). Inside the estimate below.
- **Partial (#2530):** tangent snapping to curves and perpendicular snapping to straight target
  segments for drawn lines. Controls are saved under Preferences › Smart Guides › Geometric Guides
  and available from Control bar › Snapping; both default to on. Existing-line endpoint editing and
  other tool cases remain unverified. [Public source](https://doc.zhushou.pro/sitemap.xml).
- **Missing:** gradient presets (30.0); remaining tangent/perpendicular snapping cases and the consolidated
  snapping options (30.0); artboard colors in exports and print, and managing artboards from the canvas other
  than locking and unlocking them from the Artboard tool's right-click menu (30.0); the Blend panel with ease
  in/out and separate colour acceleration (30.7);
  the Dimension tool (28.x).
- **Evidence:** Adobe's 30.0 and 30.7 release announcements, see
  [target-app-parity.md](target-app-parity.md#how-this-was-measured-2026-10-10).
- **Estimate:** 13–23 h.
- **Estimate:** 14–24 h.

## G5 Brushes, symbols and libraries

## G15 Performance budgets and a GPU renderer

- **Improved (#1257):** Craquelure, Mosaic Tiles and Stained Glass reuse squared distances during nearest-cell searches, with the original distance ordering retained near rounding/tie boundaries. A brute-force boundary regression and full-viewport pixel comparisons agree with the old result. `texture_drag_perf` reproduces a moved CMYK rounded rectangle at 190.07% and DPI 1.5; timings from a busy development machine are supporting evidence, with idle Windows drag QA still pending.
- **Missing:** an idle-machine run of `vectorcraft-cli perf` at 50k paths (2026-10-11 at 25k paths, every budget
  met, 400% zoom 12.3 ms against 16 ms, measured; runs of 0.10.0 on Linux with 4 logical CPUs, reported in #1172
  on 2026-10-13, missed all three render budgets at 20k paths), a spatial index for zoomed-in frames, dirty-region
  rendering, the GPU backend spike (M5). Large-selection edits, cached live effects and Pathfinder Trim, Merge,
  Crop and Outline landed in #1173.
- **Estimate:** 15–25 h (the budget run and fixes block beta).

## G17 Ecosystem: third-party plug-ins

- **Missing:** Illustrator's ecosystem is a C++ plug-in SDK and a large commercial plug-in market. VectorCraft
  has sandboxed WebAssembly plug-ins for object filters, live effects and file formats it writes
  ([plugins.md](plugins.md)) and MCP; missing are tool plug-ins, panel plug-ins, importers, a plug-in directory and
  any third-party plug-ins (#710).
- **Done:** exporter plug-ins (`"kind": "exporter"`). A plug-in adds a write-only file format that File › Export ›
  Export As lists after the built-in ones and `document.export` writes (`plugin.<id>`, or a path ending in one of its
  extensions). It is given the document as the native file's JSON and its parameters, with a larger budget than a
  filter's, which Background Export's Cancel stops; the host writes the file it returns, and nothing when it declines
  or returns bad data. Engine, ABI and headless Export As regressions.
- **Done:** a plug-in's parameters say how its dialogs show them: `label`, `unit`, `help`, `helpUrl`, `group`
  (sections that fold) and `visibleWhen` (shown only while the checkboxes and choices it names have one of the
  listed values). `string` and `numberList` parameters join the others, and a plug-in declares up to 256, at most 64
  outside groups. The filter, live-effect and exporter dialogs use them, and the Appearance panel's effect editor the
  labels, units, help and conditions; hosts from before the keys ignore them. Manifest unit tests and kittest dialog
  regressions.
- **Done:** a live effect is given its object's fills and strokes, read only, as a filter is, and `_context.item`
  says which fill or stroke it sits on; a change of paint runs it again. Engine and unit regressions.
- **Done:** a filter is given its objects' effect records and their strokes' join, cap and miter limit, and may
  return both: the records are admitted as `effect.apply` admits them (one refused refuses the output), so a tool can
  set up objects for a live effect in one step. A path a filter hands back unchanged stays a live shape. Engine and
  unit regressions.
- **Done:** a filter keeps data with the document (`documentData`, at most 1 MiB, in the same undo step as its
  objects) and reads it back in `_context.documentData`. It is the document's foreign data (`unknown.pluginData`), so
  the native file keeps it with no section of its own, and an exporter finds it in the document it is given. Engine
  and unit regressions.
- **Done:** a filter may ask for a heavy budget (`"budget": "heavy"`: 1 G instructions and 300 s a run), for routing,
  packing or simulation. Installing it asks the user first (`allowHeavy`; folders skip it), and the app runs it on a
  thread of its own with a progress window and Cancel, applying its result as one undo step unless the document
  changed meanwhile. ABI, engine and headless UI regressions.
- **Estimate:** 20–45 h for the APIs; the ecosystem itself isn't agent work.

## G19 Accessibility

- **Missing:** AccessKit is on by default, so egui widgets reach screen readers, but custom panels, the canvas and its objects aren't described and nothing has been tested with VoiceOver, Narrator or Orca; keyboard-only canvas operation; high
  contrast. Illustrator's own accessibility is limited, so this is mostly beyond parity.

- **Estimate:** 15–25 h.

## Highlighted-text Eyedropper (2026-10-21)

Type/Eyedropper switches preserve highlighted characters; sampling changes only their enabled
font/paint attributes. Enabled non-neutral source or target object transparency is refused
atomically; disable Transparency to preserve object transparency while sampling the range.
`tests/eyedropper.rs` covers ranges, Unicode, history and transparency; tool tests cover brush-key
sampling coexistence. Scores and estimates unchanged. See [development.md](development.md#highlighted-text-eyedropper-2026-10-21).

## Drag artwork between document tabs (2026-10-22)

Selection drags activate another visible document tab after 400 ms, then copy editable artwork
on canvas release with the original grab point. Source and clipboard preservation, resource
rendering, swatch conflicts, cancellation, rotated/zoomed views and target Undo/Redo have regression
coverage (`tests_document_drag`, `tests_clipboard`). Overflow-menu and cross-window drag remain
separate. Scores and hours unchanged. [Behavior and command details](development.md#drag-artwork-between-document-tabs-2026-10-22).

## Pathfinder › Trap (2026-10-23)

The Pathfinder panel menu's Trap… (`object.pathfinder.trap`) and Effect › Pathfinder › Trap…
(`pathfinder.trap`) ship, from the public [trapping](https://doc.ai-hao123.com/sitemap.xml)
and [Pathfinder panel](https://huve.tcti.cn/wenzhang/forecast-60448214.html) pages: where two
objects' visible areas of different solid colours meet, an overprinting strip of the lighter colour goes into the
darker one (Reverse Traps: the other way, but not a rich black), with Thickness, Height/Width, Tint Reduction and
Traps with Process Color, and in the effect Precision and Remove Redundant Points. The panel's Trap is one undo
step and groups the traps above the topmost selected object. Effect › Pathfinder is complete (13/13); the Live
vector effects missing list no longer names Hard Mix, Soft Mix or Trap. Left: gradient and pattern fills don't
trap, and the defaults (0.25 pt, 100%, 40%) are VectorCraft's own, the pages give none. Tests:
`crates/engine/src/tests/trap.rs`, `crates/effects/src/trap.rs`, `crates/pathops/src/trap.rs`.

### Hardware parity

# Hardware parity

> **Last reviewed:** 2026-10-10 · **Last updated:** 2026-10-24 · **Change:** minor (pen pressure and the pen's eraser end on macOS, read from AppKit's tablet events, #852, not yet tried on a Mac; previously: patch: web pen buttons/modifiers preserved, touch-only input left to eframe, session-only palm rejection; tool cursors painted into the window on Wayland, #1652, not run on Linux; borderless title-bar window on Windows, #1758, awaiting confirmation; a window surface larger than 8192 px keeps working, #1459 in part; Linux Display Server preference opens the window through XWayland, #1151) · **Target:** Adobe Illustrator 2026 (30.x)

What hardware Illustrator uses, per platform, against VectorCraft. Illustrator's side is from its public
documentation (GPU Performance, touch workspace, pen pressure pages); ours from the code
(`crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`, `touch.rs`, `graphics.rs`, `crates/render`). Part of
[target-app-parity.md](target-app-parity.md).

## Summary

**~35% (estimated), 25–45 h.** VectorCraft rasterizes the canvas on the CPU (multithreaded `vello_cpu`) and uses
the GPU only to composite, so any GPU that can show a window works, at the cost of GPU-accelerated preview
on huge documents. VectorCraft reads pen pressure on Windows, on the web, on macOS, and on Linux under X11 and XWayland, and it
reads the pen's eraser end on macOS, on Linux under X11 and XWayland, and on the web when it presses.
reads the pen's eraser end on Windows, on macOS and on Linux under X11 and XWayland.

| Feature | Illustrator | VectorCraft macOS | Windows | Linux | Web | Status / hours |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GPU-accelerated canvas (GPU Performance, GPU Preview, GPU anti-aliasing) | Metal, DirectX | CPU raster, GPU composite (wgpu/Metal) | CPU raster, GPU composite (DX12, OpenGL fallback) | CPU raster, GPU composite (Vulkan/GL) | WebGPU, WebGL2 fallback | partial; a GPU renderer spike is pending (M5): 15–25 h |
| Multithreaded rendering off the UI thread | partial | yes | yes | yes | single-threaded | beyond Illustrator |
| Hybrid-graphics GPU choice | automatic | power-saving GPU by default, Preferences › Graphics Processor | same; DX12 then OpenGL; no Vulkan unless asked (#545, #806) | the desktop's GPU | browser | done |
| Restart on another GPU when the first fails to present | — | yes (#502, #964) | yes | yes | restart on lost device (#369) | done |
| Pen pressure | yes (Wacom, Windows Ink, macOS tablet events) | yes, read from AppKit's tablet events before the window gets them (winit reports none), each move of a stroke with its own pressure, mouse event coalescing off (#852; not yet tried on a Mac) | yes (pointer force via `WM_POINTER`) | under X11 and XWayland (Preferences › Performance › Linux Display Server, #1151, #2028), read from XInput2 raw events (#764); **no** on native Wayland, where winit reports none and the pen may not reach the window (#491) | browser pointer events, with coalesced events; Apple Pencil on iPad (hover, palm rejection: fingers navigate after a pen contact until reload) | partial: 2–4 h for Wayland (winit 0.31), plus a check on a Mac |
| Pen tilt, bearing, barrel rotation (6D Art Pen) | yes, drives brushes | no | no | no | no | missing: 4–8 h after the input layer (#372) |
| Pen eraser end | yes | the eraser end (AppKit's tablet proximity events) selects the Eraser tool and the tip brings back the tool used before, as on Linux (#852; not yet tried on a Mac) | no | under X11 and XWayland, the eraser end selects the Eraser tool and the tip brings back the tool used before (#764); **no** on native Wayland | a press of the eraser end (Pointer Events eraser button, `button` 5) selects the Eraser tool, and that press erases; a press of the tip brings back the tool used before; Pointer Events report no end while the pen hovers | partial |
| Pen eraser end | yes | the eraser end (AppKit's tablet proximity events) selects the Eraser tool and the tip brings back the tool used before, as on Linux (#852; not yet tried on a Mac) | with Windows Ink, an inverted pen or its eraser button (`PEN_FLAG_INVERTED`, `PEN_FLAG_ERASER` in the pen's pointer messages) selects the Eraser tool and the tip brings back the tool used before, as on Linux (not yet tried with a pen) | under X11 and XWayland, the eraser end selects the Eraser tool and the tip brings back the tool used before (#764); **no** on native Wayland | no | partial |
| Touch gestures (pinch zoom, two-finger pan, rotate view, Touch workspace) | yes (Windows touch, Surface) | trackpad pinch, scroll and rotate | pinch, pan; two-finger tap undo, three-finger redo (#585) | same where winit reports touch | eframe until the first pen contact, then Pointer Events (pen and fingers told apart); long press opens the context menu | partial: touch workspace and touch-screen rotation missing, 3–5 h |
| Trackpad (smooth scroll, pinch) | yes | yes | precision touchpads | yes | yes | done |
| HiDPI / Retina, per-monitor scale | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | done; a window dragged between monitors of different scale can still grow on Windows (#1459, open); the custom title bar's window on Windows stays truly borderless so the pointer lines up with what is drawn (#1791, #1758; awaiting the reporter's confirmation) |
| Multiple monitors: panels and document windows on another screen | yes | no (one OS window) | no | no | — | missing: 6–10 h (with multiple windows, gap G7) |
| Display colour profile (proof and display through the monitor's ICC) | yes | no | no | no | — | missing: 3–5 h |
| 3D GPU rendering (Materials, ray tracing) | yes | — | — | — | — | blocked on 3D (gap G3) |

## Revision history

| Date | Change | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-10-24 | minor | macOS: an AppKit local event monitor reads each mouse and tablet event's pen pressure and the pen's end before the window gets it and writes them into the canvas's pen feed (#852): each pointer move of a stroke keeps its own pressure, mouse event coalescing is off, and the eraser end selects the Eraser tool. The mapping is unit-tested on every platform and the macOS code type-checks for `aarch64-apple-darwin`; not yet tried on a Mac with a tablet, so the score is unchanged (estimated) |
| 2026-10-15 | patch | Web review: preserve pen buttons and modifiers; leave fingers to eframe before the first pen contact; remove persistent pen policy. Canvas regression tests cover intermediate moves and long-touch cancellation on native and web input. Physical-device QA pending. |
| 2026-10-14 | minor | Tool cursors are painted into the window on Wayland (#1652; not run on Linux, #1645 stays open until confirmed); On Windows the custom title bar's window stays truly borderless, so the pointer lines up with what is drawn on systems where the hidden caption offset it (#1791, #1758; awaiting the reporter's confirmation); neither is confirmed on the hardware that reported it, so nothing is marked done |
| 2026-10-13 | minor | Web: the shell reads pen and finger Pointer Events itself (pen pressure with coalesced events, Apple Pencil hover, palm rejection: after a pen contact fingers only navigate until reload; long press opens the context menu); score unchanged (estimated) |
| 2026-10-13 | minor | A window whose surface is larger than 8192 px (stretched over several monitors, or grown by a drag between monitors of different scale) is configured up to the graphics adapter's limit instead of closing the app (#1495, part of #1459); the window growing during that drag on Windows is still open; not reproduced on a mixed-scale setup |
| 2026-10-11 | minor | Preferences › Performance › Linux Display Server › X11 (XWayland) opens the window through XWayland on a Wayland session, where pens and dropped files reach the app (#1151); score unchanged (estimated) |
| 2026-10-10 | major | First checklist from the canvas, touch and graphics code and the open hardware issues |

### Adjusting an Image Trace

# Adjusting an Image Trace

Select a placed raster image, then choose **Image Trace** or a preset from its arrow
in Properties or the Control bar. The original image stays inside the tracing object so
that subsequent adjustments always use the original pixels.

To adjust the result, select the tracing object and click **Image Trace** in Properties or the
image icon in the Control bar: the Image Trace panel opens with **Advanced** expanded. An existing floating or docked panel is activated in
its current location. Opening the controls does not add a document undo step.

| Control | Range | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Threshold (Black and White) | 0–255 | Higher values include lighter pixels as black ink. |
| Paths | 0–100% | Higher values fit outlines more closely to the image. |
| Corners | 0–100% | Higher values preserve more sharp turns. |
| Noise | 1–100 px | Suppresses small connected regions; higher values remove more small details. |
| Method | Abutting / Overlapping | Chooses shared boundaries or stacked overlapping paths. |
| Create | Fills / Strokes | Creates filled areas, stroked lines, or both. |
| Ignore Color | Color picker | Leaves out the selected color (white by default). |

Sliders apply on release, and their numeric fields can be edited directly. Each committed
adjustment re-traces the selected object as one undo step and changes the preset to Custom.
While dragging, the preset and Enhanced row stay in place until release so the
slider retains its active interaction. Committed settings are synchronized immediately,
so Undo also restores the panel values before its next frame. View can show the source image, the result, outlines, or combinations without re-tracing.
Use **Expand** when finished to turn the result into ordinary editable vector objects;
after expanding, the tracing settings are no longer available. **Release** restores the source.

**Auto Color** (the Automatic palette) counts flat art's colours by area, and also keeps colours too
rare for that count when they are distinct and drawn as regions of their own (a stem, a highlight, a
white beside a cream), at most six; scattered specks of a colour add none. Adobe does not document how
its own palettes are chosen; this is VectorCraft's own method (see
[image-trace-quality.md](image-trace-quality.md#auto-color-keeps-rare-colours)).

**Document Library color groups.** With Palette › Document Library and Library › Document Swatches,
the panel's **Colors** menu traces with every document swatch (**All**) or with the colors of one
color group from the Swatches panel, as the public
[Image Trace panel options](https://ovws.ai-hao123.com/jiaocheng/hotel-31156520.html)
page ([archived](https://udzr.ai-hao123.com/shuju/like-94113635.html))
describes Document Library. In the params of `imageTrace.make` or `imageTrace.makeAndExpand`,
`"colorGroup": "<name>"` names the group. It needs `"mode": "color"`, `"palette": "documentLibrary"` and
`"library": "document"`; a `colorGroup` with a nonempty name and any other mode, palette or library is refused. An
empty name names no group and is accepted with any mode, palette or library; with Document Library and
`"library": "document"` it traces with every document swatch. A group whose name matches exactly is used first, then one whose name differs only in case. At
most `colors` of its colors are used. A missing group and a group with no solid colors are refused. Choosing another
mode, palette or library in the panel clears the group. A group the active document does not have shows as All
and traces as All.

**Document Library** traces with the library's colors as they are. Each pixel takes the library
color nearest to it in lightness and hue, with a difference in hue or chroma counted three times
as much as one in lightness, so a gray or a muted brown takes a black, white or other neutral
library color rather than a saturated color of the same lightness.
**Abutting and Overlapping.** Abutting is the default Method, and the Default, Auto Color, 3 Colors,
6 Colors and 16 Colors presets use it. With Abutting, two neighboring colors share one exact edge. The
canvas smooths the edges of each path on its own, so each of the two paths covers only part of the
pixels along that edge, and a thin line of the background can show between the colors. Web browsers
and PDF viewers usually draw an exported SVG or PDF file the same way and show the same line. Raster
exports (PNG, JPEG, TIFF and the other bitmap formats) with None anti-aliasing do not show it at any
size. Raster exports with Art Optimized anti-aliasing, the default, do not show it up to 10 million
pixels and 16,384 pixels on a side. A raster export shows the line as the canvas does when it uses
Type Optimized anti-aliasing, or when it uses Art Optimized and is larger than either limit.
Overlapping stacks the colors instead: a lower color continues under the edge of the color above it,
and no background shows along that edge.
**Large images.** An image of more than 1500 pixels on a side is traced as any other, only more
slowly, and the trace says so: `imageTrace.make` returns the note in `warnings` and the status bar
shows it (the [results optimization](https://zkuw.yx-sf.com/shuju/report-20452859.html)
page describes the same warning for images over 1500 px). An image of more than 64 megapixels (up to
192) is traced from a copy scaled down to 64 megapixels, and the trace says that too. Flat Logo traces at
most 1024 pixels on a side: a larger decoded raster is averaged down in whole-number blocks first (a 1025-pixel
image is traced at 513, and a 16,000 × 12,000 image, decoded at 9,459 × 7,094, is traced at 946 × 710), and the trace names both sizes in `warnings`. Flat Logo gives that note in place
of the slower-trace note for an image over 1500 pixels and in place of the 64-megapixel note. An image at most
1024 pixels on a side is traced at its own size, also when the named `logoColors` differ slightly from the
image's colors. Only an image with more than 150,000 different pixel values that are not exactly one traced
color is averaged down further: the factor doubles until at most 150,000 remain or the working copy has at
most 16,384 pixels (at most six times). A trace that would
make more than 8,000,000 anchor points (2,000,000 on the web) is refused to protect memory, with advice:
raise Noise, lower Paths or Colors, or pick a lower-fidelity preset. A trace keeps
about 90 bytes an anchor; a 4000 × 3000 photo at High Fidelity Photo makes about 1.9 million.
These controls use VectorCraft's existing tracing algorithm. Parameter effects follow its
implementation; they do not claim pixel-identical results with another application.
The terminology and general control behavior are described in the
[public Image Trace panel documentation](https://udzr.ai-hao123.com/shuju/like-94113635.html).

Regression coverage: `crates/ui-egui/src/panels/image_trace.rs` tests opening the panel,
a quick trace leaving it as it was, repeated opening, floating ownership, slider commits, visible threshold
changes, undo, and the Properties entry point. Tracer tests live in `crates/trace/src/tests.rs`.

### Image Trace quality

# Image Trace quality

What Image Trace (`crates/trace`) makes of images whose right answer is known, measured by a harness and
compared with the numbers before each change. Nothing here is a judgement by eye, and nothing is compared
with any other product except the open tracer named under [Yardstick](#4-yardstick).


## Auto Color keeps rare colours

The Automatic palette (Auto Color) counts flat art's colours by area: a colour needs about 1% of the
picture (0.5% at Colors 100) to be counted, and the count is then fitted by median cut (Heckbert 1982)
and k-means (Lloyd 1982), weighted by area. A stem, a highlight or a cream close to a pale background
was averaged into a large neighbour, and Noise could remove what was left of it. Now, on the flat route
only, after the count is fitted, the colours too rare or too close for it are found and kept when they
are:

- distinct: at least 2.5 (Oklab × 100; Ottosson 2020) from every palette colour and from the main
  colour each one stands for;
- flat: mostly one histogram bin;
- drawn: a 4-connected region of their own (not blended) pixels of at least 8 pixels, or three of at
  least 4 (repeated highlights); a colour lying between two others, as an edge's anti-aliasing mixes
  them, must also have an inside (pixels whose four neighbours are all of it).

At most six are kept, largest region first. They are fixed while the other colours are refitted around
them, mixed-colour merging leaves them alone, and Noise removal keeps their regions of 4 pixels or more
(smaller specks of them still go). This follows the idea of salient-colour preservation in palette
reduction (Fukuda et al. 2019, doi:10.1117/12.2521607); the rule and its numbers are VectorCraft's own.
Full Tone, Limited and the continuous-tone route of Automatic are unchanged.

Tests (code-drawn): `automatic_keeps_a_rare_distinct_stem_or_patch` (2, 3, 5 and 8 flat colours and a
contrasting stem 1–4 px wide or a patch, about 0.05% to 0.5% of the picture, hard and anti-aliased at
1× and 2×: the stem's colour is kept and no other is added), `automatic_keeps_near_white_highlights_on_a_pale_background`
(ten white islands of about 12 px on #FFF4E0: kept, each still a path at Noise 16),
`automatic_keeps_a_thin_low_contrast_stem` (#909090 on #808080, 3 px), `scattered_noise_adds_no_colour`
(the negative control: the same areas as single scattered pixels add no colour) and
`noise_keeps_a_kept_rare_colours_regions_but_not_its_specks` (Noise 0 to 32).

Measured on 22 synthetic flat-colour logos drawn from known palettes, each hard 1×, anti-aliased 1×
and 2× (66 inputs, used locally and not committed; a key colour is missing when no traced colour is
within ΔE00 5): every key colour and no spurious one in **66 of 66** (was 39); missing key colours 0 (was 43),
spurious 0 (was 2), key colours sharing one traced colour 0 pairs (was 46); mean rendered ΔE00 against
the input 0.138 (was 0.348); paths 2547 → 2586, anchors 27,204 → 24,896, trace time 2.85 → 3.02 s in
all. On four public-domain scan crops (1024 × 1024) Auto Color takes the continuous-tone route and
nothing changes: 14, 72, 199 and 98 colours, the same paths, anchors and rendered error (2.11, 5.66,
9.15 and 1.00 ΔE00), time within run-to-run spread.


## Large images
Images over 1500 px on a side are traced with a warning that they trace more slowly (Flat Logo names
the size it traced at instead; see
[image-trace-adjustments.md](image-trace-adjustments.md)), and the anchor limit that guards memory is
8,000,000 (2,000,000 on the web) instead of 2,000,000. Measured through `imageTrace.make` (release
build, 4 cores, one trace at a time; memory is the peak allocated above the placed image, and what the
document keeps after the trace) on code-drawn photo-like pictures (40 soft-edged shaded discs on a
gradient, texture, sensor noise):
| size | preset | time | anchors | paths | peak | kept |
|:--|:--|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2000 × 2000 | High Fidelity Photo | 4.1 s | 737,478 | 16,064 | 152 MB | 52 MB |
| 2000 × 2000 | Low Fidelity Photo | 1.6 s | 114,008 | 1,486 | 142 MB | 7 MB |
| 2000 × 2000 | Default | 0.9 s | 103,084 | 1,001 | 117 MB | 6 MB |
| 3000 × 2000 | High Fidelity Photo | 6.4 s | 1,013,114 | 25,256 | 236 MB | 75 MB |
| 3000 × 2000 | Default | 1.2 s | 145,756 | 1,574 | 162 MB | 9 MB |
| 4000 × 3000 | High Fidelity Photo | 12.8 s | 1,914,018 | 58,638 | 471 MB | 150 MB |
| 4000 × 3000 | Low Fidelity Photo | 5.1 s | 258,826 | 4,833 | 428 MB | 18 MB |
| 4000 × 3000 | Default | 2.4 s | 273,392 | 3,568 | 317 MB | 17 MB |
| 4000 × 3000 | 16 Colors | 3.0 s | 103,222 | 2,434 | 364 MB | 7 MB |
| 4000 × 3000 | Full Tone, Colors 85, Paths 90, Noise 4 | 29.6 s | 5,230,847 | 164,687 | 684 MB | 412 MB |
| 4000 × 3000 | Full Tone, Colors 100, Paths 100, Noise 1 | 37.2 s | 7,885,709 | 338,561 | 876 MB | 685 MB |
| 6000 × 4000 | Full Tone, Colors 85, Paths 90, Noise 4 | 106.1 s | 10,445,409 | 398,772 | 1169 MB | 872 MB |
| 6000 × 4000 | Full Tone, Colors 100, Paths 100, Noise 1 | 116.3 s | 13,508,871 | 658,133 | 1456 MB | 1230 MB |
(The last two rows were measured without a limit; they are refused now.) The 4000 × 3000 High Fidelity
Photo trace was 86,000 anchors under the old limit; a noisier scan of the same size would have been
refused. At 8,000,000 anchors a trace keeps about 0.7 GB, with a peak of about 0.9 GB while tracing.
## Collapsed loops keep few segments
A small closed loop (or a piece that returns to its own junction) whose fit collapsed to a single
cubic cannot stay as one, so it kept every positioned point as a straight segment. A looser Paths
collapses more loops, so it could give more segments than a tighter one. Such a loop now tries the
fewest segments that still hold it, each only if the result keeps an area (more than 0.25 px²) and
stays within 1.5 × max(tolerance, 0.5 px) of the points both ways: the fit at up to three somewhat
tighter tolerances (what a slightly higher Paths gives); for a closed loop then two cubics split at
its start and its farthest point, then the outline simplified at the tolerance and finer; the
positioned points last, as before.
Test on code-drawn images: `a_higher_paths_never_gives_fewer_segments` (32 seeded 48 px images of
soft blobs in four colours plus pixel noise, Color and Black and White, Noise 1 and 3, segments at
Paths 0, 25, 50, 75 and 100 must not fall). Before, six runs fell, e.g. 125 → 79 segments from
Paths 0 to 25 (seed 21, Color, Noise 1) and 71 → 63 → 52 from Paths 0 to 50 (seed 3, Black and
White, Noise 3); now they are 75 → 79 and 41 → 48 → 52. One image (seed 16 in Black and White) still
falls from 140 to 136 segments between Paths 0 and 25, before and after this change; that fall has
another cause, still open, and the image is left out of the test. The crate's other tests pass unchanged.
## Notches read only their own piece
Where the pixel at a sharp corner falls to the other colour, the outline cuts the corner in two
one-pixel steps, and between two straight edges of three cracks or more those two steps become one
point, where the two edges meet (a notch). Whether the edges were long enough was measured on the
whole loop. An edge can run on past a junction in one region's loop while the region across it,
whose loop turns at that junction, sees a shorter edge: one side made the notch and the other did
not, the shared piece got different points on each side, and the abutting curves left a gap. The
rule in `subpixel::outline` now also requires the three cracks of each edge next to the notch to lie
in the piece (no junction among them), as the corner-pixel correction above it already did.
Test on code-drawn images: `noisy_colour_images_leave_no_sample_uncovered` (20 seeded 36 px images
of soft overlapping blobs in four colours plus pixel noise; Color, 5 colours, Noise 1 and 2, Paths
0, 50 and 100; five sample points per pixel must each lie in some path). Without the condition 93
sample points were uncovered (seeds 9, 11 and 13); with it none are. The crate's other tests pass
## Same sub-pixel shift from either side of an edge
Each crack between two regions is moved by a sub-pixel shift read from the image. The reading
looked for a thin run (one to three pixels) on the crack's inside before one on its outside, so where
both sides were thin (a one- or two-pixel sliver beside another, as in soft gradients and noisy
scans) the two regions of the crack got different shifts, their shared piece different points, and
the abutting curves left slivers that no path covers. `Layers::shift` now averages the reading from
either side, `(s(c) - s(c flipped)) / 2`, which is exactly antisymmetric in floating point, so both
regions get the same points.
Tests on code-drawn images: `a_crack_between_thin_slivers_has_the_same_shift_from_either_side` (a
noisy ripple of 1–2 px columns at three thresholds: every crack's shift is the exact negative of its
flipped crack's, and the image does have cracks the one-sided reading gets wrong) and, in
`tests/shared_boundaries.rs`, `thin_slivers_on_both_sides_of_an_edge_leave_nothing_uncovered` (a
48 px noisy ripple in Black and White at thresholds 140, 157, 170 and Paths 0, 50, 100, sampled on
the 4 × 4 grid per pixel the shared-boundary check uses). With the one-sided reading 482–1,228
sample points per trace were uncovered; now none are. The crate's other tests pass unchanged.
## A simpler contour walk
`contour::trace_mask` follows each region's outline along the pixel cracks with the inside on the
right. It used to build a table of outgoing directions for every pixel corner in a raster pass and
then follow it. It now works out each turn during the walk from the two pixels ahead of the current
corner (right if the one ahead on the right is outside, straight if the one ahead on the left is,
else left; so at a saddle it turns right and diagonal pixels stay apart, as before). Loop starts are
found by scanning the pixels for a top edge on the outline, with one flag per pixel for a top edge
already walked. A mask of the wrong length now gives no loops instead of failing an assertion.
The output is identical: `the_walk_equals_the_stored_direction_walk` compares it with a test-only
copy of the previous walk on all 65,536 masks of 4 × 4 pixels and on 400 seeded 23 × 17 masks.
Time (best of 7, release build, 4 cores): the walk alone on 2000 × 2000 masks 19.1 ms vs 26.6 ms
(a smooth pattern), 81.3 vs 93.2 ms (12% random pixels), 223.1 vs 238.1 ms (50% random pixels);
whole traces of 1000 × 1000 images 73.1 vs 77.1 ms (Black and White), 249.6 vs 251.7 ms (Color, 6
colours) and 214.1 vs 218.6 ms (Color, 6 colours, Noise 1), with the same segment counts.
## Noise threshold stability (local development, 2026-10-14)

Noise must merge whole 4-connected regions, including pixels absorbed by an earlier merge.
A count of regions alone cannot establish this: one old region may split while others disappear.
The repeated-pass implementation at `a0671777` fails a partition regression at case 0, Noise 3.

The replacement discovers the initial regions, processes them in deterministic increasing-area
order, and keeps their membership current. All adjacent regions of the chosen colour join the
merge, with ties resolved by label and region id. Increasing Noise continues the same merge
sequence: every lower-threshold region remains wholly inside one higher-threshold region.
Regions exactly at the threshold stay; an opaque island surrounded by transparency stays;
transparent pixels are never recoloured. A merged region is tested at its current area, so a
1-pixel speck joining a 2-pixel region meets Noise 3 and is retained as one 3-pixel region.

Tests generate 64 multicolour 7 × 7 grids with transparent barriers and check every threshold
from 0 through 24 with an independent component traversal. They assert nested partitions,
non-increasing region counts and unchanged transparency. Separate cases check the strict
threshold, isolated opaque islands and invalid or overflowing grid dimensions. The existing
no-small-region and traced-path regressions remain active.

This uses region and heap bookkeeping instead of repeated full-image passes, so memory and
photo quality must also be checked. Local photo/scan validation uses fixed hashed inputs and
identical settings on unchanged current source and the candidate, including separate portrait
crops and white-composited PNG comparisons. These local fixtures are not repository assets.
The parity score is unchanged.

## Pieces returning to a junction
An outline piece can return to its starting junction while being fitted as an open chain. At loose
Corners/Paths settings, a nonzero positioned boundary could collapse to one cubic and lose a small
corner-touching mark. Fixed-end pieces with identical endpoints and fewer than two fitted segments
now retain their positioned boundary when its area is finite and nonzero. Fitting the shared piece
this way also gives an abutting fill exactly the reversed boundary, including within a compound path.
Six source-generated regressions check 1- and 2-pixel regions through four rotations, both windings
and large translations; fixed junctions; zero positioned area; free ends; Noise controls; and shared
edges through four rotations and black/white inversion. Noise 2 still removes the 1-pixel mark.
The white-hole Noise check is a control, not a reproduced returning-hole case. Defaults are unchanged;
these tests establish survival and edge consistency, not a new artistic-quality or parity score.
This is separate from the closed-contour recovery in #2012 and straightening guard in #2025.
## Thin closed outlines with Snap Curves To Lines

A four-pixel stair-step mark can fit as two straight cubics along the same diagonal, leaving a closed path with zero area. The outline-distance checks accept this because both sides are close to the chord. Closed fitting now checks analytic curve area after straightening and upright levelling; if a nondegenerate source loop has lost its interior, it retains the positioned boundary as an unsimplified polygon. The area integral is translated to a local origin to reduce cancellation. This numerical degeneracy check is not a new Noise or minimum-feature-area setting.

`fit::snap_area_tests` covers the mark at two positions and five Corners settings, a white stair-step hole, reversed/rotated closed boundaries with exactly matching opposite curves, and a narrow filled rectangle. Noise still removes the four-pixel mark or hole when set to 5. It does not change open-piece fitting, global Snap tolerances or defaults, and it does not address every possible zero-area compound outline. The preset quality table below is the previous measurement, not a rerun of that full report.

## Tiny closed contours
A coarse fit can reduce a small closed outline to one cubic, which the editable-path builder cannot
represent as a closed subpath with two anchors. Previously that dropped the component or hole after
it survived Noise. The fitter now retains the positioned contour without further simplification when
that minimum is not met. Corners and Noise defaults are unchanged.
Three source-generated regressions cover a one-pixel island, a one-pixel hole with opposite winding,
and a stepped seven-pixel region across Corners values. They also check that Noise still removes the
island and fills the hole when its threshold requests that. These are survival and winding checks,
not a new quality-harness baseline or a general claim about small-feature fidelity.
## How it is measured

`crates/trace/tests/quality` draws its own inputs from vector art (no image files), traces each with every
built-in preset, and measures the result:

```text
TRACE_QUALITY_REPORT=report.md cargo test --release -p vectorcraft-trace --test quality -- --ignored
```

**Inputs** (drawn anti-aliased at 128, 256 and 512 px, and at 256 px also blurred, with compression-like
noise, as a scan of ink on cream paper with uneven light and grain, and aliased: one hard sample per pixel, no
anti-aliasing):

| kind | inputs |
|:--|:--|
| 2026-10-15 | Fixed-end pieces returning to their junction retain their positioned nonzero boundary when fitted to fewer than two cubics; source-generated tests cover survival, winding, shared-edge equality, translations and Noise controls. Defaults and parity scores unchanged. |
| curved shapes | a circle; two ellipses; a rounded badge with a round hole; a letter D with its counter |
| polygons | a triangle, a turned square and a hexagon; a five-pointed star; a letter A with its counter |
| thin lines | five lines 0.5, 1, 2, 3 and 5 units wide (of a 256-unit square), a few degrees off the pixel grid |
| askew shapes | a rectangle, a plus sign and two lines, each 1 to 2 degrees off level and upright |
| plain shapes | a circle, a rectangle, a square, a rounded rectangle, an ellipse and a hexagon, each alone on white (measured from the Shapes change on, not at the baseline) |
| linear gradients | a two-stop gradient over the whole image at 25 degrees, and a three-stop gradient at 110 degrees in a disc on white: their lines and stops are known (measured from the Gradients change on, not at the baseline) |
| flat colour art | a disc of two halves in different colours that touch; a badge of four colours on white |
| gradient, photo | a smooth two-way gradient with a glow; a photo-like image (soft-edged shaded objects, texture, sensor noise) |

The letters are drawn by hand from lines and curves: the repository has no font to set them in.

**Columns**

| column | meaning |
|:--|:--|
| ΔE | the trace drawn again against the source: mean colour difference in Oklab × 100 (black to white is 100) |
| edge ΔE | the same, weighted by how strong an edge the source has at each pixel |
| off mean, off max | distance (px) from the traced outlines to the art's true outlines: wobble and staircase |
| missed max | largest distance (px) from a true outline to the nearest traced one: what was lost |
| paths, anchors | counts, the background's frame aside |
| × art | anchors per anchor point of the art itself (1.00 is as economical as the original) |
| lines % | share of the outline length made of straight segments (100 is right for polygons, 0 for a circle) |
| upright % | share of the outline length that is exactly level or upright |
| corners % | share of the art's sharp corners with a traced corner within 1.5 px |
| kinks | anchors where the outline turns by 10° or more away from any true corner |
| odd colours, odd px | paths (and their area) in a colour the art doesn't have: slivers along anti-aliased edges |
| gap px, overlap px | area no path covers, and area covered twice (abutting traces with a white background only) |
| specks | paths under 6 px of area |
| centre off, width off, anchors a stroke | stroked centre lines (Create: Strokes) against the thin lines they trace: mean distance (px) from the true line's centre line, mean error (px) of the stroke width, anchors per stroked path |
| shapes % | with Shapes on, the share of the plain shapes that came out as that shape (a shape, not a path, whose outline lies within 0.6 px of the true one) |
| false shapes | with Shapes on, paths made a shape whose outline strays more than 0.6 px from the art (a shape the art does not have, or one put where it is not) |
| grouped % | with Auto Grouping on, the share of the paths that were put inside another (the picture is painted as the app groups it for every other measure of that row: each path together with those inside it, in the order they were traced in; a ΔE equal to the row without the option says grouping changed nothing that shows) |
| gradient paths | paths filled with a linear gradient (on inputs that are flat colour, every one would be a gradient that is not there) |
| found %, angle off, ramp off | on the linear-gradient inputs: the share of them in which a gradient was found; and for those found, the largest angle (degrees) between the true gradient line and the traced one, and the largest difference (levels of a channel, 0 to 255) between the true colours and the traced gradient's at 17 points along the true line |
| outside px | how far the trace reaches outside the image: a curve that strays |

Rows named "…, enhanced" are that preset's enhanced version (Auto Grouping on; Shapes on in all but High
Fidelity Photo) on the same inputs as the row of the preset itself. Flat Logo has no enhanced version.

Black-and-white presets trace black: on the scanned variant their ΔE includes the paper's and ink's own
colours. Silhouettes has its threshold at 200, not 128: its outline lies where the image
crosses that tone, about 0.3 px outside the true edge on anti-aliased art and 0.8 px on blurred art; with
the threshold at 128 the same preset is 0.110 px off on its inputs (1.00 px at most), as the other
black-and-white presets are. `–` means the measure does not apply; `all` that nothing was traced.

## Baseline and now

Each preset on the inputs it is meant for, all sizes and variants.

### Baseline (before any change, main at `baf9693f`)

## 4. Yardstick

Inkscape 1.4.2's Trace Bitmap, run as a black box through its `object-trace` action (two scans, background
removed, its other settings as they come) on the same one-colour drawings, and its SVG output measured by
the same code. Compare with the black-and-white presets on the same kinds of input in section 2 and 3.

## Centre lines

Measured 2026-10-17 with maximal-disc pruning and junction merging, against base `3e44478f`.
Earlier preset and cost tables retain their previous measurements. Regenerate only this class:

```text
TRACE_QUALITY_CLASS=centre-lines TRACE_QUALITY_REPORT=centre-lines.md cargo test --release -p vectorcraft-trace --test quality quality_report -- --ignored --nocapture
```

Junction clusters use their deepest pixel and a disc radius of `distance − 0.5` px. Terminal
branches shorter than `r + max(2, 0.5 × min(2r, Stroke))` are pruned, shortest first. Tiny
self-loops inside the junction disc are removed; overlapping junctions and geometrically split
crossings merge, and runs join through degree-two nodes. Simplification is bounded to 32 rounds;
nodes and branches are each capped at 200,000. An over-budget blob stays with the fill path.
Whole-blob selection, ink refinement, cap detection and curve fitting retain their current rules.

Code-drawn scenes only: 23 scenes, each anti-aliased (8×8 coverage samples) and hard (that coverage thresholded at 0.5). Coordinates, widths and scene Stroke values are fixed; junction/letter/crossing coordinates include the 0.27/0.41 px offset. Create Fills and Strokes are on, Stroke is the scene's limit (13 px, mix 6 px, varying 12 px), Black and White threshold 128, Noise 4, Ignore White on, other settings at their defaults. Today's tracer has no minimum-length setting (the dashed scenes specify 0 for future use).

Distances use dense exact centre samples (≤0.25 px), emitted curves sampled at ≤0.5 px control-polygon steps, and nearest-point searches capped at 30 px. Found is the fraction of true samples within 1.5 px; width errors use output samples within 2 px of a true stroke. Samples inside exact fills are excluded. Topology is recovered from emitted subpath endpoints and intersections, merging coincident positions within 0.05 px; an endpoint contributes one arm, an interior two. Junction matching radius is local true width + 3 px; ends use half-width + 4 px. Each match is used once. Free ends exclude true junctions, corners, other strokes and fills; unmatched emitted ends are spurs. Junctions/ends within 2 px of fills are excluded. End error is distance, with signed error along the outward tangent in parentheses. Coverage is a union of painted output at pixel centres (0.02 px flattening tolerance, actual emitted caps), compared with the exact swept shape at pixel centres, for both input variants. Area error is signed relative to exact area. Anchors counts stroke anchors, including all compound subpaths; paths counts stroked + filled paths. Time covers tracing only, one scene at a time. Profile-dependent columns are unavailable (–).

The graph stage does not reconnect separate blobs. Raw graph tests cover straight lines at 24
angles, junctions and 20–90° crossings; these do not replace the emitted-path measurements above.
The remaining spur/extra-junction target is not met by this graph-only change.

### Localization parity

# Localization parity

> **Last reviewed:** 2026-10-10 · **Last updated:** 2026-10-23 · **Change:** patch (missing translations never fail; `cargo xtask ci` prints the untranslated report)

Per-language status of VectorCraft's interface. How the catalogs work and how to add a language:
[`development.md` › Localisation](development.md#localisation). Part of
[target-app-parity.md](target-app-parity.md).

**How it is measured:** rows with a translation in each `crates/ui-egui/src/i18n/<code>.tsv`, counted on
origin/main `01e165af`, except the rows that give a count date, which were counted on `main` at `cb0a7d9` (2026-10-21).
The reference is the French catalog, which was complete when counted: 3,416 interface
strings (menus, command labels, `tl!` literals: panels, dialogs, tooltips, Preferences) plus 604 `@msg` status and
error messages, 4,020 in all. A language's % is its rows over 4,020 (capped at 100% per part). A missing
translation never fails a test or a build: the interface shows the English text until a translator adds the row.
`cargo xtask ci` prints the untranslated report (`cargo xtask i18n-report` alone), which lists per language the
strings missing from each catalog with the `complete_menus` flag and the messages missing from each language in
the `COMPLETE_MESSAGES` list. Every non-English language marked "full" has the flag, and all of them except
Bulgarian, Danish, Indonesian and Dutch are in the list. No language has help content: there is no translated (or
English) in-app help, and the docs are English.

**Native review:** every catalog was written clean-room from the English meaning, most of it by agents
(`bflatastic`), with community contributors adding or correcting (German by `dwetscher`, Japanese and Traditional
Chinese by `imachus`). Only Georgian is recorded as reviewed by a native speaker; the other catalog headers ask for one.

## The twelve key languages

| Language | Code | UI strings translated | Dialogs / tooltips / messages | Script support | Native review | Status | To `full` (h) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

**12-language score: ~82%** (equal weights: 100 + 85 + 100 + 0 + 0 + 100 + 100 + 100 + 100 + 98 + 100 + 100, over 12).
**To `full` for all twelve: ~50–85 h**, most of it Arabic (right-to-left interface) and Hindi (interface
shaping). Each new Latin-script catalog is ~4,000 rows; the existing ones were written in a few agent hours each
plus review. Native-speaker review is human work and isn't in the hours.

Twenty-three non-English catalogs in all. Illustrator, as its public documentation lists, ships around two dozen
interface languages (including Polish, Dutch, Turkish, the Nordic languages, Hungarian, and Middle East
editions with Arabic and Hebrew); it doesn't ship Hindi, Indonesian or Vietnamese.

## Czech render-site follow-up

The desktop and web file pickers look up filter labels at assignment time; format names and
extensions stay unchanged. Diagnostics retain numeric values and units. New Document's suggested
preset name uses `Preset {number}`. Contributor tooltips use named placeholders and Czech plurals;
handles and chosen names remain unchanged. Gradient descriptions reuse `{kind} Gradient` with a
contextual radial adjective. PDF/Print mark styles use `mark-style`, so `Japanese` displays as
`Japonské` while the language name stays `Japonština`; their Summary uses the same context.

The search placeholder, Home screen, toolbar/panel tooltips and Preferences already use lookups.
No new `tl!("literal")` keys were needed: only `cs.tsv` adds 19 AI-draft rows and revises the gradient
template. Every other complete catalog (`complete_menus`) has the same rows and a `Roman` row for the
other mark style; the untranslated report lists a catalog that lacks one of them.
Native review is still needed, and catalog coverage does not prove that every variable in the UI is
translated.

## Not done in any language

Locale-aware number and date formats, a right-to-left interface, translated help, and a Traditional Chinese UI
font for the web build.

### VectorCraft MCP server

# VectorCraft MCP server

`vectorcraft-cli mcp` runs a [Model Context Protocol](https://tech.zhushou.pro/sitemap.xml) server on stdio
(newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0; see [Protocol](#protocol) for version negotiation). Agents use it to
draw, inspect and look at VectorCraft documents.

It has two backends:

| Mode | How | What works |
|---|---|---|
| **Remote** | `vectorcraft-cli mcp --connect 127.0.0.1:7979` (the app must run with `vectorcraft --control 7979`) | Everything. Tool calls are forwarded over the [control protocol](control-protocol.md), so you watch the app change live. |
| **Headless** | `vectorcraft-cli mcp --headless` | An in-process engine session with a CPU renderer. Everything except the UI-only tools (`inspect_ui` or `ui_inspect`, `type_text`, `answer_dialog`, `open_panel`, `screenshot {window:true}` or `ui_screenshot`). |

With no flag, the server tries `127.0.0.1:7979` and falls back to headless. Logs go to stderr; stdout carries
only protocol messages.

## Install and register

From the repository root, with Rust 1.95+ and the platform's source-build prerequisites installed:

```sh
cargo install --path apps/vectorcraft-cli --locked
# POSIX shells, for Cargo's default install location:
export PATH="${CARGO_HOME:-$HOME/.cargo}/bin:$PATH"
vectorcraft-cli --help
claude mcp add vectorcraft -- vectorcraft-cli mcp
# or pin a mode:
claude mcp add vectorcraft-headless -- vectorcraft-cli mcp --headless
claude mcp add vectorcraft-app -- vectorcraft-cli mcp --connect 127.0.0.1:7979
```

Cargo installs a binary, not a symlink into `target/`, so it survives `cargo clean`.
Re-run the install command after updating the checkout.
By default the executable goes in `$CARGO_HOME/bin` (`~/.cargo/bin` when unset), or
`%USERPROFILE%\.cargo\bin` on Windows. If you set `--root`, `CARGO_INSTALL_ROOT`, or
Cargo's `install.root`, use that installation root's `bin` directory instead. Add it
to the `PATH` inherited by the MCP client, not just an interactive shell, and restart
the client after changing its environment. Installing does not start or register a server.

Other clients use the same command in their JSON config:

```json
{"mcpServers": {"vectorcraft": {"command": "vectorcraft-cli", "args": ["mcp"]}}}
```

If a client reports `ENOENT` or "Executable not found in $PATH", verify the install with
`command -v vectorcraft-cli` (PowerShell: `Get-Command vectorcraft-cli`) in the client's
environment. If that environment cannot be changed, set JSON `command` to the absolute
installed binary path, not a literal `~` or `$HOME` expression. Avoid symlinks into
`target/release`: cleaning the build directory breaks them. A source build alone does
not put the CLI on `PATH`.

For a live session, start the app first: `cargo run --release -p vectorcraft -- --control 7979`.

### From an installed release

The release packages ship `vectorcraft-cli` alongside the desktop app, so no build is needed:

| Install | CLI |
|---|---|
| Windows (MSI) | `C:\Program Files\VectorCraft\vectorcraft-cli.exe` by default (wherever you installed it otherwise), not on `PATH` |
| Linux (deb, rpm) | `/usr/bin/vectorcraft-cli` |
| macOS | the separate `vectorcraft-cli-<version>-macos-<arch>.zip` release asset (the `.app` holds only the desktop app) |

```sh
# Windows, default install folder
claude mcp add vectorcraft -- "C:\Program Files\VectorCraft\vectorcraft-cli.exe" mcp
# Linux, or macOS with the CLI unzipped onto PATH
claude mcp add vectorcraft -- vectorcraft-cli mcp
```

For a live session, start the installed app with the control port before the MCP client starts the server:

```sh
# macOS: quit VectorCraft first, since `open -a` passes no arguments to an app that is already running
open -a VectorCraft --args --control 7979
# Windows (PowerShell), default install folder
& "C:\Program Files\VectorCraft\vectorcraft.exe" --control 7979
# Linux (deb, rpm)
vectorcraft --control 7979
```

The Dock, Start menu and desktop launchers start the app without `--control`, so the app opens no control
port unless `VECTORCRAFT_CONTROL_PORT` is set. `vectorcraft-cli mcp` with no flag tries `127.0.0.1:7979`
once, when it starts: a server that started before the app stays headless until the MCP client restarts
it. `open -a` and PowerShell's `&` return before the app opens the port, so wait until the VectorCraft
window is open before you start the MCP client. With `--connect`, a server that finds no app stops and
prints `vectorcraft-cli: cannot connect to 127.0.0.1:7979: ` followed by the system's connection error, for
example `connection timed out`.

## Confining file access

```sh
vectorcraft-cli mcp --automation-read-root /work/project --automation-write-root /work/project/out
vectorcraft-cli mcp --automation-read-root /work/project --automation-read-root /work/shared-assets \
  --automation-write-root /work/project/out --automation-write-root /tmp/scratch
```

```json
{"mcpServers": {"vectorcraft": {"command": "vectorcraft-cli",
  "args": ["mcp", "--automation-read-root", "/work/project", "--automation-write-root", "/work/project/out"]}}}
```

The two flags (PhotoCraft and the other Craft apps take the same ones, so one client config works across
the suite) keep the agent to the folders you give it:

- Every file a command reads must lie inside a **read root**: `open_file`, `file.place`, relinking and
  updating links, the images an SVG links to, swatch library, graphic style library, symbol library, brush library and colour-profile loads, plug-ins,
  `file.newFromTemplate`, preset imports, shortcut sets (`shortcutSet.read`), the folders `text.findFontFiles` and `links.findFiles` search, the
  scripts `script.check` reads and the files they include.
- Every file a command writes must lie inside a **write root**: `save_file`, `export`, the save and
  export commands, Export for Screens, Package, Export for Web, print to file, `screenshot {path}`,
  library and preset saves to a path, the copies `links.relink {copy}` makes.
- `file.list {path}` (through `run_command`) lists a folder's files and folders, held to the read roots like any read, so an agent can see what it was given (#1163).
- Each flag may be given more than once (#3546): a path inside any of the read roots may be read, one inside any
  of the write roots written, so one session can read a project folder and a shared assets folder, or write to an
  output folder and a scratch folder, without widening a root to their common parent. A folder given twice
  counts once.
- Read and write access are separate. Give the same folder to both flags for both; a kind left out grants none
  of its access (with only `--automation-read-root`, nothing can be written to disk, though `export` and
  the save commands without a path still return the bytes). Without either flag nothing changes.
- A path is made absolute against the server's working directory, then its links are followed: a file
  (or folder) link that leads out of a root is outside it. For a file that doesn't exist yet, its nearest
  existing folder's links are followed and the rest must be plain names, so `..` below a folder that
  doesn't exist is refused, as is a link that leads nowhere (writing through it would create its target).
  The result is compared with the root by whole folder names: `/work2/x` is not inside `/work`. On
  Windows case is ignored, UNC paths (`\\server\share\…`) are resolved like drive-letter ones, and
  device names (`CON`, `NUL`, `COM1`…) are refused.
- With `--connect`, the server makes the paths of `open_file`, `save_file`, `export` (`path` or
  `options.path`) and `screenshot {path}` absolute against its own working directory before it sends
  them to the app. Paths inside `run_command` and `command_batch` params go to the app as given, and the
  app resolves them against its own working directory.
- A refused path is an ordinary tool error the agent can read and correct, for example
  `automation path rejected: outside the write root /work/project/out: /etc/x.png` (with several,
  `outside the write roots /work/project/out, /tmp/scratch: …`) or
  `automation filesystem access is not granted: write authority is absent: /work/project/out/x.png`.
  Links in an opened document that point outside the read roots show as missing.
- The preferences that move folders the app reads or writes on its own (`fontsFolder`,
  `pluginsFolder`, `recoveryFolder`, `templatesFolder`) can only be set inside the roots. The app's own folders
  (preferences, Data Recovery, the User Defined library folders, VectorCraft's Fonts folder) are not
  confined: no agent names a path there.
- The roots must be existing folders; a missing one stops the server with an error. Each flag takes one
  folder per use (`--flag <dir>` or `--flag=<dir>`) and may be used again for more.

The flags confine the headless server and imply `--headless`; `--connect` with them is an error, since
the server would otherwise talk to an app that isn't confined. A running app confines itself: start it
with the same flags, `vectorcraft --control 7979 --automation-read-root <dir> --automation-write-root
<dir>`, and connect as usual (see [Control protocol](control-protocol.md#confining-file-access)). The
server then writes nothing itself: `screenshot {path}` asks the app to write the file.

The checks hold for every thread of the server process. A path is checked, then opened: another program
that swaps a link in between can still win that race, so the roots keep an agent to the files it was
given rather than guarding against other software on the computer.

## Protocol

Newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 on stdio. The revision is **`2025-06-18`**; `2025-03-26` and `2024-11-05` are
accepted too. Every request and notification must carry `"jsonrpc": "2.0"`: anything else is
refused with `-32600` (requests) or ignored (notifications, which have no id to address a reply
to) before it is dispatched. When a tool call reaches a running app, it is one control-channel
request, and the app echoes its `id` in the reply: a reply with any other `id` is rejected, the
connection dropped, and the next call starts a fresh one — the call reports uncertainty like any
reply that never arrived whole. A malformed JSON reply also drops the connection and reports that
uncertainty; the failed operation is never replayed automatically. The app's refusals carry no `id`
(a connection past its 16, a line it would not read): the call reports the app's reason and says nothing was run. Before each call the
server checks that the app still holds the connection and opens a new one when it doesn't (the app
closes a connection left idle for 5 minutes, and a restarted app is a new one), so a request is
never written to a closed socket; when the app can't be reached, the call says that nothing was
sent. Clients requesting `2026-07-28` through `initialize`, or through a request's
`_meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion"]`, receive `resultType: "complete"`,
`ttlMs` and `cacheScope: "private"` on tool/resource/template/prompt lists and resource/prompt reads.
List TTL is 600000 ms; live reads use zero. Older clients keep the original response shapes.
This does not add streaming or input requests — see [Not implemented](#not-implemented).

One message is one line of at most 16 MiB: a longer line is answered with `-32600` and skipped,
and the server keeps serving what follows. A batch holds at most 64 messages. `command_batch`
holds at most 256 steps, and the step results it keeps (for later steps' `"$N.path"` references
and the reply) total at most 8 MiB — past that the batch stops with the reason, closing its atomic
undo group as usual. Replies from a connected app are refused past 256 MiB and the connection
dropped; the call reports uncertainty like any reply that never arrived whole.

`initialize` advertises:

| Capability | What it covers |
|---|---|
| `tools` | The tools below |
| `resources` | Three fixed resources and four templates |
| `prompts` | Five ready-made workflows |
| `completions` | `completion/complete` for prompt arguments and template variables |
| `logging` | `logging/setLevel` and `notifications/message` |

### Prompts

`prompts/list` offers five workflows; `prompts/get` returns one templated user message with its
arguments filled in. A missing required argument is `-32602`.

| Prompt | Arguments (required first) |
|---|---|
| `poster` | `brief`, `palette`, `text` |
| `icon-set` | `subject`, `count`, `detail` |
| `recolor` | `palette`, `method` |
| `trace-and-style` | `path`, `preset`, `effect` |
| `export-set` | `formats`, `directory`, `scale` |

```sh
echo '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"prompts/get","params":{"name":"poster","arguments":{"brief":"a jazz festival"}}}' \
  | vectorcraft-cli mcp --headless
```

### Resource templates

`vectorcraft://document` (summary), `vectorcraft://document/json` (the whole model), and
`vectorcraft://commands` (the live command catalog with enabled state) are the fixed resources. The templates read one thing at a time, which matters on a real document: the full model
is thousands of lines an agent pays for again on every change.

| `uriTemplate` | Reads |
|---|---|
| `vectorcraft://object/{id}` | One layer or object with its children, bounds and paint: `document.node {id, summary: true}`, the node as `document.inspect` lists it. A large container can be sliced with `run_command document.node {id, summary: true, depth?, childLimit?}` (a level that shows fewer children reports `childCount`) |
| `vectorcraft://command/{id}` | One command: label, menu path, shortcut, parameter description, enablement |
| `vectorcraft://effect/{id}` | One live effect with its parameters and defaults |
| `vectorcraft://swatch/{name}` | One swatch, colour, gradient or pattern swatch (percent-encode spaces) |

An unknown URI is `-32002`; a template with no value, or a value that names nothing, is `-32602`.

The same reads work as query commands through `run_command`: `document.node {id}` returns the object's full model
JSON (geometry, appearance, every attribute) and `document.node {id, summary: true}` the compact summary
`document.inspect` gives for it (id, name, kind, bounds, paint labels, children), without summarizing the whole
document. A summary read slices a large container: `depth` is how many child levels it includes (`0`: the node
alone) and `childLimit` how many children each node shows, top of the stack first (both default to all). A level
that shows fewer children than it has reports their total as `childCount`, so truncation is never silent; with
nothing truncated the reply is the plain summary. Both must be non-negative integers and need `summary: true`
(the full object JSON is never truncated); anything else is an error.

In the summary an object reports its paint as `fill`, `stroke` (labels) and `strokeWidth`. So does a compound path,
whose paint is its own: its member paths report `compoundMember: true` instead of a paint they don't have. Every
node (layers and groups too) reports its opacity when it is below 1, in both scales: `opacity` is the 0–1 fraction
the document stores and `opacityPct` the 0–100 % that `object.setProps`, `transparency.set`, `draw_path` and
`draw_shape` take (so an agent passes `opacityPct` back, never `opacity`); and `blend` when it isn't Normal, as
the label `object.setProps {blend}` takes (`"Multiply"`, `"Color Burn"`).

On a large document, drill instead of dumping: `inspect_document {depth: 0}` (or `run_command document.inspect
{depth?, childLimit?}`, same rules) is the skeleton (artboards with top layers and counts), `run_command
document.find {name?, kind?, text?, within?, intersects?, minArea?, …, select?, limit?}` locates nodes across the
whole tree, and `document.node` reads the
interesting ones sliced. `document.inspect` and the `doc_inspect` / `inspect_document` tools also scope the
reply themselves: `ids: [id…]` lists just those nodes (any level, in the order given, an unknown id is an error,
at most 10000), `kind` lists every node of one panel label (ignoring case; within the subtrees of `ids` when both
are given) with its ancestor `path`, and `limit` / `offset` page the list. A scoped reply carries the nodes as
`nodes` instead of `layers` (each the summary the full tree gives it, sliced by `depth` / `childLimit`) plus
`total`, the entries before paging; artboards, selection and history stay whole. `limit` / `offset` alone page the
top layers (`layers` and `total`). Without these options the reply is the whole layer tree as before.
`document.find` needs at least one filter and all given filters must match; matching
ignores case, `name` is a substring of the Layers panel name, `text` a substring of type content and `kind` the
exact panel label (`Layer`, `Group`, `Clip Group`, `Path`, `Compound Path`, `Type`, `Image`, `Rectangle`, ...).
The geometric filters read each object's geometric bounds, in the document points `document.inspect` reports
(groups included; layers, sublayers and a node without bounds do not match): `within: [x, y, width, height]` keeps
objects inside that rectangle (edges included), `intersects: [x, y, width, height]` objects touching or overlapping it,
`minWidth` / `maxWidth` and `minHeight` / `maxHeight` limit the bounds' size, `minThickness` / `maxThickness`
the smaller of width and height (thin slivers of either orientation), and `minArea` / `maxArea` width × height.
`minAnchors` / `maxAnchors` count a path's anchor points, a compound path's members together; other nodes do not
match them. Limits are inclusive, not negative, and a minimum above its maximum is an error. `select: true`
also selects the matches, leaving out hidden and locked ones, those inside another match, and a compound path's
members unless the compound path is isolated; Select › Reselect repeats the find, and an action being recorded
records it as a step (a find without `select` is not recorded). For example,
`document.find {maxThickness: 1, kind: "path", select: true}` followed by `edit.clear` deletes hairline slivers.
It answers `{matches: [{id, name, kind, path}], total}` top of the stack first, where `path` is the ancestor
chain (layer first) and `limit` caps `matches` (default 100; `0` only counts); with `select` the reply adds
`selected`, the number of objects selected. `document.json` stays whole: it is the fidelity path, not the way to
look around.

### Completions

`completion/complete` answers for a prompt argument (`ref/prompt`) or a template variable
(`ref/resource`), ranked by prefix and then by substring, capped at 100 values with `total` and
`hasMore`. The values are read from the live catalogues, so they follow the app: `formats` suggests
what the engine writes, `preset` the Image Trace presets, `effect` the effect ids, `{id}` the layer
and object ids in the document, `{name}` its swatch names. An unknown reference comes back empty
rather than as an error, since a completion is asked for mid-typing.

### Logging

`logging/setLevel` accepts any RFC 5424 severity — `debug`, `info`, `notice`, `warning`, `error`,
`critical`, `alert`, `emergency` — and an unknown one is `-32602` with the previous level left in
place. From then on the engine's own `log` records arrive as `notifications/message` with `level`,
`logger` and `data`. A `null` level turns it back off. Nothing is sent before the client asks, and
records queued at the old level are dropped rather than replayed at the new one.

Installing the logger that receives those records is `vectorcraft-cli`'s job, not the library's: a
crate that installed one would override whatever logger an embedder had already set up. Embedding
`vectorcraft-mcp` directly means calling `vectorcraft_mcp::logging::install()` yourself if you want
log records to reach your client.

### Long calls: cancellation, progress and a busy engine

A call runs to the end before its reply, and the engine runs one call at a time, in the order the
lines arrived. A thread of its own reads the stream meanwhile, so the server still hears the client
while an export runs (#2165, #2171, #2172):

- **Cancellation.** `notifications/cancelled {requestId}`
  ([spec](https://cdll.wtpuscm.cn/yingyong/rating-027550.html))
  takes a request out of the queue, or stops the one that is running, and **that request gets no
  reply**. A running export, flatten, bake or render notices at its next checkpoint (between pages
  and artboards, between flattened groups, while drawing objects), returns, and writes nothing: the
  document is exactly as it was and the engine is free for the next call. An unknown, finished or
