### Releasing VectorCraft

# Releasing VectorCraft

> **Last updated:** 2026-10-12 · **Change:** minor (RPM runtime capabilities and metadata checks, #1275)

Every push to the `release` branch runs `.github/workflows/release.yml`. The workflow builds
installers for macOS, Windows, Linux (including Flatpak bundles and a RISC-V tarball) and FreeBSD, plus the web build, and creates or updates a
**draft** GitHub Release named `VectorCraft v<version>`. Nobody sees a draft until a maintainer
publishes it.

User-facing names say **VectorCraft**. Files, binaries and ids stay lowercase
(`vectorcraft-<version>-<platform>-<arch>.<ext>`, `ai.storyteller.vectorcraft`).

## Cutting a release

1. **Bump the version** on `main`. It lives in exactly one place, `[workspace.package] version`
   in the root `Cargo.toml`; every crate inherits it and the packaging scripts read it from there:

   ```sh
   cargo xtask version                 # prints the current version, e.g. 0.3.1
   cargo xtask version set 0.4.0       # or 0.4.0-rc.1; updates Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock
   ```

   Commit the change (`Cargo.toml` + `Cargo.lock`) through the normal review flow, as a
   `Release: VectorCraft v0.4.0` commit whose message says what changed for users.
2. **Merge `main` into `release`** (or fast-forward it) and push. The workflow starts by itself.
3. **Wait for the draft.** When every job is done (macOS notarization is the slow part), the
   Releases page has a draft `VectorCraft v0.4.0`, targeting the pushed commit, with every
   artifact and `SHA256SUMS.txt`. The notes are generated from the merged pull requests.
4. **Check it.** Download an installer or two and read the job summaries. A `::warning::` there
   means a signing secret was missing and that artifact is unsigned.
5. **Publish** the draft in the GitHub UI. Publishing creates the `v0.4.0` tag. A version with a
   pre-release suffix (`-rc.1`) is marked as a pre-release.

Pushing to `release` again before you publish rebuilds the same draft and replaces its assets.
Once the draft is published, the workflow refuses to touch that version again: bump it first.

**Test runs:** *Actions › Release › Run workflow* runs the whole pipeline by hand. The optional
`version` input (such as `0.4.0-rc.1`) overrides `Cargo.toml` for that run only; each build job
applies it with `cargo xtask version set` before building. The signing jobs (macOS, Windows) and
the draft-release job run in the `release` environment, which only the `release` branch can use, so
pick that branch for a full run. Run on any other branch, it is a dry run: the Linux, Flatpak,
FreeBSD and web jobs build and upload their artifacts, the environment refuses the signing jobs,
and no draft release is created.

## What gets built

| Platform | Artifacts | Built on |
|---|---|---|
| macOS 11+ (universal: Apple silicon and Intel) | `vectorcraft-<v>-macos-universal.dmg`, `vectorcraft-cli-<v>-macos-universal.zip` | `macos-15` |
| Windows x64 | `vectorcraft-<v>-windows-x64.msi`, `vectorcraft-<v>-windows-x64-portable.zip` | `windows-latest` |
| Windows x86 (32-bit) | `vectorcraft-<v>-windows-x86.msi`, `vectorcraft-<v>-windows-x86-portable.zip` | `windows-latest` |
| Windows on ARM64 | `vectorcraft-<v>-windows-arm64.msi`, `vectorcraft-<v>-windows-arm64-portable.zip` | `windows-latest` (cross-compiled) |
| Linux x86_64 | `vectorcraft-<v>-linux-x86_64.{AppImage,deb,rpm,tar.gz}` | `ubuntu-22.04` |
| Linux aarch64 | `vectorcraft-<v>-linux-aarch64.{AppImage,deb,rpm,tar.gz}` | `ubuntu-22.04-arm` |
| Linux riscv64 | `vectorcraft-<v>-linux-riscv64.tar.gz` (cross-compiled, glibc >= 2.39; CLI smoke-tested under QEMU) | `ubuntu-24.04` |
| Linux AppImage updates | `vectorcraft-<v>-linux-{x86_64,aarch64}.AppImage.zsync` | with the AppImages |
| Flatpak x86_64, aarch64 | `vectorcraft-<v>-linux-{x86_64,aarch64}.flatpak` | `ubuntu-24.04`, `ubuntu-24.04-arm` (repackages the Linux tarball) |
| FreeBSD 14 x86_64 | `vectorcraft-<v>-freebsd-x86_64.tar.gz` | a FreeBSD 14.3 VM on `ubuntu-latest` |
| Web | `vectorcraft-web-<v>.zip`, a static site (see [`packaging/web/README.md`](../packaging/web/README.md)) | `ubuntu-latest` |

`vectorcraft --version` and `vectorcraft-cli --version` print the version from `Cargo.toml`.

**Fonts.** Every build job checks out [craft-fonts](https://tlkg.yx-sf.com/peixun/software-06471762.html) at a
pinned commit (the `ref:` of its craft-fonts checkout step) and builds with `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR` and
`CRAFT_FONTS_REQUIRED=1`, so releases embed its Japanese fonts and fail rather than ship without
them (the web build embeds only the UI font, BIZ UDPGothic Regular, to stay small). The packages carry each embedded font's licence as `OFL-<family>.txt`
(`copy_font_licences` in `packaging/env.sh`). Bump the pins deliberately, in every job at once.
The rules are in craftrules `standards/fonts.md`, the build option in
[`docs/development.md`](development.md) › Fonts.

### macOS

`packaging/macos/package.sh` builds `aarch64-apple-darwin` and `x86_64-apple-darwin` with
`MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=11.0`, joins them with `lipo` and assembles `VectorCraft.app`:

- `Info.plist` is generated from `Info.plist.in` (bundle id `ai.storyteller.vectorcraft`,
  `LSMinimumSystemVersion` 11.0, the version and the build commit). The icon is
  `assets/app-icon/vectorcraft.icns`. `cargo xtask bundle` fills in the same template for its
  development app.
- **Document types:** `Info.plist.in` declares every format File › Open reads, so Finder opens
  them with VectorCraft (double-click, Open With, a drop on the Dock icon). VectorCraft owns its own
  formats and is an alternate for the others. A test keeps the list in step with the engine's
  `OPEN_EXTS`. AppKit hands the files to the app as open-document events, which
  `apps/vectorcraft/src/open_documents.rs` opens like files named on the command line.
- **Signing** goes inside-out with the hardened runtime and a secure timestamp: the executable
  first, then the bundle, with no `--deep` on the final signature. The entitlements
  (`entitlements.plist`) are deliberately empty.
- **Notarization:** the app is zipped and sent with `xcrun notarytool submit --wait`, then the
  ticket is stapled and checked with `stapler validate` and `spctl`. The app goes on a DMG
  (`hdiutil create -srcfolder`, retried when a CI runner's device is busy, with an `Applications` link
  to drag onto), which is signed, notarized and stapled too; the app mounted from it must pass
  `codesign --verify --strict --deep` (#1085). Its Finder window (background, icon size and positions) comes from
  [`packaging/macos/dmg/`](../packaging/macos/dmg/README.md), and its volume is named `VectorCraft`
  without the version, which the window's background needs; the DMG file name keeps the version.
- **CLI:** the universal `vectorcraft-cli` is signed the same way, zipped, and the zip is
  notarized. A bare executable can't hold a stapled ticket, so Gatekeeper looks the CLI's ticket up
  online the first time a downloaded copy runs.

Locally, without certificates, the script signs ad hoc (`codesign -s -`) and skips notarization,
which is enough to check the bundle and the DMG on your own Mac:

```sh
packaging/macos/package.sh --arch universal   # needs both rustup targets
packaging/macos/package.sh --arch aarch64     # quicker, host only
```

### Windows

`packaging/windows/package.ps1 -Arch x64|x86|arm64` builds with `-C target-feature=+crt-static`,
so neither the MSI nor the portable zip needs the Visual C++ redistributable. The flag is scoped
to the target triple, so host build scripts aren't affected.

- Before packaging, the script checks each binary's PE machine type against `-Arch` (an x64 build
  can never ship labelled arm64), that `vectorcraft.exe` is a GUI program (no console window) and
  that `vectorcraft-cli.exe` is a console program.
- **Portable zip:** it ships `packaging/windows/portable.txt` beside `vectorcraft.exe`. That
  marker (or a `VectorCraft.portable` file) switches on portable mode, as in PhotoCraft: `ui.json`
  and the folders next to it (Swatches, Graphic Styles, Fonts, Data Recovery, logs…) go to
  `VectorCraftData\` next to the exe instead of `%APPDATA%\VectorCraft`. The first time
  `VectorCraftData` is created, the settings already in `%APPDATA%\VectorCraft` are copied into it
  (the originals stay), so someone updating a portable zip from before the marker keeps their
  settings. If that folder isn't writable the app logs a warning and uses `%APPDATA%`. Deleting
  `portable.txt` returns settings to the user profile (the `VectorCraftData` folder is left as it
  is). The MSI has no marker. `VECTORCRAFT_CONFIG_DIR` still wins, `VECTORCRAFT_NO_PREFS` never
  looks for the marker, and a portable copy skips the one-time read of the old DrawCraft settings.
  The logic is in `apps/vectorcraft/src/profile.rs`. On the other platforms the marker goes where
  the user sees the app, never inside it: on macOS next to `VectorCraft.app` (nothing is written
  inside the signed bundle), for an AppImage next to the `.AppImage` file (`$APPIMAGE`; the mounted
  executable's own folder is read-only). Flatpak isn't supported: `/app` is read-only and the
  sandbox has no folder "beside the app", so a Flatpak install always uses its own config folder.
- `vectorcraft.wxs` (WiX) is a per-machine install into Program Files with a Start Menu shortcut
  and an App Paths entry (Win+R `vectorcraft`). Same-version upgrades are allowed, so release
  candidates replace each other.
- Double-clicking the MSI opens a setup wizard (WixUI_InstallDir without the licence page):
  Welcome, install folder (remembered for upgrades in `HKLM\Software\VectorCraft\InstallDir`),
  Shortcuts (a ticked "Create a desktop shortcut" box), Ready, a progress page, and a Finish page
  that says where to find the app, with a ticked "Launch VectorCraft" box. The pages name the full
  version (`vectorcraft.en-us.wxl`). `package.ps1` draws the wizard's banner and side bitmaps from
  the app icon, so no WiX stock art ships. `msiexec /qn` still installs silently, with the desktop
  shortcut unless `INSTALLDESKTOPSHORTCUT=""` is passed. Building needs the WiX UI and Util
  extensions: `wix extension add -g WixToolset.UI.wixext/5.0.2 WixToolset.Util.wixext/5.0.2`.
- The ARM64 build is cross-compiled on the x64 runner. `.github/workflows/windows-arm64.yml`
  installs that MSI on a Windows 11 ARM64 runner, checks that both installed programs are ARM64,
  runs `vectorcraft-cli --version` natively and uninstalls.
- **Signing:** `packaging/windows/sign.ps1` signs both `.exe` files and then the `.msi` with
  `signtool` (SHA-256, RFC 3161 timestamp), using whichever material is present:
  1. a `.pfx` certificate (`WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE`, base64, and `WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD`), or
  2. Azure Trusted Signing (`AZURE_TENANT_ID`, `AZURE_CLIENT_ID`, `AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET`,
     `AZURE_SIGNING_ENDPOINT`, `AZURE_SIGNING_ACCOUNT`, `AZURE_CERT_PROFILE`).

  With neither, it warns and leaves the files unsigned, so test builds still produce installers.
  It is the one place to adapt when the signing setup changes; `WINDOWS_TIMESTAMP_URL` and
  `SIGNTOOL` override the timestamp server and the `signtool.exe` path.

### Linux

`packaging/linux/package.sh` builds the release binaries and packages them as an AppImage, a
`.deb` and an `.rpm` (with [nfpm](https://tech.ai-hao123.com), from `nfpm.yaml`) and a plain
`.tar.gz` tree (`bin/`, `share/`). The packages install both programs, the desktop entry, the
AppStream metainfo, the MIME type for VectorCraft documents, the icons and the licence files.

**Document types.** The desktop entry's `MimeType` lists every format File › Open reads but PSD,
PSB, `.ps` PostScript and Targa, so file managers list VectorCraft under Open With for them.
`ai.storyteller.vectorcraft.mime.xml` declares the types that shared-mime-info lacks: VectorCraft
documents and templates, `.ait` templates and Affinity files (`application/x-affinity`). An `.af`
file gets the Affinity type by its content, and `.afdesign` and `.afpub` files by their extension.
A test keeps both files in step with the engine's `OPEN_EXTS`.

The jobs run on `ubuntu-22.04`, the oldest GitHub-hosted image, so the binaries only need
glibc 2.35 or newer: Ubuntu 22.04+, Debian 12+, Fedora 36+ and RHEL 10. Moving the job to a newer
image raises that floor, so do it deliberately. After packaging, the job prints the `.deb`'s
metadata and contents, runs `ldd` on the binary and runs each AppImage with `--version`.

**RPM dependencies.** The x86_64 and aarch64 RPMs require 64-bit shared-library
capabilities rather than distribution-specific package names: `libc`, libm's `GLIBC_2.35`,
`libgcc_s`, `libxkbcommon`, and either Vulkan or EGL. Windowing and GPU
libraries are loaded at runtime, so `ldd` alone does not list every requirement.
The glibc capability enforces the same floor as the `.deb`; a distribution with
an older glibc is not supported by these binaries. It names libm, whose `hypot` and `hypotf`
are the binaries' GLIBC_2.35 symbols: RHEL 9's glibc 2.34 provides `libc.so.6(GLIBC_2.35)`
through backports, so a libc capability let it install binaries that can't start. Weak
recommendations still use package names and do not block installation.

Before publishing a Linux release:

- [ ] Check `rpm -qp --requires` on both architectures for the runtime capabilities
  above, including the Vulkan/EGL alternative and glibc floor.
- [ ] Install and start the package on the target RPM distributions. Synthetic
  provider tests verify metadata resolution, not a real desktop installation.

**RISC-V.** The `linux-riscv64` job cross-compiles `riscv64gc-unknown-linux-gnu` on `ubuntu-24.04`
against riscv64 libraries from ports.ubuntu.com (so the floor there is glibc 2.39) and runs
`package.sh --formats tar` with `CROSS_ARCH`, `CROSS_TARGET`, `CROSS_COMPILE` and
`EMULATOR=qemu-riscv64` set: a `.tar.gz` only, with `vectorcraft-cli --version` run under QEMU.

**AppImage updates.** Each AppImage embeds the update information
`gh-releases-zsync|storytold|vectorcraft|latest|vectorcraft-*-linux-<arch>.AppImage.zsync`
(appimagetool `-u`), and `package.sh` writes the matching `.zsync` beside it when `zsyncmake` (the
`zsync` package) is installed. [AppImageUpdate](https://info.yx-sf.com/sitemap.xml)
and AppImageLauncher then download only the changed blocks from the newest published,
non-pre-release release. The job checks both are there.

**Flatpak.** The `flatpak` jobs (x86_64 on `ubuntu-24.04`, aarch64 on `ubuntu-24.04-arm`) take the
Linux job's tarball and repackage it with `packaging/linux/flatpak-bundle.sh` and
`packaging/linux/flatpak/ai.storyteller.vectorcraft.bundle.yml` into a single-file bundle
(`flatpak install --user vectorcraft-<v>-linux-<arch>.flatpak`), then install it and run
`vectorcraft-cli --version` in the sandbox. No Rust build happens there, so the bundle carries the
same binaries as the AppImage. `packaging/linux/flatpak/ai.storyteller.vectorcraft.yml` is the
from-source manifest for a Flathub submission (its header says how to build it); packaging-lint
keeps the runtime and sandbox permissions of the two manifests identical.

### FreeBSD

GitHub has no FreeBSD runners, so the job builds in a FreeBSD 14.3 VM on `ubuntu-latest` (the same
image as `.github/workflows/freebsd.yml`). `packaging/freebsd/package.sh` writes a
`/usr/local`-style tree; users install it with
`tar -xzf vectorcraft-*-freebsd-x86_64.tar.gz --strip-components 1 -C /usr/local`.

### Web

The web job builds `apps/vectorcraft-web` with trunk and zips the static site
(`packaging/web/package.sh`). [`packaging/web/README.md`](../packaging/web/README.md) covers
hosting: any path works, `.wasm` must be served as `application/wasm`, and the sample header
files for common hosts.

## The draft release

The last job waits for every build, downloads their artifacts, writes `SHA256SUMS.txt` and creates
the draft `VectorCraft v<version>` with notes generated from the merged pull requests. If the draft
already exists, it replaces its assets and keeps it a draft. If that version is already published,
the job fails and asks for a version bump (`cargo xtask version set`).

## Secrets

The jobs that sign (macOS, Windows) and the draft-release job run in the `release` environment,
which only the `release` branch can use and which holds the signing secrets. The other jobs get no
secrets. Every secret is optional: a missing one produces unsigned artifacts and a
warning, never a failed build.

| Secret | Used for |
|---|---|
| `APPLE_CERTIFICATE`, `APPLE_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD`, `KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD` | the Developer ID certificate (base64 `.p12`), imported into a temporary keychain by `packaging/macos/import-cert.sh` |
| `APPLE_ID`, `APPLE_PASSWORD`, `APPLE_TEAM_ID` | notarization (`APPLE_PASSWORD` is an app-specific password) |
| `WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE`, `WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD` | Windows signing with a `.pfx` |
| `AZURE_TENANT_ID`, `AZURE_CLIENT_ID`, `AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET`, `AZURE_SIGNING_ENDPOINT`, `AZURE_SIGNING_ACCOUNT`, `AZURE_CERT_PROFILE` | Windows signing with Azure Trusted Signing |

## Revision history

| Date | Change | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-10-14 | minor | RPM glibc floor names libm's `GLIBC_2.35`: RHEL 9's glibc 2.34 provides libc's through backports |
| 2026-10-12 | minor | RPM dependencies use 64-bit runtime capabilities and enforce glibc 2.35 (#1275); real distro install/start-up checks remain pending |
| 2026-10-12 | minor | Portable mode (#1366): the Windows portable zip ships `portable.txt`; where the marker goes on macOS and Linux, and what Flatpak can't do |

### Revolve

# Revolve

This initial implementation follows the scope agreed in [issue #605](https://qcmw.tcti.cn/jishu/partner-58929344.html).

Draw an open profile with the Pen tool, select it, then choose **Effect > 3D and Materials > Revolve**.
The profile's horizontal distance from a vertical axis is its radius. **Axis side** chooses the left or right
edge of the profile's bounds; **Offset** moves the axis outward. For a cylinder made from a vertical
line, give it a nonzero offset. A vertical line at zero offset lies on the axis and has no surface.

**Revolve angle** sweeps 0 to 360 degrees. **Rotation X/Y/Z** rotates the viewing direction, with all three axes defaulting to 0 degrees. **Perspective**
runs 0° to 160°, as documented: 0° is an orthographic view, and wider angles bring the eye nearer (see
[three-d.md](three-d.md#perspective)). **Segments** controls radial resolution (8 to 128 for a full turn).
Lighting supports one to ten directional lights with the documented Light Settings (see [three-d.md](three-d.md#lighting)):
**Color**, **Intensity**, **Rotation**, **Height**, **Softness** and **Ambient Light**, and **Light behind the object**.
Color is white by default, with a picker and a reset dot. Colored light preserves neutral ambient illumination.
Turn **Shading** off to keep the source paint without lighting.

Shaded Revolve surfaces automatically use smooth lighting from the profile's tangents,
represented by linear gradients on vector triangles. There is no separate smoothing control.
Segments still controls the body silhouette; smoothing does not increase radial resolution.
Capped endpoint rings use curved vector boundaries. Original profile corners remain sharp,
and circular end caps keep uniform flat lighting. Turning Shading off disables lighting.
Smooth lighting follows the same light gizmo, rotation, perspective, preview, Cancel and undo behavior.
SVG and PDF export retain vector paths and gradients; Expand Appearance keeps
those gradients at their original positions when trimming visible surfaces. Non-solid
source paints retain their paint with a gradient shading overlay.

The dialog has **Rotation** and **Lighting** tabs. Rotation groups the profile and view controls. Drag a value or its label
to adjust it, use its slider, or double-click the value to type. Angles show degrees and lighting
values show percentages. **Segments** is in the **Advanced** section. Lighting controls are disabled
when **Shading** is off. A filled dot at the end of a row means the value differs from its default;
click the dot to reset that value. **Reset all** restores every Revolve parameter to its default.

The compact settings dialog opens beside the artboard. With **Preview** enabled, the selected
object has X (red), Y (green) and Z (blue) rotation rings directly on the artboard. Drag a ring to
adjust that axis; drag inside the rings to rotate freely. Hold Shift to snap to 15-degree increments.
The rings and the rotation fields stay in sync. Escape during a drag restores that gesture and
keeps the settings open. Escape again or Cancel restores the document before the dialog opened.
The gizmo appears while editing Revolve; normal source-path selection returns when the dialog closes.

Select the **Lighting** tab to use the light gizmo on the artboard. Drag the sun handle to move
the light on its side of the object: round the centre for its Rotation, towards the centre for a
greater Height. A hollow sun marks a light behind the object. Drag the **Rotation** ring or its label
horizontally to turn the light round the object; drag the **Height** line or its label vertically to
raise or lower it. The labels remain usable when the ring shrinks to a point (Height 90°).
Hold Shift to snap to 15-degree increments. Light gestures update their matching fields without
rotating the object, and keep the same temporary preview, Escape, Cancel and undo behaviour.
Intensity, Softness and Ambient Light are draggable fields and sliders. The Lights list selects which light the gizmo and settings edit; Add Light and Delete Light manage up to ten lights, keeping at least one. Ambient is shared and applied once. Preview, Cancel, Reset all and undo include the whole list.

**Shading** off hides the light gizmo and disables lighting controls. Switch to **Rotation** to return
to the object rings. **Show axis** in **Advanced** displays the source's vertical axis on the object.
Turning **Preview** off restores the original artwork and hides artboard controls until Preview is enabled.
In small windows, the controls scroll while OK and Cancel stay visible. Reset dots restore individual
settings; **Reset all** restores parameters on both tabs.

Preview changes are temporary until OK. Cancel restores the document; OK creates one undo step.
The source anchors remain editable. Appearance lists the effect for reopening its options.
SVG/PDF export evaluates filled vector faces; native saves retain the profile and effect parameters.
**Object > Expand Appearance** replaces the live effect with ordinary editable vector faces.

**Cap** in the shape controls closes the circular rings at the endpoints of an open profile.
It is on by default. Its saved parameter is `cap` (boolean, default true); missing parameters
also use caps. Set it to false to keep the ends open. The reset dot and Reset all restore Cap to on. Each cap is one closed curved vector path from the endpoint ring to the rotation axis,
with uniform flat shading. A full turn produces a projected circular disk (an ellipse in an
orthographic view); a partial turn produces a sector. Body faces share the same curved rim,
so no triangle patches interrupt the cap edge. Caps share the surface's rotation, perspective and paint, and appear in preview,
SVG/PDF export and Expand Appearance. The checkbox has a reset dot and is included in Reset all.

An endpoint on the axis needs no cap. Closed profiles and open profiles whose endpoints coincide
keep their existing geometry. Each open subpath of a compound profile is capped independently.
A partial revolve adds only the swept sector at each endpoint; the angular cut sides remain open.
This option does not make intersecting or compound profiles into a watertight solid.

In **Advanced**, **Keep visible surfaces only when expanding** is on by default. Expansion removes
completely covered faces and trims partially covered ones using the current rotation and perspective.
Visible interior surfaces through open ends remain. Uncheck it to retain every projected face.
The checkbox has its own reset dot and is included in **Reset all**. Its saved command parameter is
`expandVisibleOnly`; it does not change the live preview or SVG/PDF export baking.

Trimming applies to opaque solid paint. Transparent objects, gradients, patterns, non-normal blending,
later geometry effects and surfaces exceeding bounded visibility limits keep their complete geometry
to preserve their appearance. Visibility follows the same painter order as the live effect, including
its approximation for intersecting surfaces. Uncut faces keep their curved outlines. Visibility calculations use bounded polygon approximations
of curved rims; clipped portions become vector polygons. Expansion changes are undoable
with the standard command.

## Initial limits

- Lighting offers Standard, Diffuse, Top Left and Right, using the [shared original rigs](three-d.md#presets).
  Other effective settings show Custom; changing the view does not change the recognized lighting preset.
- Paths and compound paths only. Type, images and groups must be converted to paths first.
- Open profiles have circular end caps by default; turning Cap off keeps them open. Partial-sweep angular cut sides remain open. Closed profile boundaries are swept as provided.
- One Revolve per source object. Edit its options rather than applying another.
- Object-level Revolve uses the top visible fill, falling back to a stroke. Per-item Revolve uses that item's paint.
- Smooth diffuse shading, one to ten directional lights, no textures, cast shadows or physical materials. Smooth shading interpolates lighting in projected triangles; it does not smooth the silhouette or add specular highlights.
- Faces use back-to-front depth sorting. Caps facing the camera cover their rim seams; caps facing away sit behind the body. Intersecting profiles can have incorrect visibility.
- Curves use sixteen samples per segment; profiles are limited to 1,024 samples and surfaces to 32,768 faces. Smooth shaded side quads become two triangles and share that same limit. A continuous cap retains its original radial mesh cost within this limit. Projected ring curves have a 0.001-point fitting tolerance and a shared 32,768-curve limit.
- Axis, bounds and ordinary selection handles continue to refer to the editable 2D source profile.
- Extrude & Bevel, Inflate and Rotate are described in [three-d.md](three-d.md). Materials remain unimplemented.

## Architecture

Revolve geometry in `vectorcraft-three-d` uses `vectorcraft-geom`; the crate also uses `vectorcraft-pathops`
for the other 3D types. It creates a surface of revolution,
applies Euler view rotation, projects it, shades faces and sorts their depth. It has no UI or GPU dependency.
`vectorcraft-effects` turns those faces into document art. The renderer, export baking and
Expand Appearance use the same evaluator. The standard `effect.apply`, `effect.setParams`,
`effect.remove` and `effect.expandAppearance` commands expose it to the CLI, control channel and MCP.

Generated faces include narrow matching strokes to cover antialiasing seams. Their round
joins bound the overlap to half the stroke width, preventing acute triangle corners from
creating spikes along the silhouette in the canvas, SVG/PDF and expanded artwork.

Behaviour references: [public 3D and Materials options](https://bvhy.wtpuscm.cn/kuangjia/ebook-478828.html) and [public 3D effects documentation](https://news.ai-hao123.com/d/lu047577.html).
This implementation uses original mathematics and source code, with no Adobe software, assets or presets.

## Feature submission evidence

**Feature evidence last updated:** 2026-10-22.

The shared assessment status line and revision history are current upstream; this dated section records the submission's feature evidence and revisions without rescoring upstream or claiming a new combined build or runtime measurement.

- Current-main conflict reconciliation retains upstream and feature behavior; scores and estimates unchanged
- Superseded 2026-10-20 behavior, retained as history: Artboard Options shares existing presets and orientation controls and can fit artwork without moving it; artwork fitting uses the original target artboard and revision-scoped bounds caches

- Artboard Options puts Fit to Artwork Bounds and Fit to Selected Art in the Preset menu. Artwork bounds cover all drawn document art, including other artboards and off-board art; selection bounds may span artboards. Fit changes only the active artboard and keeps artwork stationary, including position-only fitting with Move Artwork enabled. Existing Background Color and presets remain available; scores and estimates unchanged.

Artboard Options forwards the active Artboard tool's Scale Artwork with Artboard option for ordinary resizing. Fit to Artwork Bounds and Fit to Selected Art explicitly leave artwork stationary. Dialog regression coverage checks preset/orientation/typed-size intent with scaling on and off, draft cancellation, one-step Undo/Redo, and fitting while Move Artwork and Scale Artwork are enabled. This is a narrow follow-up to #3277; no parity score or estimate is reassessed.

## Alpha gate

The core-workflow gate from craftrules' progress-docs standard: what a typical professional does with
Illustrator every day, checked end to end on the main platform (macOS) with save and reopen in the native
`.vectorcraft` format (lossless, property-tested round trips in `crates/format/tests/prop_format.rs`).
Checked 2026-10-10 from the code, tests and open issues; no workflow fails, so VectorCraft passes and stays alpha.

## Current focus

1. **Interaction-fidelity pass** (G1) by tool, from [ui-parity.md](ui-parity.md): Pen and Curvature, Direct
   Selection, smart guides and snapping first. 60–90 h, parallel by tool.
2. **`.ai` files from real users** (G9): layer structure (#951), guides (#779). 10–20 h.
3. **Launch and stability** (G10): the Windows and Linux start-up reports. 20–35 h.
4. **Core-tool bugs** (G11): SVG units reverting to points (#864) and a Transform effect in a fill's or stroke's own effects (#885). Shape Builder regions (#937), Asset Export ghost borders (#983 / #1037) and the stalling bezier drag preview (#834) are fixed. 8–15 h.
5. **Raster effects** (G2) alongside: the Effect Gallery's filter thumbnails and in-dialog preview area (the gallery and every Photoshop-style filter are in), 1–2 h.

  `plan/` before coding.

  budget missed (G15).

  (~170–270 h one agent, ~50–80 h with 4–6 agents).
- **1.0:** feature parity plus the fidelity pass, hardening and packaging for all three desktop OSes and the web.

## Highlighted-text Eyedropper (2026-10-21)

Type/Eyedropper switches preserve highlighted characters; sampling changes only their enabled
font/paint attributes. Enabled non-neutral source or target object transparency is refused
atomically; disable Transparency to preserve object transparency while sampling the range.
`tests/eyedropper.rs` covers ranges, Unicode, history and transparency; tool tests cover brush-key
sampling coexistence. Scores and estimates unchanged. See [development.md](development.md#highlighted-text-eyedropper-2026-10-21).

## Drag artwork between document tabs (2026-10-22)

Selection drags activate another visible document tab after 400 ms, then copy editable artwork
on canvas release with the original grab point. Source and clipboard preservation, resource
rendering, swatch conflicts, cancellation, rotated/zoomed views and target Undo/Redo have regression
coverage (`tests_document_drag`, `tests_clipboard`). Overflow-menu and cross-window drag remain
separate. Scores and hours unchanged. [Behavior and command details](development.md#drag-artwork-between-document-tabs-2026-10-22).

### Shaper

# Shaper

Sketch a basic shape with the Shaper tool (Shift+N). Rectangles, squares and ellipses snap to 45° rotation steps; hexagons to 90°. Triangles point up or down; sideways sketches snap to one of those orientations. Lines keep the angle you draw, including while Shift is held.

Scribble over overlapping paths to make an editable Shaper Group:

- Start in a filled region and cross into other regions to merge the regions touched. The result uses the starting region’s fill.
- Scribble within a region to remove its fill and keep its stroke. Hidden overlap boundaries are part of the same visible face; visible dividing strokes create separate faces.
- End the scribble outside the artwork to remove the touched fills and exposed boundary strokes. Shared edges along surviving filled areas remain, closing their contours. Compatible stroke pieces join at the new corners, so the selected stroke’s join style applies there.
- Scribble over an unfilled stroke segment to remove that piece. A line passing through a shape is split at the intersections, so its protruding ends can be removed separately.

Click once to select the group; click again to select its visible fill and change its color. Double-click with Shaper to enter construction editing and select an original shape. The Selection tool then moves or resizes it normally, and the visible composition updates. Escape leaves construction editing. The original live shapes and edit recipes survive native save/reopen. Outside construction editing, selection highlights and bounds show only the visible result. Outside construction editing, a marquee selects the group or its faces only where it reaches the visible result, and Direct Selection's clicks and marquee select only the anchor points of the visible result.

While the group or one of its faces is selected (Face Selection mode) and the Shaper or Selection tool is active, an arrow widget sits beside the middle of the right side of the original shapes’ bounds. Click it to enter Construction mode: the original shapes are isolated and nothing is selected, and a click with Shaper selects the group’s original shape under the pointer. Click the widget again to leave Construction mode with the group selected. The arrow points right in Face Selection mode and left in Construction mode.

Smart Guides and Snap to Point do not snap to the original shapes. The reference point of the transform tools snaps to an original shape only when that shape is selected, or under the pointer in Construction mode. Outside Construction mode the Lasso does not pick the anchor points of the original shapes, and the Add Anchor Point, Delete Anchor Point, Anchor Point and Scissors tools do not pick the anchor points or segments of an original shape that is not selected.

Object › Shaper › Release restores the original paths. Expand keeps the visible result as ordinary paths. Each scribble and source edit records one undo step. Sources in a composition must share a parent layer/group; Shaper limits a composition to 64 source paths and 4,096 segments.

Finer gesture heuristics remain to be implemented.

Behavior reference: [public Shaper documentation](https://yisc.ai-hao123.com/xuexi/partner-49397327.html). Rotation steps and independent fill/stroke cases follow the contributor’s supplied requirements. No reference images or product assets are included.

## Feature submission evidence

**Feature evidence last updated:** 2026-10-22.

The shared assessment status line and revision history are current upstream; this dated section records the submission's feature evidence and revisions without rescoring upstream or claiming a new combined build or runtime measurement.

- Current-main conflict reconciliation retains upstream and feature behavior; scores and estimates unchanged
- Superseded 2026-10-20 behavior, retained as history: Artboard Options shares existing presets and orientation controls and can fit artwork without moving it; artwork fitting uses the original target artboard and revision-scoped bounds caches (scores/hours unchanged)

- Artboard Options puts Fit to Artwork Bounds and Fit to Selected Art in the Preset menu. Artwork bounds cover all drawn document art, including other artboards and off-board art; selection bounds may span artboards. Fit changes only the active artboard and keeps artwork stationary, including position-only fitting with Move Artwork enabled. Existing Background Color and presets remain available; scores and estimates unchanged.

Artboard Options forwards the active Artboard tool's Scale Artwork with Artboard option for ordinary resizing. Fit to Artwork Bounds and Fit to Selected Art explicitly leave artwork stationary. Dialog regression coverage checks preset/orientation/typed-size intent with scaling on and off, draft cancellation, one-step Undo/Redo, and fitting while Move Artwork and Scale Artwork are enabled. This is a narrow follow-up to #3277; no parity score or estimate is reassessed.

## How this was measured (2026-10-10)

- **Target version.** Illustrator 2026, the 30.x line. Feature set from Adobe's public documentation and release
  announcements: 30.0 (October 2025: font browser, gradient dither and perceptual blending, tangent and
  perpendicular snapping, artboard locking and colours, Turntable beta, Firefly integration), 30.2 (TIFF in
  Export for Screens), 30.3, 30.5 (Concept to Vector, Prompt to Edit, Rewrite Text) and 30.7 (Blend panel with
  ease in/out). Sources: the [30.0 announcement](https://zkuw.yx-sf.com/shuju/report-20452859.html),
  the [30.7 announcement](https://qcmw.tcti.cn/jishu/partner-58929344.html)
  and helpx feature pages.
- **The installed Illustrator was not inspected.** Illustrator 2026 is installed on the owner's Mac, but this
  repo's clean-room rule ([`AGENTS.md`](../AGENTS.md), from the project owner) forbids reading anything inside an
  Adobe install, its `Info.plist` and `.lproj` folders included, and forbids launching or measuring it. So
  nothing here is a menu dump or a side-by-side measurement: the numbers come from our own code against
  Illustrator's public documentation.
- **From the code (measured, origin/main `01e165af`):**
  - Menu tree (`crates/ui-egui/src/menus.rs`, laid out in Illustrator's menu order): 348 items bound to
    commands, 26 stubs (`todo(…)`/`todos(…)`), so 93.0% of menu items do something (348 and 26 after Snap to Glyph shipped in #3124; 348 and 27 after the
    Revolve merge; 350 and 25, 93.3%, after Graph › Design and Marker; 353 and 22, 94.1%, after Extrude & Bevel, Inflate and Rotate). The stubs: Effect › 3D and Materials › Materials, Effect › SVG Filters, Edit › Spelling (3), Graph › Column, Live Paint
    Gap Options, Optical Margin Alignment, global and video rulers (2),
    Window › Arrange (4), SVG Interactivity, Other Script…, Help.
    Gap Options, Optical Margin Alignment, Start Global Edit, global and video rulers (2),
    Window › Arrange (4), SVG Interactivity, Other Script…, Help (the Brush and Symbol Libraries placeholders are gone: Window › Symbol Libraries works since 2026-10-23, Window › Brush Libraries since 2026-10-24).
  - Engine commands: ~710 ids registered with `cmd!` across `crates/engine/src/cmd` (plus macro-generated
    families), and 85 UI-only commands (`UI_COMMANDS`).
  - Tools: 91 in `crates/tools/src/catalog.rs`; Touch Type is listed but not implemented, and the Dimension
    tool (added in Illustrator 28.x) is absent.
  - Effects catalogue (`crates/effects/src/lib.rs`): see [effects-parity.md](effects-parity.md).
  - Tests: 4,924 `#[test]` functions plus 40 property-test blocks (was "~2,840" in the last estimate).
    ~354k lines of Rust (was ~221k on 2026-10-07).
  - Formats: the `FORMATS` table in `crates/engine/src/cmd/fileio/formats.rs`, see
    [file-format-parity.md](file-format-parity.md).
  - Languages: row counts of `crates/ui-egui/src/i18n/*.tsv`, see [localization-parity.md](localization-parity.md).
- **From users:** the 71 open GitHub issues on 2026-10-10, which show what real users hit first (Illustrator
  `.ai` files opening with the wrong layer structure #951/#868, guides lost from `.ai` #779, Shape Builder
  region detection #937/#893, launch failures on some Windows and Linux machines #858/#964/#620, pen pressure on
  macOS #852, Preferences options that do nothing #394).
- **Presence is not parity.** Each area is scored by behaviour against the public documentation, and an area is
  100% only when every feature in it behaves like Illustrator. Scores were set by the agents that built the
  features, so they are upper bounds; this pass lowered the ones contradicted by open issues.

Excluding the generative-AI row (the old table had none), depth is ~76% and the remaining feature work
~220–360 h. With 4–6 agents on disjoint crates, wall-clock time divides by about 3.5–4 (shared files such as
`menus.rs` and the i18n catalogs serialize some work): ~95–165 h to full parity.

**Why the totals moved up from ~320–500 h (2026-10-05):** the target moved (30.x added gradient dither,
perceptual blending, new snaps, artboard locking, the Blend panel, Turntable), open issues lowered three areas,
the raster-effects row was re-counted bottom-up from measured filter throughput, and generative AI is now
counted. Work that landed since (Variables, Distort/Pixelate/Texture filters, Object Mosaic, German, placed
documents) moved other rows up.

## Ready for real work

Three audiences, each with its own readiness and its own hours to ~95%. Essentials ⊂ mainstream ⊂ full, so the
hours nest. Hours are calibrated as in [Calibration](#calibration). They divide by about 3.5–4 across 4–6 agents
for the feature and fidelity work; stability on users' hardware, the real-file corpus and native-language
review parallelize less and need humans.

| Audience | Ready % | Opus 5.5 agent hours to ~95% (one agent) | With 4–6 agents | Work that dominates |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| **Full Illustrator** (ready for real work; decides the stage) | **~62%** (57–67%) | **~340–560 h** | ~95–160 h | the mainstream work below, plus 3D (50–85 h), raster effects (24–40 h), advanced type (20–28 h), generative AI (30–60 h), localization (55–90 h) and ecosystem |
| **Mainstream illustrator** | **~65%** (60–70%) | **~230–380 h** | ~65–110 h | the interaction-fidelity pass (60–90 h), hardening and QA (30–50 h), stability (20–35 h), performance budgets (15–25 h), `.ai` exchange (10–20 h), the remaining depth of the everyday areas |
| **Essentials user** | **~75%** (70–80%) | **~60–105 h** | ~25–45 h | launch and stability on Windows (20–35 h), in-app help and onboarding (8–15 h), basic QA (10–15 h), Shape Builder regions (4–8 h), UI polish |

### Full Illustrator: additive weighted sum over the dimensions

The standard's method, the same in every app: a weighted **sum** over the dimensions, with written weights.
Values are from [By dimension](#by-dimension).

| Dimension | Weight | Value | Contribution |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Features (depth) | 35 | 75% | 26.3 |
| UI/UX fidelity | 15 | 55% | 8.3 |
| File formats | 12 | 75% | 9.0 |
| Stability | 10 | 60% | 6.0 |
| Performance | 8 | 60% | 4.8 |
| Platforms | 5 | 80% | 4.0 |
| Hardware | 4 | 35% | 1.4 |
| Localization | 4 | 74% | 3.0 |
| Ecosystem and plug-ins | 4 | 15% | 0.6 |
| AI features | 3 | 0% | 0.0 |
| **Ready for real work** | **100** | | **~62%** |

The weights put most of the number on what professionals use daily (features, interaction, files, stability).
Generative AI also sits inside the features row at weight 2 of 105, so it is counted slightly twice; that costs
under a point.

### Mainstream illustrator and essentials user

Both start from feature depth over the areas concerned. **Mainstream:** ~83% over 16 areas (weight 83 of 105:
selection, drawing, path operations, colour, strokes, appearance, live effects, type core, symbols and blends,
layers and artboards, view, guides, file formats, Export for Screens, UI chrome, print). That is discounted
×0.9 for interaction fidelity, ×0.92 for stability on real machines and ×0.92 for Illustrator-file exchange
(83 × 0.9 × 0.92 × 0.92 ≈ 63). The dimensions a typical illustrator rarely hits (plug-in ecosystem,
generative AI, pen tilt, languages beyond their own) are left out. **Essentials:** see [Essentials user](#essentials-user).

The discounts, with the evidence:

- **Illustrator's own files (×0.92).** `.ai` and EPS open as editable art by reading their PDF/PostScript and the
  structure of the editing data. Users do open legacy files a lot: 28 of the 350 issues (8%, ~22 people) are
  about `.ai`/EPS, the most common single format theme. 20 of the 28 are fixed (often the same day). The 8 open
  ones are about structure, not missing art: layers flattened or multiplied (#951: 109 layers instead of 14;
  #868), guides lost (#779), slower opening (#758), live effects, brushes and symbols as their drawn look
  (#637). VectorCraft can't write Illustrator's editing data (undocumented), so its PDF-compatible `.ai` opens
  in Illustrator as plain art; the legacy `.ai` of version 7 it also writes keeps layers, groups and type as text (one
  artboard per file, no transparency) but hasn't been tested by users yet (#868). That blocks beta (the main-format rule) for people who hand files back to Illustrator users,
  but it doesn't stop someone opening and reworking their own archive.
- **Interaction fidelity (×0.9).** Pen, Direct Selection, smart guides and snapping are deep
  ([ui-parity.md](ui-parity.md)), and there has never been a side-by-side session. The issue tracker says the
  details mostly hold: 79 issues are about core drawing (pen, paths, selection, snapping, transform), 68 of them
  (86%) closed, 11 open (#991, #975, #955, #973 among them). One practitioner wrote "0 learning curve from
  pretty heavy AI use over last 20+ years" (#541).
- **Stability on real machines (×0.92).** The code never panics by design, and the main platform (macOS) starts
  reliably, but 26 issues mention a crash, freeze or failed launch (8 open: #858, #964 fixed the day of this
  review, #620, #818, #905 on Windows 7, #834). There is no field record and no real-world file corpus yet.
- **Performance unverified.** Budgets (`vectorcraft-cli perf`) were all met at 25k paths on 2026-10-11; runs of
  0.10.0 on Linux with 4 logical CPUs, reported in #1172 on 2026-10-13, missed all three render budgets at 20k
  paths. Performance is not discounted separately. Open user reports of slowness in mainstream work include #575
  (Linux AppImage), #758 (`.ai` open time), #1097 (zoom and pan in 0.9.0) and #1731 (a drag that stutters as it
  starts).
- **Missing subsystems** a minority need daily (3D, CJK vertical composition, scripting)
  pull the full number below the mainstream one.

### Essentials user

A beginner or casual user who touches only the core features, at their default settings. Excluded: advanced
options, pro workflows, file-exchange edge cases, and everything the mainstream number already leaves out.
Depth here is "does the basic use work", not the area's full score.

| Core feature | Weight | Depth | Evidence |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| New, open and save documents | 8 | 95% | New Document presets, Open for SVG/PDF/`.ai`/images, lossless native save, Data Recovery |
| Shape tools (rectangle, ellipse, polygon, star, line) | 9 | 95% | all shape tools, Live Corners |
| Selection, move, scale, rotate | 9 | 92% | bounding box, smart guides, transform tools |
| Pen and Pencil, basic use | 7 | 88% | [ui-parity.md](ui-parity.md); a few Pencil and Curvature options missing |
| Fill, stroke, colour, swatches | 9 | 95% | M3 done; highlighted-text Eyedropper font/paint and source/target transparency refusal regression-tested; scores and hours unchanged |
| Gradients, basic | 4 | 90% | Gradient panel and on-canvas annotator |
| Type: point and area text, font, size | 8 | 88% | font menu with previews; Hyphenation… and Justification… options per paragraph (#2310, #2755) |
| Align, group, arrange | 6 | 95% | |
| Layers, basic | 4 | 85% | Layers panel rework; no row context menus |
| Shape Builder | 5 | 70% | beginners lean on it; region detection failed on art of thousands of segments (#937's reproduced case, fixed, and its edge-source grid is bounded in memory; unconfirmed on the reporter's file) |
| Pathfinder | 4 | 95% | exact booleans |
| Place images, Image Trace | 4 | 85% | 13 trace presets |
| Export PNG/JPG/SVG/PDF, print | 8 | 92% | Art Optimized supersample closes Asset Export ghost borders (#983 / #1037) |
| Undo and redo | 4 | 100% | unlimited, property-tested |
| Zoom, pan, fit | 4 | 95% | |
| Artboards, basic | 4 | 88% | |
| **Weighted depth** | **97** | **~91%** | |

The discounts a beginner actually hits:

- **Launch and stability, ×0.93:** fine on macOS, but some Windows machines fail to start (#858, #620, #818).
- **Discoverability and UI clarity, ×0.92:** the layout follows Illustrator's and comes in 11 languages, but
  there is no in-app help (Help › VectorCraft Help… is a stub), no Learn panel or tutorials, and a newcomer
  meets Illustrator's density without Illustrator's learning material.
- **Opening files people send them, ×0.96:** PDF, SVG, images and most `.ai` files open as editable art.
  Layer-structure problems (#951) matter less to a beginner.

91 × 0.93 × 0.92 × 0.96 ≈ 75: **~75% (70–80%), estimated.**

### User sentiment (measured 2026-10-10)

All 350 issues and 964 issue comments on GitHub (Discussions are off), authors other than the maintainers:

- **Praise:** 17 issue threads from 15 people ("Great work on this. It's kind of amazing" #954; "really great
  job" #841; "I really love this project" #620; "0 learning curve from pretty heavy AI use over last 20+ years"
  #541).
- **"Replacing Illustrator" reports:** none found in the tracker. Praise is for the app as it is, not reports
  of having switched on paid work. Owner reports from practitioners outside GitHub aren't counted here.
- **Themes of the 350 issues:** core drawing 79 (11 open), import/export 59 (17 open), launch/crash/platform/
  performance 51 (12 open), UI chrome and layers 46 (10 open), type 28 (4 open), colour 12 (5 open), other and
  requests 75 (24 open). 35 are titled as feature requests. The open set is mostly core-path bugs and
  file-exchange problems, not niche features.

**Stage: alpha.** All six core workflows pass the core-workflow gate end to end on macOS with save and reopen
([roadmap.md › Alpha gate](roadmap.md#alpha-gate)); file exchange with Illustrator users is partial, which is
what keeps it from beta, not from alpha.

## Calibration

Hours come from this repo's own history (git log and merged-PR timestamps, `gh pr list`):

- **Raster filters**, one agent working serially on [gap 2](gaps.md): Pixelate (4 filters, merged 2026-10-10
  08:47), Texture (6, 12:44), Distort (3, 16:24). About 4 h per batch, **0.7–1.2 h per Photoshop-style
  filter** including dialog, catalogue row, menus and translations into 11 languages.
- **M3 (paint and appearance):** a 92-task plan whose packages were planned at 5–11 h each took about
  1–1.5 agent hours each, on 2026-10-04/05 with 6–8 agents.
- **Medium features:** about 0.8 h each (Text Wrap, Graphs, Effect › Pathfinder…: ~20 in ~16 h on 2026-10-02).
- **Whole repo:** 1,671 commits and 592 merged PRs from 2026-09-30 to 2026-10-10, with several agents in
  parallel and a dozen community contributors.

Large subsystems (3D, CJK composition, generative AI) have no comparable history and are counted bottom-up,
with a wider range. What needs a human: native-speaker review of the translations, an owner decision on
generative models, real Illustrator files that users own (used locally, never committed), and Wacom/pen
hardware for tilt and rotation.

## Where we already beat Illustrator

Exact curve booleans, off-thread multithreaded rendering, unlimited undo, lossless SVG/PDF export of live effects,
a documented JSON format, Affinity 1–3 import, the same app on the web and on Linux/FreeBSD, scrubby numeric fields,
sandboxed WebAssembly plug-ins, and every command, gesture and dialog drivable by agents (MCP, CLI, control channel).

## Out of scope (by design or by law)

- **Adobe cloud services** (Libraries sync, Adobe Fonts, Projects, Express templates, Firefly): pluggable
  provider APIs at most, never built in.
- **Adobe's bundled assets** (swatch, brush, symbol libraries, presets, icons): ours are original.
- **Illustrator's private editing data, beyond its structure:** see
  [file-format-parity.md](file-format-parity.md#illustrators-private-editing-data).

Film Grain (G2, 2026-10-12) is the first Artistic filter: deterministic document-space monochrome
grain, transparency-preserving tone controls, a bounded live dialog, undo and appearance editing,
with PNG rendering and SVG/PDF raster baking. Evidence: `crates/effects/src/pixel/artistic.rs`,
its `film_grain_*` tests and the canvas/export cases in `crates/engine/src/tests/rasterfilters.rs`.
This raises the measured Photoshop filter count to 29/57; the depth estimate is conservatively 49%.
The full feature/readiness headline remains unchanged at its existing rounding.

Cutout, Neon Glow and Poster Edges (G2, 2026-10-16) follow as original Artistic filters with live
preview, undo, appearance editing and save/reopen, keeping coverage at any Document Raster Effects
resolution. Evidence: `crates/effects/src/pixel/artistic.rs`, its `cutout_*`, `neon_glow_*` and
`poster_edges_*` tests, and `artistic_settings_survive_a_save_and_open` in
`crates/engine/src/tests/rasterfilters.rs`. Smudge Stick, Sponge and Watercolor follow (G2, 2026-10-16) as original Artistic filters with the same
live preview, undo, appearance editing and save/reopen; evidence: `crates/effects/src/pixel/paint.rs`,
its `pixel::tests_paint::*` tests and `tests_rasterfilters`. Measured Photoshop filter count 36/57; depth unchanged.
`crates/engine/src/tests/rasterfilters.rs`. Bas Relief, Charcoal, Photocopy and Stamp (G2, 2026-10-16, #2527) follow as original Sketch filters
(`crates/effects/src/pixel/sketch_ink.rs`, `pixel::tests_sketch::*`). Measured Photoshop filter count 37/57; depth unchanged.

## Detailed missing items per area (2026-10-05 table, still current unless the area table above says otherwise)

> **Duplicated rows (2026-10-14):** this table lists "Selection, transform & align tools" three times and "Drawing tools"
> twice, each time with different text, as merges that each edited the table left them. Which text is current needs the
> owner's judgement, so the rows are kept as they are.

The previous estimate's per-area missing lists, kept as evidence. Scores in it are superseded by the table above.

_Method (2026-10-02; M3 rows re-derived 2026-10-04, file, export, print, links and UI-chrome rows after M4 on 2026-10-05):_ Illustrator's feature surface is split into 22 areas, weighted by how much of the app (and of
real users' work) each represents. Each area is scored by depth of behaviour, not by presence of a menu item: an area
is 100% only when every feature in it behaves like Illustrator. Feature parity = Σ weight × score / Σ weight. Remaining
time is counted per area from what is missing, calibrated on measured throughput: in the last session one agent landed
about 20 medium features (Text Wrap, Graphs, Effect → Pathfinder, export baking…) in ~16 h wall clock including builds
and CI on a heavily loaded machine — about 0.8 h per medium feature; large subsystems (3D, raster filters, vertical type)
are counted bottom-up. The M3 rows (colour, strokes, appearance) come from a detailed 92-task M3 plan whose review
found more missing depth than the first estimate; all 92 tasks landed on 2026-10-04 and 2026-10-05 with 6–8 agents in parallel; its packages, planned at 5–11 h each, took
about 1–1.5 agent-hours each, so the other rows (estimated on the older scale) are likely high.

## Honest assessment by dimension (2026-10-05)

The previous assessment's evidence per dimension, kept as it was; the [By dimension](#by-dimension) table above supersedes its numbers.

**In one line:** about two-thirds to three-quarters of Illustrator's features exist and work, and for everyday
vector illustration (drawing, paths, paint and appearance, SVG/PDF/print) VectorCraft is close to usable. Measured
against "a power user can't tell the difference", it is closer to 40–55%. What stands between here and "anyone can
switch" is a handful of large subsystems plus a fidelity pass, not a long tail of small fixes.

**How much to trust the numbers:** area scores are graded by the agents that built the features, from behaviour docs
(`plan/illustrator/`) and tests, not by side-by-side use of Illustrator. Treat them as upper bounds. Look & feel is
the only dimension measured against the reference app. Performance budgets haven't been re-run on an idle machine
since 2026-10-01.

| Dimension | Estimate | Evidence and what's missing |
|---|---|---|
| **Breadth:** menus, tools and panels exist | ~90% | 13 menu items still stubbed; every tool implemented except Touch Type; 51 panel modules |
| **Depth:** each feature behaves like Illustrator | ~69–75% | Strong: paint, appearance and colour (M3), Pathfinder and booleans, selection, drawing, files (M4). Weak: advanced type (~45%; inline symbols in text are beyond parity and don't raise it), brushes and symbols (in progress), raster effects (~20%; since 57/57 filters and the Effect Gallery, #2883, see the area table above) |
| **Large missing subsystems** | 0–20% | 3D & Materials (~25%, initial 3D types without materials), SVG Filters (Photoshop-style raster effects (57/57) and the Effect Gallery (#2883) have since shipped), CJK composition (vertical type with kinsoku, tate-chu-yoko and the font's vertical metrics; mojikumi open), scripting |
| **Interaction fidelity:** modifiers, cursors, small behaviours | ~30–40% | The dedicated pass hasn't started, and there has been no side-by-side session with Illustrator yet. A power user notices this first |
| **Look & feel** | ~75–80% | Measured against Illustrator 2026 screenshots (2026-10-02); the panels added since haven't been re-measured |
| **File interop** | ~85% | SVG/SVGZ, PDF and PDF-compatible `.ai` (and legacy version 7 `.ai` out, keeping layers, groups and type as text), EPS, DXF, EMF/WMF, raster formats, PSD export and PSD/PSB placement (merged image), Place and Links, Package, Print, clipboard flavours. Affinity documents (Affinity 1–3) open natively as editable art, checked against 51 pinned public files (33 current `.af`), with selected saved-thumbnail comparisons and every-board native/SVG/PDF/PSD checks for current files; Affinity export is missing and effects, adjustments and brushes don't import. Affinity isn't an Illustrator feature, so this doesn't raise the parity score. The editing copy inside an Illustrator EPS or `.ai` is read for its structure: layers, groups, names, hidden objects and type, colours, gradients, transparency, images and every artboard (see Out of scope for what it doesn't read yet); DWG has no open spec |
| **Bundled content:** brush, symbol, style and swatch libraries | ~30% | Ours are original and generated in code, and far fewer than Illustrator ships; symbol libraries have one (Basic Shapes) and brush libraries four (Art Ribbons, Calligraphic Nibs, Pattern Borders, Scatter Shapes) beside User Defined and Other Library… |
| **Performance** | unverified | Multithreaded, off-thread rendering and caches are in place. The last budget run (2026-10-01, loaded machine) measured 290 ms for a 50k-path fit against a 16 ms budget. Re-run `vectorcraft-cli perf` on an idle machine |
| **Robustness** | good, new | ~2,840 tests, property tests, no panics in shipped code (lints, the `guard` safety net, import fuzzing), Data Recovery. Missing: a corpus of real-world files, Windows/Linux/browser QA |
| **Platforms and 1.0 polish** | ~60% | The macOS app and the web build work, and Finder opens every readable format with the macOS app (#295, #354); on macOS the menus are in the system menu bar, laid out as a Mac app's, with the in-window menus as a fallback (`--in-window-menus`; verified on Windows and by cross-compilation, not yet by hand on a Mac); hybrid-graphics laptops render on the power-saving GPU by default on Windows and macOS (#306), and Windows starts on Direct3D 12, falling back to OpenGL, and loads no Vulkan driver unless `WGPU_BACKEND` asks for it (#545: Vulkan flickered black on an Intel GPU, DX12 and OpenGL didn't; #806: a faulty Vulkan driver crashed the app before its window appeared; verified by unit tests and the reporter's runs with `WGPU_BACKEND`), and Linux on the GPU the desktop runs on, since a Wayland compositor may refuse frames from the other one; a window that fails on its GPU while starting up starts again on the next one instead of crashing (#502; the dual-GPU Wayland case is verified by unit tests and cross-compilation, not on such hardware); web drops land in the document they were dropped on (#359); desktop drops carry no pointer position (winit 0.30), so a dropped document opens as a tab of its own and a picture or text is placed in the middle of the view, while the web places anything dropped on the canvas and opens what is dropped off it, as Illustrator does (#472); a web page that loses its WebGPU device or WebGL context restarts its graphics with the same documents (#369); on Linux/Wayland the clipboard reads the compositor's own (data-control) and copied image files paste, but files can't be dropped on the window under native Wayland until eframe moves to winit 0.31 (#398; the Wayland side is verified by compilation only), so Preferences › Performance › Linux Display Server › X11 (XWayland) opens the window through XWayland, where drops work (#1151; verified by unit tests and cross-compilation, not on a Wayland desktop); on Linux the Paste menu checks the system clipboard on a background thread, so a clipboard owner that never answers no longer freezes the window, while Windows and macOS keep their quick in-line check (#510; the X11 hang verified by the contributor, here by headless tests); on KDE Plasma 6.3+ under Wayland, pens and pen displays reach the app only under XWayland (`WAYLAND_DISPLAY=`) or with KWin's `KWIN_WAYLAND_EMULATE_TABLET=1`, since winit 0.30 has no Wayland tablet input (#491, not verified on hardware); Windows/Linux packaging and accessibility are pending; an experimental, unsupported Windows 7 x64 OpenGL build exists (community-contributed, not verified by maintainers) |
| **Agent automation** | beyond Illustrator | Every command, gesture and dialog is drivable over MCP, the CLI and the control channel; synthetic-input counts, pending events and per-frame control requests are bounded (#1709); what an agent reads and writes on disk can be confined to chosen folders (`--automation-read-root` / `--automation-write-root`, as in PhotoCraft, #832) |
| **Scrubby numeric fields** | beyond Illustrator | As in Photoshop, dragging a numeric field's label (`W:`, `Opacity:`, the Character panel's icons) left or right steps its value live; one undo step per drag, Escape cancels (#400) |
| **Align Stroke on live type** | beyond Illustrator | The Stroke panel's Align Stroke works on type's character stroke: inside or outside the glyphs without Create Outlines, the type staying editable (as InDesign does; users have asked Illustrator for it since 2010, e.g. [redd.it/1dwhos6](https://xksn.wtpuscm.cn/huodong/page-531602.html)). Canvas, PDF and EPS clip it to its side of the glyphs; SVG keeps the text live and draws the stroke on the glyph outlines (#2294) |

## Evidence: what ships today, by area

- 3D lighting presets: `crates/effects/src/lighting_presets.rs`, `crates/engine/src/cmd/effectcmd/lighting_presets_tests.rs` and the pointer tests in `crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs/revolve/tests.rs` cover recognition, atomic targeting, native round trips, preview, Cancel, reset and Undo.

- **Status-bar pointer readout (2026-10-18):** uses the same effective ruler origin as the position fields, then formats the relative X/Y in General units. The absolute pointer position, document, selection, Undo/Redo and saved state are preserved. Three `chrome::tests::status_coordinates_*` painted-text regressions cover zero/positive/negative origins, unit conversion, global/artboard mode, active artboard, reset and missing pointer/document. Original headless status-bar captures were reviewed before and after the change. Scores and hours are unchanged.

**Drawing tools — Polygon and Star counts:** The existing canvas placement dialog reads the stored count and saves it only after successful placement. `polygon_and_star_canvas_counts_persist_without_new_toolbar_dialogs` covers both tools, repeated drags, tool switching, reopening and Cancel. Counts remain session tool options. Existing click and toolbar gestures are retained; no score or hour change.
**Live trace result bounds and selection highlights exclude the retained bitmap except in source-image views:** `live_trace_result_bounds_exclude_the_retained_bitmap_at_any_angle` checks every TraceView, geometric and visual bounds and rotated result bounds. `live_trace_selection_highlight_excludes_the_retained_source_rectangle` checks result highlights and the existing ordinary-group policy. Shared editing-child traversal also preserves Shaper handling.
**Artboard Options shares existing presets and orientation controls and can fit artwork without moving it; artwork fitting includes all drawn document art across artboards and off-board; artwork bounds are cached by active document and revision, and selection uses the shared bounds cache across artboards:** Shared existing preset definitions are reused; no external preset assets are added. Presets preserve each selected artboard's orientation, and orientation choices apply even when the active board already matches. Fit operations draft bounds until OK, affect only the active artboard and leave artwork in place. Regression coverage checks draft/Cancel, selected-set application, active-only fitting and Undo.

**Review follow-up:** The fit-query follow-up covers fitting after draft dimensions change, updated artwork after a document revision, cache scope and new-artboard fitting/history. Selection uses the existing application bounds cache; global artwork queries include all drawn document art and are cached by active document and revision; draft geometry and target artboards do not limit membership. This is not a native timing claim.

- **Stable status-bar readouts:** The status message keeps its left anchor and clipping allocation as live values, canvas hover and background-job state change. Coordinate and spinner slots stay reserved; narrow windows hide optional diagnostics, then coordinates, to preserve message space. Widths are measured from the active font, translated labels and fixed numeric samples, never current readings. Coordinates through +/-9999.99 selected units, timings through 9999.9 ms and FPS through 9999 remain readable. Extreme values are elided with full tooltip/accessibility text; only elided fields show a tooltip. Coordinate inspection retains the last point per document and clears on PointerGone. Regressions cover message origin/clip/bounds/elision invariance, all registered languages and ten units, responsive layouts, coordinate inspection and document switching, and accessible busy transitions. The contributor rebuilt and confirmed the original status-bar issue is fixed with their own artwork on 2026-10-19; the subsequent upstream rebase is checked by regressions and full CI. The artwork stays local. Scores and estimates are unchanged. Sample widths use a bounded single-entry UI cache keyed by language, unit and pixels per point; two regressions verify reuse during live updates and invalidation after each display-setting change.

- **Canvas review follow-up:** Cached canvas dimensions match the renderer limit before cache-key creation, view construction and worker submission. Controlled-worker regression checks oversized width and height, high DPI and the render transform without allocating oversized images. Scores and estimates are unchanged.
- **Cached canvas frames during viewport changes:** Cached screen textures use their own raster dimensions and pixels-per-point when reprojected. `canvas::tests::cached_frames_keep_their_scale_during_resize_rotation_and_dpi_changes` holds the worker and checks every UV corner against the cached render transform, including isolated viewport-only resize at zero/30-degree rotation, fractional raster dimensions, zoom/pan, changed rotation, monitor-DPI changes in both directions, Pixel Preview and replacement-frame delivery. The contributor rebuilt and confirmed the original resize issue is fixed with their own artwork on 2026-10-19; the subsequent upstream rebase is checked by regressions and full CI. The artwork stays local. Scores and estimates are unchanged.
- **PDF editable import:** Place from bytes or a path with `link: false`, and `clipboard.importPdf` followed by Paste, preserve live type on the selected page. Place still honors `textAs: "outlines"`. Synthetic two-page regressions: `crates/engine/src/cmd/fileio/tests_pdffidelity.rs`. No change to the PDF reader's existing fallback rules.
- **Selected Grid Repeat handles (#2691):** `tools/src/repeat_grid.rs` tests place the handles outside the grid at zoom 0.5, 1 and 4, preview rows, columns and spacing, leave no undo step for a drag that ends where it began, and give bounding-box handles priority; a headless canvas regression drags the row handle two tiles down in a zoomed view (3 → 5 rows, the source unchanged, one Undo back) and the column-spacing slider. Scores and hours unchanged.
- **Selected Mirror Repeat handles:** a headless canvas regression creates the default mirror repeat and drags its Top bounding-box handle where the axis crosses it; the repeat grows vertically while its width stays fixed. Existing mirror-axis checks cover center movement and end-handle hit priority. The focused UI mirror tests pass. Scores and hours unchanged.
- **Transform effect options (#885):** Effect › Distort & Transform › Transform… has visible Transform Objects, Transform Patterns and Scale Strokes & Effects checkboxes (`distort.transform` params `objects`, `patterns`, `strokes`; files without them draw as before). - **Video display options (#2849):** Artboard Options' Show Video Safe Areas and Video Ruler Pixel Aspect Ratio, and View › Rulers › Show Video Rulers ([Set video display options for artboards](https://mmrp.yx-sf.com/yanjiu/mobile-85039228.html)). The help page names the safe areas without numbers; our choice is [EBU R 95](https://bdax.wtpuscm.cn/gongsi/change-947830.html)'s (note 5): the canvas outlines the action-safe area 3.5% and the title-safe (graphics-safe) area 5% in from each edge, 1 point wide and turned with the view; exports and print leave them out. - **Pattern names and swatch names:** `pattern.options` refuses a new name that another pattern, a swatch or a color group has. It takes a name that only the pattern's own swatches have. The reference page does not say what happens when the new name is taken; the refusal follows VectorCraft's rule that swatches and color groups share one namespace (`Document::swatch_name_taken`), which `swatch.new` and `swatch.edit` also follow. A rename gives the new name only to the pattern's swatches that had the old one; any other swatch with the old name keeps it, and art linked to that swatch stays linked. `object.pattern.make` and `object.pattern.saveCopy` number a color group's name as they number a swatch's. Tests in `tests/pattern.rs` cover each command. Public reference: [Create and edit patterns](https://xcea.yx-sf.com/yunying/forum-52415577.html) (archived copy).
