### Extrude & Bevel, Inflate and Rotate

# Extrude & Bevel, Inflate and Rotate

The other three 3D types of **Effect › 3D and Materials** next to [Revolve](revolve.md). Like Revolve each is a
live effect: the source path stays editable, the effect draws shaded vector faces, and SVG/PDF export, native
saves and **Object › Expand Appearance** use the same evaluator.

Select a path or compound path, then choose **Effect › 3D and Materials › Extrude & Bevel…**, **Inflate…** or
**Rotate…**. The options dialog opens beside the artboard with tabs:

- **Object** (Extrude & Bevel and Inflate): the shape's own options, below.
- **Rotation**: a **Presets** menu, **Rotation X/Y/Z** (−180° to 180°) and **Perspective** (0° to 160°, below). The rotation rings
  on the artboard turn the object about the centre of its bounds; Shift snaps to 15°.
- **Lighting**: **Shading** and the light's settings (below), as for Revolve; or drag the light on the
  artboard.

Preview changes are temporary until OK; Cancel restores the document; OK is one undo step. An object takes one
3D effect: edit its options in the Appearance panel, or remove it before applying another.

## Extrude & Bevel

The art is the front face; its outline is extruded backwards by **Depth** (0–2,000 pt), so seen straight on the
object is where the art was.

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| Depth | 0–2,000 pt. At 0 the object is flat (the art turned like Rotate). |
| Twist | 0° to 360°: the back face turned against the front, the walls following in slices. |
| Taper | 1–100 %: the back face's size against the front's. |
| Cap | **Solid** closes the front and back; **Hollow** leaves them open, showing the insides of the walls. |
| Bevel Shape | **None**, **Classic** (a straight chamfer), **Rounded** (convex quarter round), **Cove** (concave), **Step** (two steps) or **Ogee** (an S curve). Our own cross-sections. |
| Width, Height | How far the bevel reaches across the face and along the depth (0–1,000 pt each). The height is limited to the depth (half of it on each side with Bevel both sides). |
| Repeat, Space | The cross-section repeated 1–32 times across the width, with a share (0–90 %) of the width flat between repeats. |
| Bevel Inside | The bevel carved into the shape (the front face shrinks) instead of added around it (the walls stand outside the art). |
| Bevel both sides | The back is bevelled too. |

Holes stay holes, with walls of their own. Bevels move each corner along its bisector (mitres are limited to four
times the width), so a bevel wider than a narrow part of the shape folds over itself.

## Inflate

The shape puffed out like a cushion: its outline stays where the art is and the surface rises towards the
middle.

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| Depth | 0–2,000 pt of flat side between the front and the back. |
| Twist | 0° to 360°: the back turned against the front (its puff too), the sides following in slices. |
| Taper | 1–100 %: the back's size against the front's; a puffed back is lower in proportion. |
| Cap | **Solid** closes the back; **Hollow** leaves it off, so the inflated front is a shell open behind, its inside showing. The public documentation lists Cap for every 3D type without saying what it means for Inflate; this is our reading. |
| Volume | 0–100 %. The surface is a membrane under even pressure, held along the outline (and around holes): it rises vertically from the edge and rounds smoothly inside, without creases along the shape's middle. At 50 % a circle becomes a half sphere; 100 % puffs twice as high, 0 % is flat. |
| Both sides | The back puffs out too; otherwise it is flat. |

The surface starts with a grid of 48 cells across the larger side, halved or quartered where it rises steeply near the outline. White-light Inflate retains the existing clipped polygon cells, shading, paint composition and seam joins. With colored lights, simple cells are triangulated with shared border samples, and lighting interpolates shared membrane normals through ordinary RGB vector gradients, including on a puffed back. Solid fills batch those triangles into three channel groups and one coverage clip for the whole surface. Source gradients retain per-facet vector composition and apply transparent coverage once. Seam widths retain the 0.05 to 0.75 pt bounds; colored facets use round joins. Shading is automatic, with no additional dialog option.

## Fills and strokes

Extrude & Bevel and Inflate build a solid from the path for the object's top fill, and one from the outline of
each visible stroke (with its caps, joins, dashes, alignment and arrowheads), each in its own paint. An admin's
reply on the reference app's bug forum says that strokes "will be treated as outlined when applying 3D"
([August 2024](https://icuw.ai-hao123.com/anfang/tag-95326275.html)).
The rest is our reading:

- When the fill and every stroke are opaque with Normal blending, the faces of all the solids are drawn in one
  back-to-front order, and the caps turned toward the viewer are drawn last, the lower item's first. Otherwise
  each solid is drawn on its own with its opacity and blending, the lower item's first. With a light that is not
  white, each solid is also drawn on its own when one of them is a puffed, shaded Inflate surface in a solid color
  (drawn as one composite) or is painted with a gradient that has transparent stops (drawn with an opacity mask).
- The solids turn, twist and taper about the center of the bounds of all their shapes, Inflate's grid covers
  those bounds, and with Perspective one eye sees every solid. A stroke too narrow to hold a point of Inflate's
  grid stays flat.
- A stroke whose outline takes more than 2,048 points is left out, and the fill's solid still draws.

## Rotate

The flat art turned in 3D about the centre of its bounds. Every fill and stroke is turned with its own paint (a
stroke as its outline, so it foreshortens with the art) and shaded as one plane; a plane has two sides, so its
back shows when it is turned past 90°.

## Rotation presets

**Front**, **Back**, **Left**, **Right**, **Top** and **Bottom** face the art that way. **Off-Axis** tilts each 20°
down and 25° aside, so the top and the right show. **Isometric Left/Right/Top/Bottom** lay the art on that plane
of an isometric view (each visible axis foreshortened equally). These are our own values, from the geometry of
each view; the dialog shows a preset's name when the angles match it and **Custom** otherwise. The new effects
open at Off-Axis Front.

## Perspective

**Perspective** runs 0° to 160°, as the public panel options give it ("how close or far the object appears"),
for Revolve too. The documentation doesn't say how the angle places the eye; our reading: the eye stands where a
sphere about the object's centre fills that angle of the view, the sphere's radius √3 times the object's size
(for Extrude & Bevel, Inflate and Rotate half its largest side, depth included; for Revolve the larger of its
radius and its height, the sizes the earlier strength used), so the object fits inside it. 0° is no
perspective; wider angles bring the eye nearer, and at 160° it is just outside that sphere, so never inside the
object. Default 0°, as before.

Effects saved before the angle (and scripts) give `perspective` as a 0–100 % strength. It is read as the angle
that shows exactly the same view: the strength put the eye at 4 × that size / strength, so
sin(angle / 2) = √3 × strength / 4, and 100 % is about 51.3°. An angle given as well wins; the dialog shows and
saves the angle.

## Lighting

### Presets

The Lighting tab has **Standard**, **Diffuse**, **Top Left** and **Right** choices. Choosing one
replaces the whole light rig with one white front light at 80% intensity and sets Ambient Light.
It leaves Shading, the object's view, geometry and other effect options unchanged. Manual edits
remain available; the list shows **Custom** whenever the effective lighting matches none of the
presets, including when there is more than one light. An equivalent explicit single light is
recognized too. Reset all returns to Standard. Preview, Cancel and Undo work as for other options.

These are original VectorCraft settings based on the public preset names and directions. Adobe's
documentation does not publish numeric rigs; the values are not copied from its software or files
and are not claimed to reproduce its presets exactly. Standard retains the existing default.

| Preset | Rotation | Height | Softness | Ambient Light |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Standard | 125.26438968275465 degrees | 30 degrees | 0% | 25% |
| Diffuse | 125.26438968275465 degrees | 30 degrees | 100% | 35% |
| Top Left | 135 degrees | 45 degrees | 0% | 25% |
| Right | 0 degrees | 30 degrees | 0% | 25% |

`effect.lightingPreset {index: 0, item: null, preset: "standard" | "diffuse" | "topLeft" | "right", ids?, target?}`
applies the same settings through commands, CLI and MCP. The index and item address an already
applied 3D effect. Every target must have a 3D effect at that position; validation is atomic, and
the whole operation is one undo step. The numeric light settings are saved, not a preset name.
Existing documents keep their appearance unless a preset is chosen.

### Light settings

One to ten directional lights. **Lights** selects the light whose settings and artboard gizmo are edited. **Add Light** adds and selects a white front light; **Delete Light** removes the selected light while retaining at least one. Ambient Light is shared by all lights. The public panel options' Light Settings are kept in their order:

| Option | |
|---|---|
| Color | Opaque RGB light color, white by default. The picker previews changes; its dot resets to white. |
| Intensity | 0–100 %, default 80 %: the light's brightness. |
| Rotation | −180° to 180°: round the object on the page. Our reading: 0° is on the object's right, counterclockwise, as Illustrator's other angles. |
| Height | 0° to 90°: from beside the object (0°) to straight in front of it (90°). |
| Softness | 0–100 %, default 0 %: how far round the object the light reaches. Our reading: at 0 % the light falls off with the angle to nothing at 90° (as before), at 100 % it reaches nothing only straight away from the light. |
| Ambient Light | 0–200 %, default 25 %: neutral light from everywhere. Each channel is clamped to the art's own color; at 100 % ambient every channel is fully lit, so higher values add nothing. |
| Light behind the object | The documented "Move selected light to the back of object": the light shines from behind. |

Colored illumination multiplies each source RGB channel by `clamp(ambient + sum(intensity * diffuse * color), 0, 1)`. Each light has its own direction and softness. Ambient is added once, and channel saturation happens after the sum. Ambient light stays neutral. Softness supplies the same diffuse falloff as before. White supplies neutral illumination; Shading off ignores the lights. Solid fills and gradient stops (including freeform points) receive the color. Pattern fills retain the existing neutral shadow approximation because their referenced tiles are not evaluated per face. SVG/PDF and Expand Appearance keep the shaded solids and gradients as vectors.

Revolve interpolates the directional illumination before clipping each RGB channel, adding vector stops where a channel saturates. Its continuous caps keep flat lighting. A source gradient and the light ramp are combined with isolated vector Multiply groups; a vector clip applies the curved face boundary once, avoiding antialiasing seams, and a vector opacity mask preserves transparent stops when needed. With multiple lights, each RGB channel has its own affine vector gradient; disjoint channel ramps combine through Screen before multiplying the source paint. This preserves differently colored directions and clips each channel after interpolation. No raster image is needed.

The documentation gives no numeric defaults; ours keep the earlier light: Rotation 125.26° and Height 30° are the direction
the default light had (45° left of the eye and 45° up). Effects saved before (and scripts) give the light by
`lightAzimuth` and `lightElevation`; those are read as the Rotation, Height and side of the same direction, so the
shading is exactly as before.

## Parameters (`effect.apply`, `effect.setParams`)

`threeD.extrude`: `depth`, `twist`, `taper` (%), `cap`, `bevel` (`none`, `classic`, `rounded`, `cove`, `step`,
`ogee`), `bevelWidth`, `bevelHeight`, `bevelRepeat`, `bevelSpace` (%), `bevelInside`, `bevelBothSides`.
`threeD.inflate`: `depth`, `volume` (%), `bothSides`. All three take the view and lighting parameters Revolve
uses: `rotationX`, `rotationY`, `rotationZ`, `perspectiveAngle` (degrees), `shade`, `lightColor` (`#rrggbb`, default `#ffffff`), `lightIntensity` (%), `lightRotation`,
`lightHeight` (degrees), `lightSoftness` (%), `ambient` (%, to 200), `lightBehind`. Lengths are points and scale with the object (Scale Strokes & Effects).
Commands validate the shape and the parameters before the document changes. All four also take `lights`: null (the default, use the earlier single-light fields), or an array of one to ten objects. Each object takes `color` (opaque `#rrggbb`, white), `intensity` (0..100%, 80), `rotation` (-180..180 degrees, 125.26), `height` (0..90 degrees, 30), `softness` (0..100%, 0), and `behind` (boolean, false). Omitted settings use those defaults. An explicit list replaces the earlier single light; `ambient` and `shade` remain shared. Set `lights` to null to return to the single-light fields. Invalid lists, counts, keys and values are rejected before editing; malformed loaded lists fall back to the earlier light safely.

## What differs from the public documentation

Behaviour reference: the public [3D and Materials panel options](https://yzqn.yx-sf.com/zhineng/analytics-42300717.html)
and [Create 3D objects](https://feed.waepv.cn/d/OSaBm7QIJW)
pages, and the archived Extrude & Bevel option list (depth 0–2,000, cap on/off, bevel height, bevel extent in or
out, perspective). No Adobe software, assets, presets or bevel shapes were used.

- **Materials** (base, Adobe Substance and graphics), **shadows**
  and **ray-traced rendering** are not built: shading uses directional lights, in the paint of the fill or
  stroke the solid is built for ([Fills and strokes](#fills-and-strokes)).
- The bevel shapes and their names are our own; custom bevel paths are not supported.
- Visibility is a painter's algorithm: faces of a closed solid turned away are left out, and the rest are drawn
  back to front, with a flat cap or flat back turned toward the viewer drawn after all of them. Concave solids
  seen at steep angles can overlap wrongly; open (hollow) solids show both sides. Twisted walls and bevels are
  drawn in pieces about as long as a wall slice is wide (fewer near the limit of 32,768 facets). The piece drawn
  on top can still lie a few points behind another nearby piece.
- Extrude & Bevel and Rotate retain planar shading. Colored Inflate uses smooth vector lighting; white-light Inflate keeps its original polygon shading; bounded cell triangulation leaves a cell flat when it contains a complete hole or an unusually complex/degenerate contour. Its geometric silhouette is still a polygon approximation.
- Paths and compound paths only: convert type, images and groups to outlines first. One 3D effect per object.
- Curves are followed within 1/2000 of the shape's size (at least 0.05 pt), so a small curve takes a few points
  and a large one up to 32. Extrude & Bevel and Inflate take up to 2,048 outline points (a stroke's outline is
  counted on its own), Rotate (which only turns the outline) 65,536.
- **3D (Classic)** (the track cube, surface types, blend steps, map art), Turntable and 3D export are separate,
  unbuilt items.

Release measurements and a repeatable CLI scene are in [3D lighting performance](3d-lighting-performance.md).

## Revision history

| Date | Change |
|---|---|
| 2026-10-21 | Four original lighting presets, shared by all four 3D effects and commands, with effective-setting recognition and existing preview/history behavior. |
| 2026-10-17 | Smooth colored Inflate lighting and surface batching; legacy white-light appearance and the 0.05 seam minimum preserved; shared light Color and multiple lights remain vector output. |

Type is Illustrator's largest single area by use (weight 13 of 105 across "Type core" and "Type advanced" in
[target-app-parity.md](target-app-parity.md)). This checklist lists the features one by one. Status is from the
code and tests (`crates/text`, `crates/engine/src/cmd/type*.rs`, `textstyles.rs`, `crates/tools/src/text.rs`)
against Illustrator's public documentation; **estimated** unless noted.

## Summary

| Part | % | Remaining (h) |
|---|---:|---:|
| Type core (point, area, path type, Character/Paragraph, styles, threading, OpenType, fonts) | 80% | 14–19 |
| Type advanced (CJK composition, Middle Eastern, spelling, Touch Type, Retype, variable fonts) | 50% | 20–28 |

## Checklist

| Feature | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Native font-family labels | partial | With Show Font Names in English off, localized legacy names are used when typographic names contain no native label (#2208); loaded-font and catalog-only regressions. Choosing among multiple native languages is unchanged. |
| Point, area and type-on-a-path type; vertical variants | done / partial | vertical point, area and path type have initial support; fullwidth `！` / `？` keep the nominal glyph upright when no vertical alternate exists (Unicode Tu); in a non-rectangular area a word too wide for the top lines moves down to the first line that holds it (#1615); Escape while typing ends the edit, keeps the type selected and switches to the Selection tool (#1802); `text.create` and `text.createInPath` take `justify` (#1752); MCP `add_text` forwards `vertical` to both commands |
| Area Type Options (rows, columns, inset, first baseline, Auto Size, Shrink Text to Fit) | done | the commands that make or restyle type say when it does not fit its frame; MCP `add_text` takes Auto Size and Shrink Text to Fit (#1471) |
| Threaded text, Fit Headline, Text Wrap | done | Fit Headline sees wrapping in a frame one line tall (#1444); a thread holds area type and type on a path in any mix, as Illustrator links type in an area or along a path ([help](https://tech.ai-hao123.com)) |
| Threading from the ports: selected area type and type on a path show an in port and an out port, empty, with an arrow on a side where the frame is threaded, or with a red "+" in the out port when the text doesn't fit; a click on either port loads the text; a click on a closed path, area type or type on a path threads into it, a click on empty canvas makes a frame of the same kind, shape and size there, a drag draws a rectangular frame; the frame placed comes after the clicked one from its out port and before it from its in port (the story then starts there); Escape or another tool cancels; a double-click on a threaded port breaks the thread there | partial | #2572: the Selection tool, `text.thread.add {from, to?, rect?, at?, before?}`, as the reference app's help describes ports and threading ([archived help, Threading text between objects](https://udzr.ai-hao123.com/shuju/like-94113635.html), [create text threads](https://www.mw-wm.com/s/ep00MQi1Eq2KHWxflF)); area type's in port sits on the left side below the top-left corner, type on a path's just before its start bracket; Show Text Threads draws its lines between the same ports; with more than 1,000 such objects selected no ports are drawn. a double-click on a port where the frame is threaded breaks the thread there, the story flowing into the frames before the break and the frames after it left empty, still threaded with each other when two or more (`text.thread.break`, [archived help](https://view.yx-sf.com/d/ok960657.html)). Remaining: the ports only take clicks with the Selection tool, and the loaded cursor borrows the I-beam until it's drawn |
| Type on a Path effects and options; brackets | done | #429 |
| Character and Paragraph panels, styles with overrides | done | Character-style Auto-leading resets, partial definitions, local leading overrides, override markers, Undo/Redo and native serialization have regression coverage; differing paragraph alignments leave the shared alignment buttons unselected (headless regressions, full integration CI and visual review pass); mixed-value display for other paragraph fields remains missing |
| Character size and horizontal scale after object/group scaling | done | #1034: fields and setters compensate the stored affine; point size follows the transformed em-height axis, not the glyph ink bounds. Range edits, keyboard increments, leading and baseline shift use document points; rotation, reflection and shear remain editable. |
| Preserve font sizes while scaling a group | missing | Separate enhancement; scaling still scales text with the other artwork. |
| OpenType panel, Glyphs panel, alternates | done | Highlight Alternate Glyphs preference (#394, off by default) paints pink behind OpenType substitutions on screen when on; stylistic sets ss01–ss20, stylistic and titling alternates, proportional and lining figures, superscript and subscript are character-style features (`text.setStyle {features}`, #1607) |
| Font menu: samples, live preview, filters, favourites, recent families; font matching by any name; Find Font | done | #3515: recently applied families appear first, once each; missing families are omitted and the existing Number of Recent Fonts setting applies; #339; script filter: Japanese, Latin, Thai; the font scan on Linux also reads the folders fontconfig's configuration lists, such as TeX fonts under `/usr/share/texmf/fonts` (#1548, fixes #1529; not verified on Linux) |
| Missing glyphs set in an installed font made for their script (Thai, Lao, Khmer, Myanmar first; then any font that has them) | done | Thai: Leelawadee UI, Tahoma, Thonburi, Sukhumvit Set, Noto Sans Thai, TLWG |
| Full font-name matching (OpenType name ID 4) | done | #1258: loaded/cataloged faces and Missing Fonts searches; localized names and variable default faces; Windows font-service QA pending |
| Variable fonts | done | named instances as styles; Character panel › Variable Font sets each axis (`fontAxes`); the font menu's Font Technology › Variable lists only variable font families, with the script, kind and ★ filters ([Find, apply, and adjust variable fonts](https://sfuh.tcti.cn/gongsi/search-02953890.html)); a family with a variable file beside static ones counts as variable. Evidence: `font_menu::tests::the_variable_filter_lists_only_variable_families`, `tests_axes::a_family_with_variation_axes_is_variable`, `tests_sysfonts::a_family_with_a_variable_file_beside_static_ones_is_variable` |
| Fallback glyphs keep the text's weight and slant | done | #2491: a character from a fallback face is set in that family's face nearest the run's weight and slant; Bold Italic of a missing family is drawn Bold (Source Sans 3 has no Bold Italic) rather than Italic |
| Colour fonts (bitmap, COLR, OpenType SVG) | partial | bitmap glyphs (`sbix`, `CBDT`) done: the largest strike's PNG, transformed with the type, fill and stroke ignored; PDF Type 3 glyphs or images, SVG images with outlined text (live text leaves emoji to the viewer, their fonts not embedded), EPS and legacy `.ai` images, Create Outlines images; not `sbix` duplicate, flipped, JPEG or TIFF glyphs, or `CBDT` BGRA or mask data, or ruby; in envelopes they warp as images do, and a Warp effect moves them without bending them. COLR (v0 and v1) done: a glyph's layers as vector art (solid colours, linear and radial gradients, clip glyphs and boxes, blend modes, transforms, palette 0, the foreground colour from the run's fill, variable fonts at the face's instance), transformed with the type; drawn on the canvas, written as paths in SVG, EPS, legacy `.ai` and PDF with outlined text, as text in PDF (Type 3 glyphs), and Create Outlines makes groups of editable paths. Paints documents have no form for draw the glyph as an image (256 px per em): sweep gradients, Porter-Duff compositing, radial gradients from a circle that isn't the centre, repeating or reflecting gradients. Not ruby. COLR and SVG glyphs also go with type that geometry effects reshape (on the canvas and in exports), into Expand Appearance and EMF/WMF export, as their art, and bitmap glyphs as images. OpenType SVG done: a glyph's SVG document (its element `glyph<gid>`) is read by the SVG importer into vector art in font units, `currentColor` in the run's fill (and the legacy `context-fill` and `context-stroke` in its fill and stroke), a `viewBox` mapped onto the em square, and then drawn, exported and outlined as COLR glyphs are; in PDF real text such glyphs are text that draws nothing, with their art drawn where they sit. Images in glyph documents are in the art, holding their pixels until a document takes them in; text, scripts and embedded content are left out, as the table rules them out. Not CPAL palette variables. Evidence: `tests_svg_glyphs`, `svg/tests/it/svg_glyphs.rs`, `tests_colourfonts::svg_glyph_images_draw_and_outline`, `tests_colourfonts::create_outlines_turns_svg_glyphs_into_groups`, `tests_colourfonts::pdf_real_text_draws_svg_glyphs_as_art_and_keeps_their_characters`, `tests_colourfonts::expand_appearance_keeps_the_colour_glyphs_of_type_with_effects`, `render::tests_colrglyphs::colour_glyphs_go_with_type_that_a_geometry_effect_reshapes`, `tests_bitmaps`, `tests_colr`, `render::tests_bitmapglyphs`, `render::tests_colrglyphs`, `pdf::tests::colour_bitmap_glyphs_export_as_images`, `pdf::tests::colr_glyphs_export_as_vector_art`, `svg/tests/it/colour_glyphs.rs`, `eps` `colour_bitmap_glyphs_*` and `colr_glyphs_*`, `tests_pathops::create_outlines_turns_bitmap_glyphs_into_images`, `tests_pathops::create_outlines_turns_colr_glyphs_into_layer_groups` |
| Every-line and Single-line composers | done | tuned by eye, never compared side by side |
| Optical Margin Alignment | done | Type › Optical Margin Alignment, `type.opticalMarginAlignment`: per type object, with one setting for all the frames of a thread, in point and area type of left-to-right paragraphs, and at the brackets of type on a path whose first paragraph runs left to right; right-to-left paragraphs of point and area type, and type on a path whose first paragraph runs right to left, do not hang |
| System Layout | done | Character panel menu › System Layout, `type.systemLayout`: the whole document, off by default and for documents from before it, saved only when on. On, every text object advances by whole points (at least one when a character takes space). New point, area and path type, threaded frames, placed text, graph and dimension labels and pasted plain text inherit it. Evidence: `tests::system_layout_rounds_positive_advances_to_whole_points`, `typecmd::area_tests::system_layout_sets_the_document_and_every_text_object`, `panels::character::tests::system_layout_menu_item_toggles_the_document` |
| Fractional Widths | done | Character panel menu › Fractional Widths, `type.fractionalWidths`: per type object, and every frame of its threads. On by default and for documents from before it; saved only when off. Off, each character that takes space advances by a whole number of points, at least one, so small type does not run together. Evidence: `tests::fractional_widths_off_rounds_positive_advances_to_whole_points`, `typecmd::area_tests::fractional_widths_is_set_per_object_and_saved_only_when_off`, `panels::character::tests::fractional_widths_menu_item_toggles_the_type_object` |

Evidence: `tests::roman_hanging_punctuation_hangs_punctuation_but_not_letters`, `typecmd::area_tests::roman_hanging_punctuation_is_set_per_paragraph_and_saved_only_when_on`. Whole paragraphs hang as published with both composers, ragged, centred and justified, with Line-end Punctuation Half Width and bidirectional lines; Justification's Glyph Scaling leaves the hung marks at their width, and Standard burasagari counts what hangs at a line's start as room before hanging a comma (`tests_hang`) |
| Hyphenation… and Justification… options | done | Hyphenation… (`ui.hyphenation`, `text.setFormat`) sets each paragraph's Words Longer Than, After First, Before Last, Hyphen Limit, Hyphenation Zone (Single-line Composer only) and Hyphenate Capitalized Words, and paragraph styles carry them (#2310). Justification… (`ui.justification`, `text.setFormat`, #2755) sets Word Spacing, Letter Spacing and Glyph Scaling (Minimum, Desired, Maximum), Auto Leading and Single Word Justification; Desired applies to every line, justified lines and the Every-line Composer use the ranges. Evidence: `tests::roman_hanging_punctuation_hangs_punctuation_but_not_letters`, `typecmd::area_tests::roman_hanging_punctuation_is_set_per_paragraph_and_saved_only_when_on` |

| No Break | done | Character panel menu (`text.setFormat` / `text.setRangeStyle {noBreak}`): the marked characters stay on one line, including across a space; a run that does not fit after earlier text moves together, and a run longer than the line stays together. Evidence: `layout::wrapping_tests::no_break_keeps_marked_characters_on_one_line`, `tests::no_break_keeps_marked_words_on_one_line`, `typecmd::no_break_is_a_character_attribute_saved_only_when_on` |
| CJK: ruby | missing | #633 |
| Inline symbols in text | beyond Illustrator | not scored |
| Align Stroke (inside, outside) on live type's character stroke | beyond Illustrator | not scored; `stroke.set {align}` and `text.setRangeStyle {strokeOptions: {align}}`; saved natively, drawn around the glyphs on the canvas and in PDF, EPS and SVG (live text, stroke on the glyph outlines); visual bounds grow with it (#2294) |

Character Styles menu New/Redefine and footer New capture the first selected character of a nonempty Type selection, including exact style-run and UTF-8 boundaries; New adds a definition without applying it. New/Redefine commands accept optional `end` for range capture. Start-only command affinity, existing UI caret/object behavior and paragraph capture at `start` remain unchanged. Pointer regressions assert captured definitions, linked-text updates and local overrides, complete-document Undo/Redo and saved state, with whole-object, collapsed-caret and range-Apply controls. Capture closes prior typing while preserving the Type selection. Live text and Select All regressions exercise menu New/Redefine and footer New, asserting that further typing retains the captured definition and that typing, capture and further typing have separate Undo/Redo steps. Focused engine and egui input tests pass for boundary capture, all three live-typing capture routes and the existing compatibility controls. Full workspace CI passes.

### Typography and Custom Lettering in VectorCraft

# Typography and Custom Lettering in VectorCraft

## What you can do

- **Typesetting:** use an available font to create editable text, then adjust its size, style and spacing.
- **Custom lettering:** convert text to vector outlines and reshape the letters for a title or logo.
- **Reusable font files:** VectorCraft does not currently create or export installable TTF or OTF fonts.

This guide covers the first two workflows. The steps apply to the v0.13.1 release; the desktop app
can use installed system fonts, while the web app uses the fonts supplied by its deployment.

## Getting started with the Type Tool

1. Create a document with **File → New…**, or open an existing one.
2. Select **Type Tool** in the toolbar, or press **T** when you are not typing in a text field.
3. Click an empty part of the artboard and type a short heading, such as `MOON`. A click creates
   point text, which grows as you type. To create text that wraps inside a frame, drag a rectangle
   instead. If placeholder text appears selected, typing replaces it.
4. Press **Escape** to finish typing. Select **Selection Tool** (**V**) and click the text object.
   This lets you format the whole heading rather than just characters selected while typing.
5. Open **Window → Type → Character**. Use the font family menu at the top of the panel to search
   for a font and click its name to apply it. The menu below it chooses an available style, such as
   Regular, Bold or Italic; the choices depend on the font. **Type → Font** also lists available fonts.
6. Adjust **Font Size** (the field beside **T**) and **Tracking** (beside **VA↔**) in the Character
   panel. Hover a field's label to see its name. For example, enter `72 pt` for a large heading and
   try tracking `50` to spread its letters slightly. Positive tracking adds space; negative tracking
   tightens it. **Leading** controls the spacing between lines; **Kerning (0 = Auto)** adjusts pairs.
7. To change only part of the text, select **Type Tool**, click into the text and drag across the
   characters before using the Character panel. Press **Escape** when finished. Keep the text
   editable until its wording, font and spacing are settled.
8. Choose **File → Save As…**, select the **VectorCraft** format, and save the document as
   `lettering-editable.vectorcraft`.

The desktop app scans system fonts and loads faces as needed. If you install a font while it is
open, use **Refresh Font List** in the Character panel's menu. On the web, installing a font on your
computer does not add it to VectorCraft's font menu; the available fonts depend on the hosted build.

## Turning text into editable outlines

Create Outlines replaces text with vector paths. You can reshape those paths, but you can no longer
edit the words or choose a different font for them with the Type Tool.

1. Keep the editable file saved above. Choose **File → Save As…** again, select **VectorCraft**,
   and save as `lettering-outlines.vectorcraft`. Continue in this second file so later saves do not
   overwrite your editable original.
2. With **Selection Tool** (**V**), select the text object you want to convert.
3. Choose **Type → Create Outlines**. The default shortcut is **Ctrl+Shift+O** on Windows and Linux,
   or **Cmd+Shift+O** on macOS.
4. Select **Direct Selection Tool** (**A**) and click a letter's edge to inspect its paths and anchors.
   The text has become a group of paths, one compound path per glyph. A compound path can include
   both a letter's outer edge and its inner holes, such as the middle of an `O`.

Conversion uses the font currently drawn. Resolve missing or substituted fonts before outlining,
or the paths will capture the substitute's shapes.

## Customizing individual letters

Try making the final `N` in `MOON` taller to give the heading a distinctive ending.

1. Select **Direct Selection Tool** (**A**). Click empty canvas to clear the current selection,
   then click an anchor on the outlined `N`. Anchors are the points that define a path's shape;
   Direct Selection can reach paths inside the group without ungrouping the letters.
2. Drag the anchor a short distance to change that part of the letter. To move several anchors
   together, Shift-click them before dragging, or drag a selection rectangle around them from
   empty canvas. For the taller `N`, select its top anchors and move them up slightly.
3. On a curved letter such as `O`, select an anchor on a curve. Drag the end of a visible direction
   handle to change the curve's bend. These Bézier handles control how the curve leaves or enters
   the anchor. Straight corners may have no handles to drag.
4. Switch to **Selection Tool** (**V**) to inspect the whole heading. Use **Edit → Undo** if a change
   distorts the letter or closes an inner hole, then try a smaller adjustment.

These changes affect the artwork in this document. They do not change the installed font or other
text using it. A glyph is not always one typed character: for example, a font may join letters into
a ligature, which becomes a single glyph outline.

## Saving and exporting your artwork

- **Keep the project:** use **File → Save** to save `lettering-outlines.vectorcraft`. Retain
  `lettering-editable.vectorcraft` separately for future wording or font changes. A native file keeps
  editable text only where you have left text objects unconverted.
- **Export vector artwork:** choose **File → Export → Export As…**, select **SVG** or **PDF**, and
  continue through the export options. The outlined letters are vector shapes in the output, not
  keyboard-editable text. Check **Use Artboards** if you want the artboard bounds rather than the
  bounds of the visible artwork.
- **Create an installable font:** SVG and PDF exports are artwork, not TTF/OTF files. Renaming their
  extension does not turn them into fonts.

## Can VectorCraft create a font file?

No. VectorCraft does not currently provide a complete font-authoring workflow or TTF/OTF export.
It does not turn your letter paths into a reusable font with character encoding, glyph metrics and
font-wide kerning definitions. Character panel spacing changes format the text in your drawing;
they do not edit a font's kerning tables.

To make an installable typeface, use a dedicated font editor to assign glyphs to characters, set
metrics and spacing, and generate the font file. VectorCraft's outline tools are useful for custom
lettering artwork, but exporting that artwork is only one part of making a font.

## Troubleshooting

- **I cannot find my font.** On desktop, check that it is installed, clear the font menu's search
  and filters, then choose **Refresh Font List** from the Character panel menu. **Type → Find Font…**
  lists fonts used by the document and marks missing ones; it can replace them with available fonts.
  A missing family, style or character may use a fallback, so check the result before outlining.
  On the web, the site must supply the font; system-font scanning and the desktop refresh option
  are unavailable there.
- **I cannot change the words after Create Outlines.** The result is paths, not text. Use
  **Edit → Undo** if the conversion is still in the undo history, or reopen your editable original.
- **I cannot install my modified letters as a font.** They are drawing objects. SVG/PDF export
  does not add the structure required by an installable font; see [Can VectorCraft create a font
  file?](#can-vectorcraft-create-a-font-file).
- **How do I keep text editable?** Save the text in a native `.vectorcraft` file before outlining,
  then use a different file name for the outlined version. Saving paths in the native format does
  not turn them back into text.

## Feature submission evidence

**Feature evidence last updated:** 2026-10-22.

The shared assessment status line and revision history are current upstream; this dated section records the submission's feature evidence and revisions without rescoring upstream or claiming a new combined build or runtime measurement.

- Current-main conflict reconciliation retains upstream and feature behavior; scores and estimates unchanged
- Superseded 2026-10-20 behavior, retained as history: Artboard Options shares existing presets and orientation controls and can fit artwork without moving it; artwork fitting uses the original target artboard and revision-scoped bounds caches

- Artboard Options puts Fit to Artwork Bounds and Fit to Selected Art in the Preset menu. Artwork bounds cover all drawn document art, including other artboards and off-board art; selection bounds may span artboards. Fit changes only the active artboard and keeps artwork stationary, including position-only fitting with Move Artwork enabled. Existing Background Color and presets remain available; scores and estimates unchanged.

Artboard Options forwards the active Artboard tool's Scale Artwork with Artboard option for ordinary resizing. Fit to Artwork Bounds and Fit to Selected Art explicitly leave artwork stationary. Dialog regression coverage checks preset/orientation/typed-size intent with scaling on and off, draft cancellation, one-step Undo/Redo, and fitting while Move Artwork and Scale Artwork are enabled. This is a narrow follow-up to #3277; no parity score or estimate is reassessed.

How VectorCraft's tools, handles, snapping and panels behave next to Illustrator's. A vector illustrator's
trust is in the details: where a handle lands, what Shift and Alt do mid-drag, what a smart guide snaps to,
how far an arrow key nudges. This checklist is the work list for the **interaction-fidelity pass**
([gaps.md](gaps.md) G1). Part of [target-app-parity.md](target-app-parity.md).

**How it is measured:** from the tool state machines' own documentation and tests (`crates/tools/src/*.rs`,
`crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`, `shortcuts.rs`, the `tests_*` files) against Illustrator's public documentation
(helpx tool pages and the keyboard-shortcut reference). Never against the running app: the clean-room rule
forbids launching or measuring Illustrator, so there has been **no side-by-side session**. Every "done" below is
"behaves as the documentation describes", which is weaker than "a power user can't tell". Status:
**done** (documented behaviour implemented and tested), **partial**, **missing**.

## Summary

| Area | % | Remaining (h) | Kind |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Pen, Curvature and anchor tools | 85% | 6–10 | estimated |
| Direct Selection, handles and anchors | 85% | 5–8 | estimated |
| Smart guides and snapping | 70% | 8–12 | estimated |
| Transform handles, bounding box, Free Transform | 80% | 5–8 | estimated |
| Nudging, numeric entry, precision, units | 85% | 3–5 | estimated |
| Modifier keys and temporary tools | 80% | 5–8 | estimated |
| Keyboard shortcuts (default set) | 70% | 6–10 | estimated |
| Cursors | 75% | 3–5 | estimated |
| Panels, Control bar, Properties, context menus | 70% | 15–25 | estimated |
| Look and feel (layout, theme, metrics) | 80% | 5–10 | measured once against public screenshots on 2026-10-02; panels added since not re-measured |
| Accessibility (screen reader, keyboard-only canvas) | 20% | 15–25 | estimated: AccessKit on by default for egui widgets; canvas and custom panels not described, never tested with a screen reader |
| **UI/UX overall** | **~55%** | **~70–110** (overlaps the feature areas) | estimated |

The overall figure is lower than the rows because what users notice first (small differences across many
tools, never checked side by side) isn't captured row by row.

## Keyboard shortcuts

Cmd/Ctrl+/ (`appearance.addFill`) and Cmd/Ctrl+Alt+/ (`appearance.addStroke`) add a new fill and a new stroke to the
selected objects, as the Appearance panel's Add New Fill and Add New Stroke buttons do.

~110 distinct modified shortcuts on menu commands plus single-key tool shortcuts for the default toolbar
(`crates/tools/src/catalog.rs`), a shortcut editor with chords, and saved sets. Cmd/Ctrl+Alt+L (`ui.newLayer`) opens Layer Options for a new layer, as an Alt-click on the Layers panel's New Layer button does, and Cmd/Ctrl+L still adds a layer without the dialog. F8 (`ui.symbolOptions`) opens Symbol Options for a new symbol made from the selection, as the Symbols panel's New Symbol button does. Not yet diffed item by item
against Illustrator's published default shortcut list; estimated ~70% of it. Remaining: the panel shortcuts,
the type shortcuts (tracking/kerning/leading/baseline steps with Alt/Shift), and selection shortcuts in the
Layers panel. The shortcut editor also lists the commands that are in no menu but run without parameters (Edit › Duplicate,
panel-menu commands such as Break Link to Symbol), so they can be given shortcuts (#1539). It lists each button of the
Align panel's Align Objects, Distribute Objects and Distribute Spacing rows under Align, with no default shortcut, and a
shortcut set there runs what a click on the button runs, with the panel's Align To choice and Distribute Spacing value. The [ and ] keys reach the Blob Brush, the Eraser and the Symbolism tools in the app (#1734, part of #1661).

Cmd/Ctrl+Alt+N (`file.newWithoutDialog`, New Without Dialog in the shortcut editor) makes a document with the
settings the New Document dialog opens on (the first Recent entry, or the Print category's Letter while Recent is
empty), without opening the dialog.

## Look and feel

- [x] Recolor Artwork › Assign: double-click a row's new color to pick it in the Color Picker, in the model it was picked in (part of #4028); a Lab new color is kept but can't be typed yet (the picker's Lab fields work in RGB); Lab entry, swatch libraries and the row menu remain.

- [x] Recolor Artwork Edit color chips scroll within the screen, preserving the wheel and actions (#3416); 5, 20, 200 and 400 colors, resizing and UI scaling, final-chip editing and preview/history covered by egui_kittest.

- [x] Status messages and bounded readouts remain stable as values, canvas hover and background jobs change; ordinary values fit all registered languages and units, and optional groups yield in narrow windows (regressions; contributor rebuilt and confirmed the original-file status-bar scenario on 2026-10-19). Sample widths are cached per UI and refreshed only when language, document units or pixels per point changes.

- [x] Cached canvas dimensions match the renderer limit before cache-key creation, view construction and worker submission (controlled-worker regression).
- [x] Cached canvas frames keep their document scale during panel/window resize, including rotated views and DPI changes (controlled-worker regression; contributor rebuilt and confirmed the original-file resize scenario on 2026-10-19).
Medium Dark theme and four brightness levels, the categorized and Advanced toolbars, 35 pt document tabs,
33 pt panel tabs, hint bar, contextual task bar and native macOS menus, restyled to values measured from
public screenshots on 2026-10-02 (~75–80% then). Missing: a System theme that follows the OS (#825), a
re-measure of the panels added since. Slider rails show on Medium Dark (#1808, #1662).

- [x] Native saves restore Show Transparency Grid (#1968), without dirtying the document or adding an undo step.

- [x] Compact Color Picker with a distinct header, stacked actions and aligned input groups. #2008; translated action widths, visible warnings, stable mode switching and vertical scrolling in narrow windows; real egui events and two UI scales covered; German and enlarged English renders reviewed locally. Scores unchanged

## Highlighted-text Eyedropper (2026-10-21)

Type/Eyedropper switches preserve highlighted characters; sampling changes only their enabled
font/paint attributes. Enabled non-neutral source or target object transparency is refused
atomically; disable Transparency to preserve object transparency while sampling the range.
`tests/eyedropper.rs` covers ranges, Unicode, history and transparency; tool tests cover brush-key
sampling coexistence. Scores and estimates unchanged. See [development.md](development.md#highlighted-text-eyedropper-2026-10-21).

## Drag artwork between document tabs (2026-10-22)

Selection drags activate another visible document tab after 400 ms, then copy editable artwork
on canvas release with the original grab point. Source and clipboard preservation, resource
rendering, swatch conflicts, cancellation, rotated/zoomed views and target Undo/Redo have regression
coverage (`tests_document_drag`, `tests_clipboard`). Overflow-menu and cross-window drag remain
separate. Scores and hours unchanged. [Behavior and command details](development.md#drag-artwork-between-document-tabs-2026-10-22).

### Windows 7 x64 compatibility build (experimental, unsupported)

# Windows 7 x64 compatibility build (experimental, unsupported)

Windows 7 is not a supported platform. This build is experimental and community-maintained,
and the VectorCraft maintainers have not verified it on Windows 7.

This separate build targets **64-bit Windows 7 SP1**. It uses OpenGL instead of wgpu,
and omits the native AccessKit accessibility adapter. Printer discovery supports the
PowerShell version included with Windows 7, and printer setup opens Control Panel.
Printing retains the PDF viewer's Print/PrintTo verb on this build: Windows 7 has no
Windows.Data.Pdf renderer. The win7 target excludes `craft-print` from its dependency
tree; normal desktop builds use the shared spooler. The `windows7` feature and dedicated win7 target must be selected together; the
existing compile-time guards reject mixing this feature with the ordinary Windows target.
The normal desktop and web builds retain their existing defaults. A vendor graphics driver providing **OpenGL 3.3 or newer**
is required; the Windows built-in generic display driver is insufficient. GPU selection
in Preferences and `WGPU_POWER_PREF` do not control this OpenGL build.

## Build or download

In your GitHub fork, open **Actions → Windows 7 x64 compatibility → Run workflow** (it
also runs weekly and on pull requests changing the compatibility path).
When it succeeds, download the `vectorcraft-windows7-x64-portable` artifact, extract the
contained portable ZIP, then run `vectorcraft.exe` on Windows 7. The CLI is included.
No MSI is provided: the existing installer remains for modern Windows.

To build locally, use a **Windows 10/11 build computer**, with Rust/rustup and Visual Studio
2022 C++ build tools (x64 compiler and Windows SDK). Open an **x64 Native Tools Command
Prompt for VS 2022**, change to your clone's repository root (the directory containing
`Cargo.toml`), and run:

```powershell
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File packaging/windows/windows7.ps1
```

Add `-Test` to also run the app and CLI tests on the build computer.

Output: `dist/release/vectorcraft-windows7-x64-portable.zip`. The script installs the pinned
nightly compiler and `rust-src`, rebuilds the standard library for
`x86_64-win7-windows-msvc`, and links the C runtime statically. It never installs Rust on
the Windows 7 machine. The optional `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR` setting works as in the normal build.
Without it, install fonts for the languages you need on the destination machine.

The Windows 7 target matters: modern Rust's ordinary `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` target
requires Windows 10, including standard-library and random-number APIs. Selecting OpenGL
alone or changing an installer version check cannot fix that.

References: [Rust's Windows 7 target](https://vzre.tcti.cn/jiaoliu/content-60579127.html)
and [Windows baseline change](https://zpgm.yx-sf.com/pingce/system-27140582.html).

The packaging script checks x64 PE headers, the subsystem version, and known incompatible
imports (including `GetSystemTimePreciseAsFileTime`) before creating the ZIP. This is a
regression check, not an exhaustive audit of every Windows API.

The small vendored `windows-link` patch routes `CoTaskMemFree` to its documented
`ole32.dll` export on the Windows 7 target; the newer binding otherwise imports
`combase.dll`, which is absent on Windows 7. Only this script uses it: it passes
`--config "patch.crates-io.windows-link.path='vendor/windows-link'"` to Cargo, so every other
build, including the normal Windows one, keeps the checksum-verified crates.io crate. Cargo
records the patch in `Cargo.lock`, so the script resolves once, fails if anything other than
windows-link's source changed, builds with `--locked`, and then restores `Cargo.lock`.

## Runtime validation

The contributor reports that a user ran the portable x64 compatibility build on Windows 7 SP1
with an NVIDIA graphics card. Their original build failed at startup with
`GetSystemTimePreciseAsFileTime` missing from `kernel32.dll`; the compatibility
build resolved that failure. The tested build was based on upstream commit
`1f7873273b67007b0aefc63313e0d34a39f45453`. The exact GPU/driver version and completion
of every checklist item below were not recorded, and the maintainers have not reproduced it,
so the build remains experimental and unsupported.

## Runtime acceptance checklist

A successful build on the Windows 2022 CI runner does **not** prove Windows 7 runtime
compatibility. Before declaring support, test on a Windows 7 SP1 x64 machine and record
its GPU, driver version, Windows updates and any missing-DLL/entry-point error:

- Start `vectorcraft.exe`; verify a visible canvas, resizing, minimize/restore and exit.
- Draw a shape, save a `.vectorcraft` document, close and reopen it.
- Open `examples/dusk-poster.vectorcraft`; export PNG and PDF and inspect both.
- Exercise native Open/Save dialogs, clipboard text/images and drag-and-drop.
- Change a preference, exit and verify it survives restarting.
- Run `vectorcraft-cli.exe --version` and a headless export from a Command Prompt in the
  extracted application folder.

This build is experimental until that checklist passes. New dependency versions can add
newer Windows imports, so retain Cargo.lock and repeat runtime QA after dependency updates.
